Tense CISA election-security call: Fontes "They don't work with us, they work against us"; Simon "states are almost entirely on their own"; Mullin reportedly vowed to withhold funds from states not implementing administration proposals. ProPublica: the August video call, a few weeks after the speech, was many officials' first meeting with acting CISA Director Nick Andersen; he said DHS was preparing an election plan and blamed lapses on the fall 2025 shutdown; Fontes: "I told him I didn't trust him" (R).

Chronology: Aug 21 FDNS personnel redirected to Unlawful Voter Initiative; Aug 25 FDNS voter reviews begin; late Aug ICE adds unlawful-voting question to booking intake (Oct 1 directive: ask admitters mail vs in-person); Aug 27 FDNS Tactical Operations social-media analytics solicitation; Aug 31 HSI "Public Voter Data and Handling" RFI. The CNA v. Mullin PI order (ECF 87, Oct 21, pp.1-2, citing ECF 10-7 at 11-13, 198-202, 336) describes the DHS "Unlawful Voter Initiative": USCIS personnel generate target lists for investigation for improper voting, initiated in August, and coordinate with HSI field offices to investigate them "through interrogations" (D, court's description). The government's opposition (ECF 46 p.37, Sept 28) quotes plaintiffs' Aug 21, 2026 start date for the "Voter Eligibility Matching Policy" and the TECS records under it without disputing it (D).

DHS Secretary Mullin writes the White House Transparency Task Force (letter dated Aug 24, 2026) that voting machines with China-made parts "introduce significant security risks": ES&S, Hart and Dominion (over 80% of the market) have "acknowledged that their voting machines have parts made in China," and tampered components could allow "synchronized attacks across multiple machines and jurisdictions"; he cites vendors' 2020 testimony, the "recently declassified" 2024 ODNI Annual Threat Assessment and an Oct 2024 NIC memorandum, not any exploitation; says "I have directed the Department of Homeland Security to prioritize election security," that DHS is doing rolling production and declassification review for the task force (some documents "cannot be released at this time"), and that full DHS grants require "random post-election manual counts of paper ballots." The task force posts it with an open-source supplement Aug 26.

The Aug 24 Mullin letter to the White House Transparency Task Force, as hosted by Just the News (file "08.20.2026 WHTF Letter  Commerce S1 SIGNED.pdf"), carries Word document properties Author and dc:creator "Disalvo, Karen", created 2026-08-24 16:44 ET in Microsoft Word for Microsoft 365 (read with pdfinfo, Nov 15). The White House copy (whitehouse.gov DHS-Election-Integrity-Memoranda.zip, with the Task Force's "Open Source Supplements" sheet dated Aug 26) has the same text with the document properties removed. Democracy Docket first reported the metadata (Aug 28; R).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin; DHS senior adviser Karen DiSalvo; White House Government Transparency Task Force; Just the News

tl.e: The White House (Government) Transparency Task Force releases, with the DHS Election Integrity Memoranda zip, an open-source supplement headed "Pursuant to Presidential Memorandum 'Promoting Government Transparency and Accountability'" linking the 2024 ODNI Annual Threat Assessment, the 2024 NIC memorandum "Foreign Threats to US Elections After Voting Ends in 2024," the 2020 House Administration vendor hearing, and a 2020 ES&S CEO op-ed calling for paper-ballot backups; the zip confirms Mullin's Aug 24 letter and the HSGP hand-count condition word for word.

Mullin tells reporters (Tuesday, Sept 1) DHS could be at polling places if there is "a threat to that polling place or we're serving a warrant on someone ... if we're serving a warrant we will be where we need to be," and gives a third exception: reports of specific undocumented immigrants at a location could be a reason to deploy. A subsequent DHS statement added that "ICE is not planning operations targeting polling locations" (per the Sept 4 House Homeland minority letter; an unnamed DHS official had used the same line Jul 31, Wisconsin Examiner). This departs from the Feb 2026 Heather Honey statement "There will be no ICE presence at polling locations."
Todd Blanche is confirmed as Attorney General "earlier this month" per Mullin's Sept 2, 2026 letter (exact confirmation date not stated; he was Acting AG through at least Aug 2026).

DHS Secretary Mullin writes Attorney General Blanche (Sept 2, 2026, on its face; scanned on whitehouse.gov as AG-Letter-S1-Signed.pdf), congratulating him on his confirmation "earlier this month" and, invoking DHS's Sector Risk Management Agency role for election infrastructure, informing him of "prior referrals" DHS made to DOJ "during my predecessor's tenure" (Noem); it makes no new requests and asks DOJ to "review these referrals." Referral 1: whether voting systems that count from barcodes or QR codes comply with HAVA Title III's voter-verifiable paper record and manual-audit requirement, 52 U.S.C. 21081(a)(2)(B); it cites EO 14248 and the CISA report in the White House "Vulnerabilities-in-Electronic-Voting-and-Ballot-Counting-Systems.zip" (p.4: hackers "could change the votes encoded in the barcode"). Referral 2: legality under the DPPA (18 U.S.C. 2721-2725) of states sharing motor-vehicle and voter data with ERIC and, via ERIC, with CEIR; DHS and DOJ met on it in Sept 2025. The letter asserts the ERIC model contract requires MVA data every 60 days and bars sending records indicating non-citizenship; cites a 2022 Colorado mailer to ~30,000 noncitizens, a 2026 Georgia SAVE run finding >42,000 deceased registrants, and a Feb 2026 Renton, WA ballots-by-dumpster claim (sourced to the Skagit County GOP); quotes the ERIC founder on Democratic targeting; and closes "as we support the President's America First agenda." It does not mention recounts and does not ask DOJ to investigate whether election nonprofits "improperly obtained" data in those words (earlier NOTUS/NYT summaries, R).
House Homeland Security Committee minority letter (Sept 4, 2026, pp.1-3) challenges Mullin's Sept 1 rationale (a threat or a warrant) for DHS presence at polling places.

Sens. Padilla and Schumer make public a USCIS whistleblower disclosure on the "Unlawful Voter Initiative" (Senate letter dated Sept 13, enclosing the Sept 8 disclosure letter; Padilla floor statement Sept 14). On the floor Padilla says he and Schumer wrote Mullin and USCIS Director Edlow demanding the program be halted and unreliable law-enforcement records deleted. The disclosure (hundreds of FDNS staff diverted, short training, "supplemental magic," ~40 subjects/day, raw data including "a lot of U.S. citizens," TECS records leading to HSI/FBI referral) is entered in the Congressional Record Sept 14 (S4641). Follow-ups: 16 senators ask DHS OIG to investigate; a 34-senator letter (incl. Kaine, Sept 28) combines the program, FEMA conditions and the TECS-to-HSI path. The CNA v. Mullin PI order (ECF 87 p.4) later recites from the disclosure that TECS records "can be used against [an individual] in any interaction they may have with the federal government" and that USCIS has created TECS records for U.S. citizens.
tl.a: Sens. Padilla and Schumer; USCIS whistleblower

tl.e: Lawfare links to Just the News and the Daily Signal for the text of Mullin's Aug 24 voting-machine letter.

In Hilton v. Mullin, No. 2:26-cv-00092-JAW (D. Me.), the government's motion to dismiss (ECF 117) says Agent J.C. documented plaintiff Carlyn Williams's name and vehicle in HSI's "Internal Case Management ('ICM') system," "which led to the March 2026 border stop referenced in the FAC" (n.13: he believed she was interfering with an arrest), and that J.C. documented subject records on 8 individuals he believed posed potential threats; no watchlist nomination (nn.12-13).

California Nurses Ass'n v. Mullin (N.D. Cal. 4:26-cv-10680) filed: challenges voter-matching and field operations incl. home visits questioning eligibility, intimidation of voter-assistance groups; PI hearing Oct 19.
tl.a: California Nurses Ass'n, NNU, City and County of San Francisco, Santa Clara County, Voto Latino (v. DHS, USCIS, ICE, CBP and officials)

tl.e: HSI "Enforcement Stats FY26 (last 7 days)": "Voter Fraud Cases Initiated: 869 1,163 (+497)."

On Fox News (Kayleigh McEnany, a Saturday, most likely Sept 19) Mullin says "We have 1,620 cases moving right now that are under investigation," 151 arrests, and "300,000 we're looking into and that list grows every single day"; he gave the same figures on CNN earlier that week. AP later reported 160 arrests.

CISA releases "2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan: Securing the Next 250" (Mullin "tasked CISA" with it in July): 10 regional directors as election-security advisers; CISA "coordinates closely with ... the FBI" on insider threats and calls the temporary workforce's insider risk "a structural feature of election administration"; CISA, DHS I&A and FBI route federal threat reporting to fusion centers and "through them" to election officials; an information-sharing platform on the FIFA World Cup model; VRDB logs retained "at least one year"; it says hackers "attempted to breach voter registration systems in all 50 states, with confirmed success in at least 20 states" (no country named; p.6, fn 4 = CISA web page "Vulnerabilities in Electronic Voting and Ballot-Counting Systems (2026)") and recommends "paper ballots that can be easily reviewed" and audits "before certifying" (p.5); the Plan contains no China/PRC, "human-readable," barcode or "not binding" wording (saved text searched in full). DHS release quotes Mullin: "Election security is national security ... will be implemented in full." The plan says seasonal and volunteer workers, contractors and vendors make insider threat structural and that foreign adversaries may "exploit insider access"; it reports 107 open-source election-related incidents in TRIPwire since Jan 1, 2022 (96 bomb threats) and, from 2022 to Aug 2026, 58 exercises, 53 C-IED trainings and 2,100+ physical security assessments (pp.7-8).
Minnesota indictments Sept 24 (ten defendants, HSI), announced Sept 30 (DOJ26-1119) by Blanche, Mullin, Rosen.

Supreme Court stays the June D.D.C. (Sooknanan) ruling that the revamped SAVE was unlawful, in DHS v. League of Women Voters, No. 26A308 (stay application filed Sept 8); states may use SAVE pending appeal. Reported: DHS said it kept using SSA data "to help determine whether illegal voting may have occurred" during the block; SAVE has run >65M voters and flagged 28,635; in Texas 21% of flagged voters were citizens; error rate not released (R). California SOS (PR26-121) says it will not use SAVE. The stay runs pending the D.C. Circuit appeal and any certiorari petition; Justices Jackson, Sotomayor and Kagan dissent (docket). The government's Sept 28 brief in CNA v. Mullin quotes the order: "individualized inquiries ... are permitted under federal law during this period" (slip 6), and the government is "likely to suffer irreparable harm" if ordered to stop sharing information on noncitizens on voter rolls (slip 5).

Senate Democrats' letter to Secretary Mullin warns against DHS election activities: "Taken together, these actions amount to an illegal attempt to federalize the administration of the upcoming midterm elections"; cites the FDNS whistleblower's account of an "Unlawful Voter Initiative" and the HSGP holdback.
tl.a: Sens. Peters, Padilla, Durbin, Schumer, Hassan, Blumenthal, Sanders and others

tl.e: Bartell declaration (CNA v. Mullin ECF 46-1): USCIS compares voter information from states, public and "other lawfully available data ... against DHS and commercial database holdings" (¶10); before the LWV order SAVE referred positive non-citizen matches to FDNS, and "Following the LWV order, SAVE stopped referring such information to FDNS," but FDNS kept using what SAVE had referred because it was by then held under the FDNS SORN (¶¶12-13); SAVE referrals were "only a small portion" of what FDNS reviewed (¶14); FDNS weighed "the possibility that in rare circumstances U.S. citizens might be incorrectly identified as aliens" and proceeded (¶17). Bartell says EO 14248 prompted FDNS to review noncitizens and naturalized citizens who may have voted before naturalization (para 9) and that FDNS "is not a SAVE User Agency" (n.1; para 15); FDNS's new Criminal Investigative Division is "not directly involved in the investigations into unlawful voting" (para 7); FDNS closes a review on derived/acquired citizenship or discrepancies except where data suggest voting or registration before naturalization (para 19).
tl.a: USCIS FDNS Assoc. Dir. Nicolas Bartell

tl.e: Government opposition in CNA v. Mullin (ECF 46) does not deny that TECS records are generated on matched voters but calls a TECS record a nonfinal "starting point" that "simply 'warrants further review'" (responding to plaintiffs' contention that "DHS's directive to generate TECS records flagging certain individuals for further scrutiny" is final agency action); says DHS used the "best data it had available" and interviews were "expressly designed to resolve the discrepancies"; as a fallback offers an injunction "akin to Paragraph 3.b." barring field operations against people DHS knows or should know are citizens, saying HSI filters already do that.

HSI declaration in CNA v. Mullin (ECF 46-2) says "USCIS transmits lists regarding aliens or USCs to HSI," HSI "will send to ERO to determine alienage," and "When potential inaccuracies were identified in the USCIS lists, DHS ... developed a new model for generating leads"; HSI does not interview everyone USCIS entered a TECS record for.
tl.a: HSI (Acting Deputy Assistant Director, CBFCC; name redacted)

tl.e: SEB resolution "Dominion Update Coordination": "the Federal government has deemed the voting systems to be 'critical infrastructure' and the Dominion systems are 'protected computers' within the meaning of 18 U.S.C. sec. 1030(e) such that the knowing transmission of information over a Dominion system that is compromised could impair the integrity of data"; forensic images of EMS and ICC hard drives to be "provided to the State Election Board, DHS and the US Department of Justice (DOJ) ... for examination, review, or investigation"; directs Mills to assist DHS and DOJ "pursuant to their letter of September 2, 2026" on QR codes (HAVA) and ERIC/CEIR data sharing (DPPA, NVRA). Mills's Sept 30 letters to Mullin and Blanche ask DOJ to set a six-month deadline, compel patching with forensic backups first, and "preserve all such records under federal supervision."
tl.a: Georgia State Election Board (member Carolyn Roddy; executive director James Mills)

tl.e: DHS admits Americans may be watchlisted by mistake (Reason Sept 30); Palantir ICM records auto-shared to CBP TECS as lookouts (Maine litigation; Wired); HSI agent declaration in CNA v. Mullin: DHS "developed a new model for generating leads for HSI's unlawful voting investigations."

Hilton v. Mullin (D. Me.) filings: ECF 129 plaintiffs' response on First Amendment discovery privilege (Oct 1); ECF 132-40 Hilton and 132-42 Pantos supplemental declarations (Oct 2); ECF 142, 142-5, 142-10 (Oct 9); ECF 145 (signed Oct 9, filed Oct 13). ECF 129 (plaintiffs) says the government seeks community Signal chats and the names of people who identified federal employees and vehicles, and that the record shows at least one HSI agent in Maine planned to infiltrate a community group. ECF 145 opposes defendants' motions to seal (ECF 119, 137) agent names, Signal-chat content, ICM/TECS information, the OCTD operations order (PI Ex. 29), a briefing deck (Ex. 30) and a roster (Ex. 45).

Plaintiffs file their PI motion in redacted public form (ECF 132; unredacted version ECF 101-1 under seal), alleging use of HSI ICM and CBP TECS to create records on people observing immigration enforcement (deposition testimony); ECF 145 (Oct 13) later asks for public filing of the unredacted motion.

NYT, from documents: on the morning of March 24, Noem's last in office, DHS approved a contract change to buy the five most expensive planes in its no-bid Daedalus deal (a converted 737 for $108M; two Gulfstreams for $53M each; two 737s for $45M each), well above what Daedalus paid or experts called market value. Two White House officials said Mullin considered backing out but Wiles told him not to block it. Walters gave $10,000 to a PAC that supported Noem.
tl.a: DHS (Kristi Noem; Markwayne Mullin); Daedalus Aviation (William Walters); Susie Wiles

tl.e: Senators' letter to Mullin demands evidence for noncitizen claims, the "Unlawful Voter Initiative," and rescission of HSGP election conditions (IBs 569, 569a).

CNA v. Mullin ECF 67 grants record completion for safeguard documents; ECF 71 (Oct 13) describes Nov 2025 email, Aug 2026 FAQs, Sept 2026 email instructing naturalization/passport/travel checks. ECF 67 (Judge Martinez-Olguin) requires FDNS documents on "safeguards intended to reduce the risk" of erroneous referral under the "Unlawful Voter Initiative Policy" and vacates the Oct 6 hearing.
Newly unsealed filings in the Maine observers case (Hilton v. Mullin) include agent deposition excerpts; other depositions remain sealed.
Ed Martin (Bolling interview): Mullin concluded machines are "compromised."

CNN and others report on the Oct 1 ICE FOIA release (Democracy Forward v. DHS): HSI ingested 50.6M DOJ-sourced voter records and 48.4M records "obtained by DAS Heather Honey through independent sources" (CNA v. Mullin ECF 87 gives 48.2M); data sent to iLab "for secondary enrichment and identification of high-value targets"; some records pending "entry into ELITE" (all D, FOIA); HSI reviewed "150+" voter-registration organizations (reporter's sum of component counts), considered undercover agents, and shared status updates with the White House from July (R, CNN). Palantir: "Voter roll data has never been integrated into ELITE" (R).

Plaintiffs' opposition to the motion to dismiss (Hilton v. Mullin ECF 142) argues the ICM and TECS records about Williams and her vehicle "have already led to Williams's (and Pantos's) detention once and [redacted], at least through January 2027" (citing CBP 30(b)(6) Dep. 146:7-147:10); each observer's ICM record carries a designation redacted in the public copy; and defendants "agreed to conduct only very limited database searches, excluding many of the databases discussed in the FAC" (n.37) (arguments, not findings). The brief also says ICE's Rule 30(b)(6) witness testified that threatening observers with a "domestic terrorist" designation was an appropriate "deescalation" technique consistent with DHS policy, and that no training on the 2019 DHS First Amendment memo was identified (pp.5-9, 15, 20).

Acting DAG McCotter sends letters (Oct 13) to California SoS Shirley Weber and LA County Registrar Dean Logan with a list of people DOJ "believes are likely noncitizens" who were mailed ballots, giving 48 hours (noon Oct 15) to verify; they are to "segregate not cancel" those mail ballots, send no new ballots and pause signature verification and tabulation, or DOJ "will seek emergency relief"; the letters cite 18 U.S.C. 611 and Norwood v. Harrison and ask the officials to work with DHS. HSI Assistant Director McLoughlin helps deliver the list (just over 20,000 names) to DOJ and the USAO (C.D. Cal.), and an HSI special agent serves the demand letter and the list on an encrypted drive at the LA County Registrar-Recorder's Norwalk office, handing it to the receptionist (Dkt 62-3 para 24, Ex. A, D). Per the order (D): on Oct 13 DOJ "hand-delivered a letter and password-protected thumb drive" to Logan containing PII of "over 20,000 individuals," while Weber was "emailed the same requests with a 48-hour deadline without an accompanying list" (ECF 149 pp.3-4, Compl. Ex. C; Weber Oct 15 letter p.2: "despite failing to send the list ... to my office, you demand that we request transmittal"). Instructions per the order: review the list within 48 hours, (1) segregate VBM ballots of non-confirmed citizens, (2) withhold unsent ballots, (3) not verify signatures or tabulate until citizenship is confirmed (Compl. Ex. D). LA County says it would not open the drive. DOJ release 26-196 gave the >20,000 count; our Oct 17 notes add that the password was on a sticky note (not in the order; R) and that DHS earlier claimed 190,000; Mullin called it a "preliminary analysis."
DHS S&T "Securing the World Cup" counter-drone named Innovation of the Year; Mullin (Jul 21): nearly 2,000 drones brought down.
Current-case safeguards production describing restricted supplemental material.

Defendants file the safeguards supplement to the administrative record in Cal. Nurses v. Mullin (ECF 71, Oct 13; exhibit ECF 73-1 sealed) and move to seal the supplemental AR (Dkt 74) as containing "detailed internal procedures, operational safeguards, and investigative methodologies that USCIS [FDNS] personnel employ when investigating unlawful voting"; the court grants sealing Oct 21 (ECF 87 pp.5, 17-18).
Democracy Defenders Fund files a Hatch Act complaint against Mullin, Edlow and Blanche over the Omar search.

Defendants reply ISO motion to dismiss (ECF 149); plaintiffs file PI reply with deposition excerpts of D.L., ICE 30(b)(6), J.C., J.R., S.C. and exhibits 68-83, under seal motion (ECF 148, 150); plaintiffs move for oral argument (ECF 151).
At PI hearing judge called requested relief "amorphous," signaled unlikely PI on APA claims, took VRA claims under advisement.

The CNA v. Mullin preliminary-injunction order finds that DHS data include 48.2 million records received "through independent sources" plus DOJ's voter-roll data, and that DHS "enriches" data through iLab, "using unknown artificial intelligence tools to ingest data from various systems and create a compiled list of individual profiles." The order also recites 50.6M records from DOJ (official rolls or, for non-sharing states, "unreliable commercial versions"), USCIS told to treat DHS source data as "presumptively valid," a 40-subject surge quota (~12 minutes per person), 1,586 leads to 24 HSI field offices from 2,290 records, and review of naturalized citizens for pre-naturalization voting.
tl.a: N.D. Cal. (CNA v. Mullin PI order)

tl.e: Judge Martínez-Olguín (California Nurses Ass'n v. Mullin, ECF 87) bars DHS election-related field operations and interviews involving people agents know, suspect or "should reasonably know or suspect" are citizens, including operations "based wholly on TECS records" from the matching, in nine states (CA, CT, GA, MO, NV, NY, PA, WA, WI); calls the target list "voluminous and unreliable" and finds likely voter intimidation under VRA §11(b) (APA and right-to-vote claims not reached); DHS's stated intent to target only noncitizens "does not cure" the reasonable fear. Stayed to 5 p.m. Oct 23; $100 bond due 5 p.m. Oct 22; runs only to 8 p.m. Nov 3 "or when polling places close." Only CNA/NNU have standing (associational, VRA sec. 11(b) intimidation of voter assistance and mobilization); the local governments and Voto Latino lack standing; sec. 11(b) carries an implied private right of action and reaches federal officials (pp.7-17).
Plaintiffs post the $100 bond in CNA v. Mullin (ECF 88); no stay motion or appeal as of Oct 22, 4:47 p.m.

CNA v. Mullin order takes effect 5 p.m. Oct 23 (runs to 8 p.m. Nov 3): (a) no elections-related field operations or interviews in nine states involving persons the enjoined parties know, suspect, or should reasonably know or suspect are U.S. citizens; (b) no elections-related field operations "based wholly on TECS records generated from the Voter Eligibility Matching Policy" against such persons (reading (b) as a subset of (a) is I). Court: "There is no federal database containing citizenship status of U.S. residents." DHS: "We have no plans to question or investigate people we believe to be U.S. citizens" (the court applies an objective standard, not DHS's belief); no stay request was reported by then.

CISA releases strategy "CISA 2030: Defend, Harden, Prevail" (cover Oct 2026; press release Oct 26): implements the President's Cyber Strategy for America (Mar 2026), the National Resilience Strategy (Jun 2026) and EO 14239; moves "from passive defense to an aggressive, anticipatory stance"; "deprioritize threat-agnostic, all-hazards approaches"; "integrate intelligence" pipeline with the IC; "maintain and analyze infrastructure data"; NS/EP communications lead; 60/180/365-day milestones. The word "election" does not appear in the strategy. Coverage (R): service review, "sharper focus" on critical-infrastructure threats; AI risks termed "super intelligence" (echoing the Sept 29 EO's terminology mandate); helps the White House build a "National Risk Register."
tl.a: CISA (Acting Dir. Nick Andersen; DHS Sec. Mullin foreword)

tl.e: DOJ files a notice of appeal to the Ninth Circuit from the CNA v. Mullin preliminary injunction (Dkt. 89, Oct 26), four days after plaintiffs posted the bond (Dkt. 88, Oct 22); named defendants include Edlow, Homan, Mullin, Salisbury, Scott and Venturella.
DOJ files an ex parte application to stay the CNA v. Mullin preliminary injunction pending appeal, with a Declaration of James C. Harris (Dkt 90); plaintiffs oppose the same day (Dkt 91).

At a CISA all-hands, Mullin says DHS will hold a post-election "debrief" to weigh changes to voting systems to improve voter trust in outcomes, and that DHS is not trying to "suppress" votes; scope unstated.

DHS release "Dozens of Illegal Aliens Arrested In Nationwide Voter Fraud Crackdown": ICE "has arrested dozens of individuals in connection with alleged voter fraud and election-related offenses"; it lists 13 examples, two described as having "illegally voted in the 2026 election," with alleged votes ranging from 1992 to 2026, each framed by criminal history; it says the government is "investigating alleged violations" by "aliens who admitted to voting." Mullin: "American elections are for Americans only." No total, no charges count, and no states given for most examples.

At a CISA all-hands, per an anonymous CISA official, Mullin said he would hold a post-election "debrief," that DHS was not seeking to "suppress" votes, and that he would weigh whether system changes were needed to improve voter trust; scope and who conducts it unclear. (R, Nextgov; Politico first)
Ninth Circuit denies DOJ's stay of the CNA v. Mullin injunction barring DHS election-related field operations in nine states; government "had not carried its burden."
Mullin tells Newsmax noncitizens on voter rolls "top 300,000" (headline; full text not retrieved).

Mullin says DHS sent DOJ a "large case" involving multiple people in the Omar probe; a DOJ filing refers to Omar and "other individuals"; more than a dozen grand-jury subpoenas in Minnesota; no charges.

CNN: Mullin says "Our job is to make sure that it's a legal ballot and it's counted" and "to make sure there's not vulnerabilities where bad actors can get into the system and change the vote," alleging past vulnerabilities without evidence; DHS stood up a last-minute online threat-intelligence platform and CISA an information-sharing tool that officials trust less than past channels.

DOJ stay motion (ECF 33, Nov 1, pp.13-19): Section 11(b) "does not apply to the federal government" (citing Judge Tung's dissental in CNA v. Mullin: "person" does not include the sovereign; "It is nonsensical that the Attorney General would sue the United States on behalf of the United States"); 11(b)'s definition of "vote" "presupposes a lawful vote," so it "protects those who aid qualified voters"; an "accurate statement of federal criminal law" cannot be "intimidation" at all; "the Elections Clause in no way limits or applies to the executive branch"; prosecution decisions get "a presumption of regularity." Democracy Docket reported the same argument Nov 2 (R).
tl.a: DOJ (SEIU v. DOJ, N.D. Cal. 3:26-cv-12800, ECF 33, stay motion; also argued in NAACP v. Blanche per reporting)

tl.e: On Election Day, Mullin tells Fox News: "ICE agents aren't going to be around polling places unless there's a threat"; "The only reason you'd see the Department of Homeland Security is if there's a threat"; "That's not their job. We're enforcing immigration." DHS also announces arrests of people from the Philippines, Italy, Finland, Algeria and Iraq for voting in 2024 (no names or totals reported); Mullin: "Only American citizens should be deciding American elections."

On Fox News on Election Day: "After this election we'll be gathering all the data, we'll be gathering the voting logs" ... "making sure that no illegals voted"; DHS "will be looking at the registers" and "all those that voted"; "it is still DHS' job to make sure that this was an election that was handled by the federal laws." No legal authority or method named. On X: "If you vote illegally, we will find you." ICE on X: "There will be no escape."

Thompson writes DHS Secretary Mullin demanding compliance with all document-preservation requirements and written assurance by Nov 11 "that Departmental records, documents, data, and information have not been and will not be destroyed, modified, removed, transferred, or otherwise rendered inaccessible"; the committee "intends to closely observe the compliance of the Department—and all its components"; responses to outstanding requests due by Dec 2; "In the 120th Congress, the Committee intends to address the Trump administration's assault on the rule of law" (D).
tl.a: House Homeland Security Democrats (Ranking Member Bennie Thompson, D-Miss.)

tl.e: Right-wing blogger Joe Hoft revives the FEC filing-system outage (Oct 27-28) as a "Midterm Early Voting Cyberattack" and asks "Where Is Secretary Mullin and Homeland Security?" The reporting he cites does not show a successful intrusion. (R)

DHS releases: at the White House Task Force (2028 Olympics) drone forum, Mullin: drones are "a serious and growing threat to public safety, critical infrastructure, and national security"; DHS is "building a lasting capability"; $250M FY27 Counter-UAS grants open to all 56 states and territories. In the Austin release: "No matter how much sanctuary politicians try to obstruct us, the patriots of ICE will keep doing their jobs." No election statement. (D)

DHS: ICE made more than 491,000 immigration arrests (nearly 475,000 administrative) and 483,200 deportations in FY26, records; 50,925 arrests in August. Mullin: "ICE has been unleashed to target and remove illegal aliens so that we can save American lives." DHS: "more than 3 million migrants have left the U.S."

American Oversight sued DHS and USCIS (D.D.C.) to force release of records on the USCIS "Unlawful Voter Initiative": six FOIA requests from Sept 16 for emails of Mullin, Deputy Secretary Troy Edgar, Senior Counselor Heather Honey and USCIS's Joseph Edlow using "unlawful voter," "voter fraud," "state voter," "FDNS enhancement"; Aug 21 training materials; review quotas; data sources and matching software; contacts with officials in 19 states and D.C. The suit cites a whistleblower disclosure (forwarded by Sens. Padilla and Schumer) that FDNS officers were reassigned to review voter rolls with quotas of five cases an hour and 40 a day.
tl.a: American Oversight; DHS; USCIS (Mullin, Edgar, Honey, Edlow)

tl.e: DHS release (sent Nov 16) on the Kinetic IV Counter-UAS Test Event, Stringtown, Okla., Nov 12: "This was the first time the event had been held at the Choctaw Nation of Oklahoma Emerging Aviation Technology Center (EATC), which had been championed by Secretary Mullin during his time in the U.S. Senate." Mullin: "DHS is working with state, local, tribal, and territorial partners, industry, and international allies to evaluate technologies that can address the evolving threat posed by unmanned systems," and "I am especially proud that the Choctaw Nation's Emerging Aviation Technology Center is hosting this critical work." Separately (Fox, Nov 15, via Epoch Times): "Absolutely not," "I'm not stockpiling," "This was a catastrophic outage that we were able to overcome."
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; DHS S&T Under Secretary Pedro Allende; Choctaw Nation Chief Gary Batton; Bahrain Ambassador Shaikh Abdulla bin Rashid Al Khalifa

tl.e: DHS S&T release on its Nov 3-13 counter-drone test at the Choctaw Nation's FAA-designated testbed, "championed by" Mullin as a senator; Mullin: "DHS is working with state, local, tribal, and territorial partners, industry, and international allies to evaluate technologies that can address the evolving threat posed by unmanned systems"; "I am especially proud that the Choctaw Nation's Emerging Aviation Technology Center is hosting this critical work."
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; DHS S&T (Under Secretary Pedro Allende)

tl.e: At a White House briefing on the FAA nationwide ground stop, Mullin: "There is no indication, and we have no reason to believe that as of right now that this was a threat to the United States"; "there was no indication, as of yet, that this was a nefarious act against us"; "We're not ruling out anything at this point"; "I don't want to say that this is a crisis, but it is"; on the FAA's new AI tool: "That's part of something that obviously, through CISA at DHS, we're taking a look." Fox: DHS "not ruling out" a cyberattack. Duffy reopened the airspace at 8:15 pm ET.
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy

tl.e: DHS release of the White House FAA briefing quotes Mullin: "This is what the Department of Homeland Security is all about. This is why we were stood up, to have a continuity of government to bring all the resources together in an emergency like this... This is a national emergency. We have all of our assets, be it from DOW, to CISA, to all of our NOCs ... NSA is working with us." And: "The President has declared this a national emergency, and now we have to have Congress act and fund it." Also: "We have seen zero evidence that this is a cyberattack or an SI attack." No proclamation, executive order or National Emergencies Act notice published (White House presidential actions and Federal Register public inspection checked Nov 14).
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin (with DOT Secretary Sean Duffy)

tl.e: SecurityWeek (citing Bloomberg): the FBI is examining whether a software update caused the FAA outage and does not think a cyberattack or criminal activity was behind it; Mullin says NSA, DoD, CISA and others were involved; "there's no chatter, we haven't seen any footprints ... we're not going to rule that out." No official root cause announced.
tl.a: FBI; NSA; Department of War; CISA

tl.e: DHS release (Nov 13; also quoted by Newsweek): "This is a national security risk because our air traffic control system is outdated and it hasn't been a priority from Congress. This is what happens when Congress kicks the can down the road."

Potter County Republican Party v. Benge (N.D. Tex. 2:26-cv-00215-Z, Kacsmaryk), ECF 72 First Amended Class Action Complaint (the Oct 27 original already sought the statewide defendant class, the pre-certification hand count, and cited Mullin's Aug 24 and Sept 2 letters; NEW in the amendment: plaintiff Alexander Hale, CISA's plan, results "corrected to match," and the reconciliation gaps). Keeps a defendant class of "similarly situated Texas county election officials" ("all the counties in Texas"); asks that "before final certification" all lawful paper ballots in the federal races of Nov 3 be hand counted and results "confirmed, or corrected to match the hand count"; a statewide hand count "in all precincts in Texas"; preservation of ballots, ballot images, cast vote records and chain-of-custody records. Opens: "Election security is national security." Relies on Mullin's Aug 24 letter (China-made parts, "synchronized attacks"), Mullin's Sept 2 letter to AG Blanche (QR/barcode ballots may not meet HAVA 52 U.S.C. 21081(a)(2)(B); EO 14248), CISA's 2026 Election Infrastructure Security Plan ("Securing the Next 250": "post-election manual audits ... before certifying"), and the Mar 20, 2026 router "National Security Determination." Cites preliminary-reconciliation gaps: Harris -4,085, Dallas -544, Randall -71, Lubbock +245. Potter County audit set for Nov 16; defense reply due Nov 17.
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party, Daniel Rogers, Alexander Hale (attys Jared Woodfill, Daniel Bates); defendant Christy Benge (Potter County Elections Administrator)

tl.e: Plaintiffs' response to the county's motion to dismiss (N.D. Tex. 2:26-cv-00215-Z, ECF 73): the injury is not "potential foreign actor and AI-assisted third-party interference" but unequal treatment, since each custodian decides whether a discrepancy leads to any further count; again quotes Mullin's Aug 24 letter ("election security is national security"; parts "manufactured by foreign adversaries introduce significant security risks"); says "DHS and FEMA have conditioned federal grant funds on a post-election manual audit of at least five percent of paper ballots"; the claims "challenge the procedure for counting and certifying in the face of vulnerabilities federal reviewers have found." County reply due Nov 17.
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party, Daniel Rogers, Alexander Hale (Woodfill Law Firm); Potter County Elections Administrator Christy Benge

tl.e: Mullin takes a government plane to the LSU-Texas football game in Baton Rouge less than 24 hours after the FAA ground stop, while travelers are still stranded; on Nov 17 he defends the use of the plane. (R, headlines: AP, CNN, USA Today, NY Post, Fox News, Nov 17)

Asked whether a bad actor could have flooded the Arkansas routers: "I don't believe in coincidences until I'm proven wrong. And right now, I'm being proved wrong"; "So is it a possibility? ... Possibly"; "with 98 percent certainty, that this was ... a 50-year-old system"; "use all 22 of our components to make sure that's not taking place. And if it did, we'd be honest with the American people and say, 'This is what's taken place, this is who did it, and this is who we're going after.'" On Iran: Trump and family "target number one"; drone threats "very aspirational, but we are well prepared inside the United States" (R, Daily Beast; Fox live blog).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin (Fox News, The Sunday Briefing, host Peter Doocy)

tl.e: Word-run comparison (8-word runs) of the Potter County complaints against the primary Aug 24 letter: ECF 1 reproduces 354 of the letter's 758 words, ECF 72 reproduces 374, including both ODNI quotes, the full China-parts paragraph and the footnote URLs. ECF 72 paras 1, 2 and 5 state the letter's sentences as the plaintiffs' own allegations without quotation marks ("Election security is national security. Electronic voting systems have one job..."; "States must trust but verify the results produced by the voting machines"), footnoted to the letter or to CISA's plan. ECF 1's "rogue artificial intelligence" paragraph (no source cited) is gone from ECF 72. Docket (CourtListener, 72 entries): no standalone preliminary-injunction motion filed after the Nov 4 order (ECF 50) and the Nov 6 extension request (ECF 58, citing "the loss of a second attorney"); intervention motions by DSCC/DCCC and Common Cause/LWV Texas/MOVE Texas/NAACP Texas undecided; ECF 43 (plaintiffs' certificate of interested persons) lists no financially interested persons and names "DSCC and DCCC" as the filer; the county's motion to dismiss (ECF 59/60/63, County Attorney C. Scott Brumley) calls the suit "statewide intervention into the process of certifying election results based on no more than theoretical possibility."
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party, Daniel Rogers, Alexander Hale (Woodfill Law Firm; Daniel Bates); DHS Sec. Mullin

tl.e: Mullin calls counter-drone his number one issue, says DHS saw more than 2,000 drones during the World Cup (700 confiscated), says "we're seeing new technologies that we're having a hard time defeating right now," and lists where he wants the same protection next: the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, critical infrastructure, high school football, parades, college and NFL games, "any mass gathering" (as reported by DroneXL). Same interview: "I don't think anybody's going to get fired over this. This was an issue with the equipment" (The Hill).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin (Fox News, The Sunday Briefing)

tl.e: On Fox's Hannity, Mullin says of the recent outages (FAA, Microsoft, banks): CISA told him "we're not seeing any traffic that would make us think that this is a cyberattack, they're all individually unrelated"; an unnamed tech source told him "I believe that it's the SI"; "it causes these systems to be over[run] that weren't designed to run as fast as the SI technology is today ... That kind of makes sense to me"; "the backup systems are overwhelmed by the new systems now." HuffPost reports he put his certainty there was no cyberattack at 98%. On Nov 17 CNBC headlined him: "We are not under attack."

On the FAA outage: "I believe that it's the SI" (superintelligence, relaying an unnamed tech-industry contact's theory about self-coding, self-fixing programs) and "with 98% certainty, we're not seeing a cyber attack." (R, Fortune, Nov 17)
tl.a: DHS Sec. Markwayne Mullin (Fox News, Hannity)

tl.e: On CNBC: "Let me tell you what this is not, as far as we can tell … this is not a cyberattack, and this is not a coordinated effort by a nation state. We've looked very closely"; "many people are patching their systems ... it is time for an upgrade across our digital infrastructure." The Hill: Clayton "echoed Mullin's point" on "SI." (R)

Washington Sun (Jeff Stein): Wall Street executives and the NSA told members of Congress the outages were caused by attempts to fix vulnerabilities "identified by artificial intelligence"; a briefed congressional official: "They're trying to push through a lot of patches all at once — more than the system was designed for." NSA publicly cited "scheduled routine maintenance." Mullin to CNBC: "they're pushing new technology on top of really old computer systems, and it just seems to overwhelm the system. ... We're going to see more of this as new technology rolls out." (R)

Politico Playbook (Nov 19): "Markwayne Mullin is on a primetime time-out"; Miller "intervened in the early morning hours from Manila" on Tuesday to replace Mullin with DNI Jay Clayton and Secretary of State Rubio as the administration's voices on the outages, after Mullin's Nov 16 Hannity appearance drew "WTF" messages in administration group chats; a person close to the White House: "We need to speak with one voice and the right voice, and the decision was made to put Jay out there." An administration official disputed the account to The Blaze: "We wanted to make sure that the top official with the best knowledge was the person who went out on each of these topics." (Politico read through Political Wire, Just the News, The Blaze and The New Republic; original not read.)
tl.a: Stephen Miller (White House chief of staff); Markwayne Mullin; Jay Clayton; Marco Rubio

tl.e: CNN live: a senior administration official says the outages are not a cyberattack and not connected to "any actor" or state sponsor, but the result of "upgrades of the systems"; asked how systems would respond to a real attack: "That is a question the American people should be asking." NSA network patching is going "slower than expected." Vance pulled out of the NYT DealBook Summit; his office: he "has been asked to attend meetings amid the wave of outages." Mullin, Clayton and FBI Deputy Director Raia testify to House Homeland at 10 am. (R)
tl.a: Senior administration official; NSA; JD Vance

tl.e: Mullin's written testimony, "2026 Worldwide Threats to the Homeland": domestic violent extremists include "anarchists and anti-fascists" and people motivated by "opposition to law and immigration enforcement; extreme views in favor of mass migration and open borders; adherence to radical gender ideology; and anti-Semitism, anti-Americanism, anti-capitalism, or anti-Christianity"; CISA has shifted "from passively defending toward proactively identifying, mitigating, and reducing malicious access to critical infrastructure" and launched "CI Fortify" to prepare operators "for sustained essential operations during a potential geopolitical conflict"; threats include "cybersecurity attacks from adversarial super intelligence (SI)"; "election security is national security"; for 2026 CISA addressed election threats "by information sharing"; he urges Congress to reauthorize FISA 702 and the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act (D).
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; House Homeland Security Committee; CISA

tl.e: House Homeland worldwide-threats hearing (R, CNN live): Clayton has "a very high level of confidence" the week's outages were not a cyberattack: "They are different causes ... Do we see any of them here? We do not see them"; Iranian "lethal plotting" has "substantially increased." Raia, asked by Thompson whether the President ever directed the FBI to investigate or not investigate anyone: "Absolutely not"; asked to name a right-wing group that might qualify as a domestic terror threat: "I don't want to paint a broad brush here" (he named Antifa). Mullin on the Nvidia matter: "We weren't privileged to that information at all until it broke"; DHS is not involved because it was "outside of my lane"; "If it was a direct threat to the homeland, I would have been I would have been right in on it." Garbarino criticized FBI Director Patel for not appearing.
tl.a: DNI Jay Clayton; FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia; DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; Rep. Bennie Thompson; Rep. Seth Magaziner; Chairman Andrew Garbarino

tl.e: DHS release, "DHS Denounces Texas Officials for Allegedly Planning to End Cooperation with ICE": Mullin: "If Texas were to stop cooperating with ICE and become a sanctuary state, it would be one of the worst derelictions of duty we've seen in a very long time"; "We are calling on Governor-elect Hinojosa and other leaders throughout the state to continue cooperating with us. If they do not, then crime and violence will plague the Lone Star State, and innocent Americans will suffer as more sanctuary politicians put illegal alien criminals over their own constituents" (D).
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; Texas Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa

tl.e: CISA's "CI Fortify" page (as saved Nov 18; Mullin's Nov 18 written testimony: "Earlier this year, CISA launched CI Fortify"): operators should prepare "to sustain essential operations during a geopolitical conflict," assume third-party connections "will be unreliable" and "threat actors will have some access to the OT network," plan for "safe operations for weeks to months while isolated," identify "critical customers, such as military infrastructure," and track "CISA and Sector Risk Management Agency (SRMA) communications to know when to isolate." Andersen: "In a geopolitical crisis, the critical infrastructure organizations Americans rely on must be able to continue delivering—at a minimum—crucial services." (D)
tl.a: CISA (Acting Director Nick Andersen); Sector Risk Management Agencies

tl.e: CNA v. Mullin (N.D. Cal. 4:26-cv-10680), ECF 107: plaintiffs file a notice of voluntary dismissal without prejudice under Rule 41(a)(1)(A)(i); the court terminates the case Nov 18. (D)
tl.a: California Nurses Association; National Nurses United; Voto Latino Foundation; San Francisco; Santa Clara County; DHS (Mullin)

tl.e: Mullin's written House Homeland testimony: "Since February, Iranian activity has increasingly targeted the transportation, healthcare, water, energy, and financial services sectors. These operations historically have produced localized and minimally disruptive effects against poorly secured industrial control devices, but vulnerable systems and weak cyber hygiene in lifeline infrastructure could create disruptive consequences" (D). At the hearing: "What happens online is [there] is a tremendous amount of fear, and we can understand it ... but there's no cause for it" (R, IBTimes). Clayton: agencies "have no evidence that this is a coordinated cyberattack or state-sponsored activity" (R). The NSA's internal network went down Tuesday Nov 17 in "temporary degradation during schedule routine maintenance" (R).
tl.a: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin; DNI Jay Clayton

tl.e: Bloomberg (Myles Miller, Ellen Milligan, Nov 18): Mullin's written testimony: "Iranian government cyber actors and pro-Iran cybercriminals have targeted US critical infrastructure networks since the conflict with Iran began earlier this year"; Clayton at the hearing: "These are separate service outages associated with maintenance and technical changes ... They are not a coordinated or state-sponsored attack"; Raia: "At this point, there is no indication whatsoever that there is any cyber malicious activity related to any of those incidents"; Raia's written testimony says Iran, North Korea and Russia are establishing "footholds in US critical infrastructure that could be exploited during a future crisis or conflict." Vance blamed the war in part for the midterm loss; per the NYT, Trump is weighing new strikes "as Israel increasingly pressures Washington to move quickly." Rubio said Nov 17 the outages were unrelated and not hostile.
tl.a: Markwayne Mullin; Jay Clayton; Christopher Raia; Marco Rubio

tl.e: DHS and GSA, "in coordination with the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud chaired by Vice President JD Vance," say 1,579 firms holding over $53 billion in federal contracts are potentially noncompliant with E-Verify (FAR 52.222-54); notices dated Nov 16 give 30 days (to Dec 16) or referral to the contracting officer. The Mullin-Forst letter to Senior Procurement Executives: "By matching up E-Verify and SAM data, we identified a set of contractors that may potentially not be in compliance"; COs to issue "a letter of concern" to firms left on the list. Mullin: "For too long, federal contractors have been raking in billions of dollars with too little scrutiny. That ends now." (D)
tl.a: DHS (Markwayne Mullin); GSA (Edward C. Forst); White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud (JD Vance, chair; Scott Brady, executive director); USCIS E-Verify

tl.e: CNA v. Mullin (N.D. Cal. 4:26-cv-10680), ECF 108: the Ninth Circuit approves the parties' joint stipulation and dismisses the government's appeal of the preliminary injunction (filed Nov 19), after plaintiffs' voluntary dismissal.
tl.a: Ninth Circuit; DHS (Mullin); USCIS (Edlow); ICE (Venturella); CBP (Scott); Homan; Salisbury

tl.e: DHS launches "Sanctuary Insanity," "a new daily series by the Department of Homeland Security highlighting the insanity of sanctuary politicians," opening on Minneapolis and Hennepin County; Mullin: "This is sanctuary insanity at work ... Sanctuary policies only serve to protect criminal illegal aliens while putting every single American at risk."

Stanford Daily v. Rubio (9th Cir. 26-6906): the government's opening brief appeals N.D. Cal. 5:25-cv-06618-NW, where the court declared the INA's deportation and visa-revocation provisions violate the First and Fifth Amendments "with respect to enforcement based on protected speech"; the brief calls that "circular and absurd"; related case AAUP v. Rubio (D. Mass. 1:25-cv-10685).
tl.a: Marco Rubio; Markwayne Mullin; DOJ Civil Division

tl.e: DHS Secretary Mullin meets UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed in Abu Dhabi; state media say they discussed "regional developments" and ties; DHS posts photo pages of Mullin at an Oklahoma sheriffs' banquet and Melton Truck Lines. No new on-record Mullin quote on the outages, elections or voting systems found Nov 21-22.

WSJ (Michelle Hackman, Nov 21): "A week of widely criticized choices has renewed calls within the administration to get rid of Mullin"; Miller "this week ordered Mullin to stop appearing on television" after Mullin said on Hannity some outages "could be attributed to artificial intelligence"; Mullin then "left for a three-country swing through the Middle East" against some advisers' advice; Mullin "is also one of the government's top cybersecurity officials"; firing him is harder because "Democrats will take over the Senate in January, giving the White House just a few weeks to confirm a potential replacement," and first-term acting secretaries were found improperly appointed so "nearly every major policy they signed got voided"; Mullin's nominee for ICE, his former bodyguard Lance Schroyer, was pulled; White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis: "The President has confidence in his entire Administration"; Mike Howell (Mass Deportation Coalition): "People are using him as a proxy for decisions actually being made at the White House."
tl.a: Markwayne Mullin; Stephen Miller; White House

tl.e: Janelle King appointed to Georgia State Election Board.

ProPublica (Doug Bock Clark, Nov 13): recordings, board documents and EIN communications show board members and much of the professional staff working with EIN and allied groups; five sources say Mills worked closely with EIN members; at least three of eight staff attended EIN meetings; chair Fervier: "the Election Integrity Network has been having an undue influence on the State Election Board"; Fervier accused Mills of exceeding board authority by calling for DOJ and DHS to assess the state's voting machines.
tl.a: Georgia State Election Board (Executive Director James Mills; members Janice Johnston, Janelle King); Election Integrity Network (Cleta Mitchell)

tl.e: House Judiciary testimony urging Congress to enact the SAVE Act; no federal database proposal.
DHS associate chief of USCIS briefed Cleta Mitchell's Election Integrity Network on using SAVE to "aid in assuring that noncitizens are removed from our voter rolls."

Urged Commerce Sec. Lutnick to use regulatory authority (EO 13873 foreign-adversary supply chain; foreign-made parts) over voting machines before midterms: "impose mitigation or prohibition"; Ed Martin account of Oval meeting; Becker: "The commerce secretary has no authority."

Mitchell argues EO 13873 (May 2019 ICT supply-chain emergency) lets Commerce Sec. Lutnick require changes to Georgia voting software; Martin recounted Peters' White House meeting on his show (Democracy Docket); a transcribed Oct 6 appearance in project notes has him urging Commerce action (recording not linked, U).
Votebeat: Mitchell argues the 2019 EO 13873 emergency lets Commerce compel a partial hand count; Lindell: "The president needs to completely declare a national emergency."

Reported HSI workflow: state voter files and DOJ records (50.6M) plus ~48.4M records sourced via Heather Honey (FOIA figure; the CNA order gives 48.2M "through independent sources" and does not name her) -> HSI iLab matching/enrichment (Athena named; this production does not name RAVEn) -> leads -> HSI operations/organization reviews -> proposed ELITE entry (later reported not integrated); the Athena voter-matching pilot preceded the 2026 expansion; enriched records for 6 states awaiting ELITE.

Announced participation in pilot to improve SAVE with DHS, USCIS, DOGE (33 referrals to AG); Dec 9, 2025 Texas-DOJ MOU; Mar 25, 2026 meeting of TX SoS GC Adam Bitter with Heather Honey and USCIS; Apr 28 USCIS reply naming FDNS and SAVE leads; Nelson raised erroneous citizenship flags.
Heather Honey (who challenged 2020 results) appointed DHS deputy assistant secretary for election integrity.
Honey tells state officials DHS had not received/requested voter data; DHS contradicts same day (officials' Nov 18, 2025 letter).
OGE answers FOIA FY26-032 ("278s, waivers, recusal documents related to Heather Honey") with a full denial under exemption (b)(3) in one day.
tl.a: Office of Government Ethics; Heather Honey (DHS)

tl.e: Honey: "Any suggestion that ICE is going to be present at polling places is simply disinformation ... There will be no ICE presence at polling locations."

Heather Honey placed as Deputy Assistant Secretary, Election Integrity (new position); ICE records title her "ICE Senior Advisor, and Deputy Assistant Secretary, Election Integrity, DHS Policy Cyber, Infrastructure, Risk, & Resilience section" (May 20, 2026) and "Senior Advisor to the ICE Director and now also S1 Counselor" (Jun 5, 2026); weekly reports credit "DAS Heather Honey" with 48.4M records "through independent sources of information" (May 25/Jun 1). Reporting: Feb 2026 she represented DHS in a federal election-resources briefing with EAC, USPIS, FBI, DOJ; Feb 2026 summit with Kurt Olsen where participants urged federal takeover; Mar 2026 met Texas SoS staff.
ICE won't be at polling places this year, a DHS official promised.

Texas SOS counsel Adam Bitter meets Heather Honey and USCIS staff; USCIS assigns incoming FDNS chief Nicolas Bartell and SAVE director Larry DeNayer to follow up; an HSI analyst obtained voter data straight from county registrars.

A PLCY Border Security & Immigration Policy senior advisor (on detail from OPLA) asks, on behalf of the "ICE Senior Advisor, and Deputy Assistant Secretary, Election Integrity, DHS Policy Cyber, Infrastructure, Risk, & Resilience section" (May 20, 2026), to add DHS staff to the weekly Voter Fraud Integrity report distribution; approved; the ICE Director's office clears and edits the report before it goes to DHS (May 27-28); a Jun 5 email names her: "Heather is a Senior Advisor to the ICE Director and now also S1 Counselor." On Jun 11 the report for the week of June 8 had not arrived; the ODD chief of staff asked "Are you asking for the Visa fraud report that HSI prepares?" and was told "The Voter Fraud Integrity" report.

HSI's May 25, 2026 weekly voter-fraud report: cases 411 -> 418, not referred 314 -> 318, administrative arrests 56 -> 64 (May 26 change summary vs May 18); a "network-based investigative approach, prioritizing organization and facilitation analysis over individual leads," now stated as strategic direction; "DOJ Dataset Intake: 50.6 million records ingested"; "DHS Dataset Intake: 48.4 million records were obtained by DAS Heather Honey through independent sources of information"; "Data Enrichment & Targeting: Datasets are currently with iLab for secondary enrichment and identification of high-value targets" (repeated in the Jun 1 report); criminal histories excluded from iLab processing for now; "Coordination with iLab continues, particularly on ingesting processed voter roll data into the ELITE enforcement system"; USCIS-derived records 25,752 -> 26,235 (a separate FDNS review line; 26,563 on Jun 1). The Jun 1 report adds that HSI searched New Jersey voter-registration NGOs "in ICM, Athena, or FinCEN" (Bates 125, 129-130). Other metrics: 2,290 records processed and 1,586 leads sent to 24 HSI field offices; top states NJ, MI, PA, MN, OH; 24,273 pending on Jun 1; the overview says the efforts "ensure the reliability of immigration and identification systems used in voter registration" and are "fully aligned with DHS and DOJ priorities." (The CNA court order gives 48.2M for the Honey-sourced records.)

In a call with Nevada (DHS official Honey present), DHS says its initial claim of ~16,000 noncitizens on Nevada's rolls was an upper bound; the result is 185 "confident," ~6,000 "higher confidence" and 14,000+ needing review; USCIS declines to give the matching fields; Nevada says it is "unable to conduct an analysis without real verifiable information." In the Aug 13 meetings Nevada also learns the 15,903 figure was not based on a full manual review, and DHS tells Pennsylvania it "did not have high confidence" in its 14,576 figure (R, DSCC complaint paras 66, 70).
Anthony Salisbury (ex-HSI Miami SAC) becomes deputy Homeland Security Adviser; ProPublica (Aug 14, 2026) calls him "deputy homeland security adviser and head of HSI" (dual role unverified).

NBC News (live blog, Nov 12): "Tony Salisbury, who previously served as deputy homeland security adviser at the White House, has been promoted to homeland security adviser, according to two administration officials and two sources familiar with an internal announcement," replacing Stephen Miller; "In his previous role, Salisbury often ensured that the Department of Homeland Security was carrying out Miller's ideas by communicating with officials and giving directives on how to carry out policies, including the targeting of foreign students, expanding immigration detention and the deportation of immigrants to Guantanamo Bay"; the role lets him "convene the National Security Council as the Homeland Security Council on certain topic areas, including immigration." (R) His OGE 278e (annual, Aug 13, 2025, via ProPublica) lists him as "Executive Associate Director, Department of Homeland Security," the title of HSI's head (D).
tl.a: Tony (Anthony W.) Salisbury; Stephen Miller; Caleb Orr; White House Homeland Security Council

tl.e: During Noem's tenure DHS refers to DOJ (a) whether barcode/QR-code vote-counting systems comply with HAVA 52 U.S.C. 21081(a)(2)(B) and (b) the legality of state MVA/voter data sharing with ERIC and CEIR under the DPPA (exact referral dates not stated).
Letter to DHS Sec. Noem asking easier state access to citizenship data in SAVE; DHS updated SAVE the next month.
tl.a: Alabama SOS Wes Allen and 20 GOP secretaries of state

tl.e: C.D. Cal. (Judge Frimpong, No. 2:25-cv-5605) issues a TRO against Los Angeles roving immigration stops; the Ninth Circuit largely denied a stay (stayed only "except as permitted by law"); the Supreme Court stayed the TRO Sept 8, 2025 (Noem v. Vasquez Perdomo, 25A169).

After the TRO, Noem calls the judge an "idiot" and says operations will not change (July 12, 2025); Bovino says his division will "go even harder" (July 17) and posts car-wash arrest videos (Aug 29, 2025).
tl.a: DHS Sec. Noem; CBP Chief Patrol Agent Bovino

tl.e: Letter to Sec. Noem regarding CISA and hacking.

DHS/USCIS final rule on USCIS law-enforcement authorities (90 FR 42797, FR Doc. 2025-16978; published Sept 5, effective Oct 6, 2025) codifies arrest, warrant and firearms authority for officers the Director designates and lets designated supervisory officials initiate criminal investigations (Delegation 15006; 8 CFR 287.2); describes FDNS as the information-sharing conduit; ICE keeps "sole responsibility" for criminal benefit-fraud investigations; MOAs "will be updated"; "DHS is not recombining USCIS and ICE." The rule does not itself say FDNS is designated law enforcement (FDNS appears only in the background section). Issued without notice and comment under the 5 U.S.C. 553(b)(A) "procedural" exception as "internal house-keeping"; DHS says it is not a CRA "rule" (5 U.S.C. 804(3)(C)) but sent it to Congress and GAO; claims no federalism implications; signed by Secretary Kristi Noem; filed Sept 4, 2025. The Director may designate individuals "or a class of individuals" to make warrantless arrests for offenses in the officer's presence and for felonies (287.5(c)), execute search warrants and serve arrest warrants (287.5(e)), carry firearms (287.5(f)(8)), and use non-deadly and deadly force and vehicular pursuit (287.8); sets "substantially equivalent" training (287.1(g)); and must issue search-and-seizure and firearms guidelines (287.9).

Supreme Court stays the July 11, 2025 TRO in C.D. Cal. 2:25-cv-5605 that had limited Los Angeles immigration stops based on four factors (apparent race/ethnicity, Spanish or accented English, location, type of work); the order is unsigned and unexplained. Kavanaugh concurrence: reasonable suspicion "means only that immigration officers may briefly stop the individual," and a citizen "will be free to go after the brief encounter"; apparent ethnicity alone cannot furnish reasonable suspicion but can be a "relevant factor" with others. Sotomayor (with Kagan, Jackson) dissents, citing "Operation At Large" (early June 2025, nearly 2,800 arrests in a month) and U.S. citizens seized.
tl.a: Supreme Court (Noem v. Vasquez Perdomo, No. 25A169)

tl.e: Benioff-Noem DHS HQ meeting (DHS photo); Salesforce 2025 ICE proposal (tip line, hiring 10k officers).

Trump posts that Democrats' threats to impeach Attorney General Blanche and to go after Republican officials and donors are "extortion at the highest level" and "Weaponization and Lawfare at another level": "By copy of this statement, I am ordering the Department of Justice to look into this criminal act, immediately!" and "The imprisonment should be against these EXTORTIONISTS, and Republicans should get smart, fast!" He names Sen. Elissa Slotkin. The post follows incoming House Oversight chair Robert Garcia's "Lawyer up" and Democrats' planned probes of ICE abuses and Trump family business dealings (Newsmax); Rep. Ramirez separately named "Noem, Markwayne, Miller, Homan, Bovino" (Fox via Yahoo). No DOJ statement that an investigation has opened; no statute named (R).

Allen signs Vice President Vance's "Pledge to Protect Americans from Fraud," citing his "fraud prevention partnership with the Department of Justice" (date approximate; the SoS feed and X post point to about Oct 19). He separately says his office "referred 25 noncitizens who illegally voted" to federal authorities.
tl.a: Alabama Secretary of State Wes Allen

tl.e: USAID IG Paul Martin fired.
Joe Gebbia reported joining DOGE (OPM retirement modernization).
Joe Gebbia appointed chief design officer; former DOGE staff (e.g., Edward Coristine) joined NDS (Reuters).

OGE closes FOIA FY26-078 in one day as "Full Denial / No Records": the request sought any OGE Form 278e or 450 filed by Gebbia, records of whether he serves "as a regular employee, Special Government Employee (18 U.S.C. § 202(a)), Intergovernmental Personnel Act Title IV detailee/assignee, or unpaid volunteer," and any 18 U.S.C. 208(b) waiver. FY26-080 ("Records related to Joe Gebbia," closed Jul 7) and FY26-079 (DOGE and National Design Studio disclosure regime, "including any determination of which regime" applies; still open) were filed the same day; FY26-119 (Sept 30) is open.
tl.a: Office of Government Ethics; Joe Gebbia (National Design Studio)

tl.e: On CNBC at the America.gov launch, Chief Design Officer Gebbia says Google Gemini and xAI Grok power America.gov ("great partners behind the scenes"); terms undisclosed; GSA runs the site with OMB and NDS; OMB can add or remove services by memo (memo due ~Dec 28); the EO says America.gov "is not intended to create a centralized federal system of records concerning individuals." At launch it answers questions and routes to agencies across 29,000+ sites as a "single point of entry" with Login.gov sign-in (OMB universal sign-on memo M-26-18, Aug 31); Medicare, passports and federal jobs are planned for 2027; the Login.gov roadmap lists "sharing fraud / threat signals," "AI-assisted user support" and a "state partner working group."
tl.a: U.S. Chief Design Officer Joe Gebbia

tl.e: Coristine on X (Oct 31): "Working at @ndstudio has been the greatest honor of my life. Yesterday was my last day"; NDS's Tai Groot: "First engineer. Then, lead engineer. Direction setting, PM-ing, and then, despite paperwork and process, writing an extremely high percentage of shipped code himself." His next role is not stated. (R)
tl.a: Edward Coristine; National Design Studio; Tai Groot; Joe Gebbia

tl.e: Antoine McCord becomes DHS CIO (Mar 2025); OBIM placed under him Aug 2025 by Homeland Security Council decision.
On HSC decision, OBIM (300M+ face/fingerprint/iris profiles, ~500,000 searches/day) placed under DHS CIO Antoine McCord, "in close contact with the Homeland Security Council."

Democracy Docket (Dec 5, 2025) reports that as a Los Angeles County deputy DA in 2022, Eric Neff brought charges against election-software company Konnech's CEO over claimed China access to poll-worker data, a case that began with information from True the Vote's Gregg Phillips; the charges were dismissed and the county paid $5 million to settle the resulting suit. Neff now helps lead DOJ's voter-roll demands.
tl.a: Eric Neff; Konnech; True the Vote (Gregg Phillips)

tl.e: Phillips: "The Department of Homeland Security now wants to partner with us"; he later took a FEMA post at DHS.

"America's AI Action Plan" (July 2025). Among its actions: OMB to "consider a state's AI regulatory climate when making funding decisions and limit funding" for states whose rules "may hinder" it; NIST to revise its AI Risk Management Framework "to eliminate references to misinformation, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion, and climate change"; federal contracts only with LLM developers whose systems are "objective and free from top-down ideological bias"; a DHS-led AI-ISAC; CISA's Cybersecurity Incident & Vulnerability Response Playbooks modified "to incorporate considerations for AI systems"; NIST-led AI incident response standards and "fly-away kits"; a cohort of High Impact Service Providers to "pilot and increase the use of AI to improve the delivery of services to the public." (D)
tl.a: White House (OSTP Michael Kratsios; David Sacks; Marco Rubio as national security adviser)

tl.e: Caleb Orr: Assistant Secretary of State for Economic and Business Affairs (confirmed 53-47 Nov 5, 2025; in office Nov 12, 2025-Aug 31, 2026), then deputy chief of staff for policy under Miller (Nov 2026). Earlier: clerk to Judge Jennifer Walker Elrod; adviser to Marco Rubio, Christopher Landau and Michael Needham; Boyden Gray PLLC research fellow (7/2022-10/2023) and associate (10/2023-8/2024), $200K, with legal-services clients including America First Legal, Alliance Defending Freedom, Philanthropy Roundtable, the American Free Enterprise Chamber of Commerce, Liberty Energy and Valero (D, OGE 278e via ProPublica); spouse at CRC Advisors (D, same); reported Project 2025 contributor (R, Newsweek via Wikipedia). (D/R)

The State Department designates four European left-wing groups in Germany, Italy and Greece as Specially Designated Global Terrorists, calling them "violent Antifa," with Foreign Terrorist Organization designations to follow; the first terrorism designations of "Antifa" groups. (R, Fox News, Deseret News, Reuters via The Star)
tl.a: State Department (Secretary Marco Rubio); four European groups

tl.e: Rubio's "Ministerial on the Resurgence of Political Terrorism" in Washington drew 65+ countries; international dimension of NSPM-7 domestic-terrorism campaign.

Delegation of Authority No. 635 (signed Sept 16, filed Nov 17, publishes Nov 18, FR 2026-23462): NED audits, NED's FOIA compliance, administration of the NED grant, and the statutory pre-program consultation are all delegated to the Under Secretary for Public Diplomacy; "The Department will therefore not view NED's consultation responsibility as having been satisfied by any communications that do not include the Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy or that Under Secretary's designee."
tl.a: Secretary of State Marco Rubio; Under Secretary of State for Public Diplomacy; National Endowment for Democracy

tl.e: Miller's first staff memo restructures the White House: "The White House will run a clear and regular policy process through the Deputy Chief of Staff for Policy" and the National Security Advisor; per the Washington Post, all West Wing policy decisions are now expected to flow through Caleb Orr (a longtime Rubio aide, promoted to deputy chief of staff for policy) or Rubio (Secretary of State and national security adviser); the National Economic Council (Hassett) and Domestic Policy Council (Haley) are not mentioned in the memo; Cabinet secretaries take over their agencies' public messaging; several Wiles aides lose power. A White House official says NEC and DPC have always been under the policy deputy. (R)
tl.a: Stephen Miller (White House chief of staff); Caleb Orr; Marco Rubio

tl.e: Leaked preliminary FY2026 State Department report to Congress proposes $888M for a U.S.-focused global health "innovation fund" (from $60M), zeroes country health aid for eight nations (South Africa -$437.1M), and plans to withhold or redirect about $605M of $607.5M Congress approved for family planning; Rubio authorized up to $125M in redirections to energy security on Sept 25. (R)

Washington Post: Katie Miller, the chief of staff's wife, has done public-affairs work for corporate clients and, over the past year, denounced ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini for liberal bias and lax security "while holding a major financial interest in a rival company, Elon Musk's xAI"; she denies being paid for posts and is not a registered lobbyist. Same story: Rubio had briefed Trump on intelligence warnings about Huang's conduct before Trump kept giving him access. (R)
tl.a: Katie Miller; xAI; Marco Rubio; Jensen Huang

tl.e: White House release "No Indication of a Cyberattack": the outages are "separate incidents caused by companies patching vulnerabilities and upgrading outdated systems." Rubio: "Companies, which is a good thing, are now immediately sharing vulnerabilities because they don't want to be accused of covering up something"; "We are not under systemic attack." Clayton: "As a result of SI and the ability to scan systems more quickly, the ability to identify vulnerabilities has increased"; patched systems are "not coming back as expected in all cases"; "it's a good news story."
Email describing Brady's role as "a possible discreet assignment" for Giuliani Ukraine material intake.
Andrew Giuliani appointed Executive Director, White House Task Force on FIFA World Cup 2026.

Scott Brady (ex-U.S. Attorney W.D. Pa.; HHS special counsel from Jan 2026) becomes executive director; in 2020 he ran DOJ's intake for Giuliani's Ukraine material (American Oversight FOIA); also ran 2020 COVID fraud task force with Josh Shapiro; employing agency, charter and records status unknown.

World Cup security: FBI joint operations centers in each host city on match days; FEMA $625M to 11 host cities plus $250M counter-drone; "thousands of AI-powered cameras"; Gillette Stadium opt-in face-to-wallet entry; Seattle linked stadium CCTV and ALPRs to a Real-Time Crime Center; ICE said agents would play a "key part."
tl.a: FBI / FEMA / White House FIFA Task Force (Giuliani)

tl.e: NYT (Haberman and Swan, Jun 15, 2026) reports White House staff secretary Will Scharf's confidential Apr 29, 2025 memo to Chief of Staff Wiles, subject "THE WRIT OF HABEAS CORPUS," warning against Stephen Miller's push to have Trump claim the power to suspend habeas for undocumented immigrants; Scharf wrote a second memo against invoking the Insurrection Act to deploy the military as protests grew. A senior official says "senior staff" requested the memos.
tl.a: Will Scharf; Stephen Miller; Susie Wiles

tl.e: HSC reviews all DHS biometrics programs; OBIM placed under DHS CIO (DOGE consulted).
HSC begins review of "all biometrics programs"; DOGE extends operations to DHS biometrics office (OBIM) and consulted on replacement system.

CBS: about 20 target and preservation letters so far; Elias a target; the DSCC received a grand-jury subpoena; the probe is led by the Alaska U.S. Attorney's Office with Civil Rights Division criminal-section prosecutors (acting chief Brandon Wrobleski has sought to recruit Alaska AUSAs, some declined); federal prosecutors have not named the crimes. AP: more than 100 subpoenas so far. Stephen Miller on Fox suggested 18 U.S.C. 241 could apply (CBS). U.S. Attorney Heyman: "We're not escalating anything except to the extent that a new article came out."
tl.a: DOJ (USAO Alaska, Civil Rights Division criminal section); Stephen Miller

tl.e: Trump announces Stephen Miller will become White House chief of staff "starting Monday, November 9, 2026," replacing Susie Wiles. Miller: "Fight with all of our soul to support our President." (R)

Blanche says DOJ may investigate congressional Democrats after Trump's Nov 7 order but names no crime: "Well, it depends on what's said"; "So yes, there could be… when the threats become so vile and so dangerous"; "They are not allowed to just go around threatening existing members of the administration"; "If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer." On Fox: "If you work in this administration, you have a lawyer ... It's me." (NYT, Nov 11, quotes him on TV: "Stephen Miller has a lawyer. It's me. It's me and the entire Department of Justice.") No investigation announced. (R)
tl.a: Attorney General Blanche (CNN State of the Union; Fox)

tl.e: NYT (Thrush, Feuer): Singh told U.S. attorneys "We are now a wartime department"; the "Four Guys" (Blanche, Trent McCotter, Stanley Woodward Jr., Singh) oversaw and, in many instances, signed filings including the failed bid to block certification of the Alaska Senate race; Blanche on TV: "Stephen Miller has a lawyer. It's me. It's me and the entire Department of Justice." A D.C. grand jury earlier refused to indict six lawmakers at Trump's demand.

CNN investigation: the administration acted as "a friendly partner" in more than a dozen AFL lawsuits, "roughly 40% of AFL's caseload" in the second term; Hamilton (DOJ chapter author for Project 2025) was deputy White House counsel for five months, then returned as AFL president; Rubinstein was State's top lawyer while his own AFL suit was pending and is back as AFL senior vice president; AFL's D.C. filings listed Hamilton as sole "beneficial owner" in Jan 2026. CNN found no evidence recusal or lobbying rules were broken.
tl.a: America First Legal (Gene Hamilton, Reed Rubinstein, Daniel Epstein); Stephen Miller

tl.e: Miller's second memo bars White House staff from meeting registered lobbyists on the White House complex without prior approval from the counsel's office; the Office of Public Liaison, which handles business ties, is exempt. It follows Calley Means's accusation that Wiles's team accommodated sugar, tobacco, pesticide and food interests. (R)
tl.a: Stephen Miller; White House Counsel's office; Office of Public Liaison

tl.e: NYT (Broadwater, Kanno-Youngs, Barrett, Nov 14): the administration plans "an all-out effort" against Democratic oversight, "threatening to treat some legislative oversight as a potential crime"; DOJ OLC "over the summer quietly published an opinion asserting that even communications by those outside government could be covered by executive privilege" if they concern Trump and top aides; former Jordan staffer Rachel Jag coordinates DOJ's response to subpoenas; Blanche says DOJ leaders "had been working with Mr. Reitz"; Scharf: "I meant everything I said," and he and others are "collecting examples" of lawmakers' statements. Warren, Garcia and Blumenthal opened an inquiry into fund-raiser Meredith O'Rourke (Nov 12).
tl.a: White House (chief of staff Stephen Miller; counsel William Scharf); DOJ (OLC; Rachel Jag); AG Todd Blanche

tl.e: May Mailman, who helped Miller draft executive orders in the 2024-25 transition and oversaw the lawsuits against Ivy League universities, has temporarily returned to the West Wing and is compiling a list of "wins" for Trump's final two years, many "designed to come from executive orders," plus foreign policy; Miller's aides are drafting a Venezuela executive order to ease business for energy, financial services and critical-minerals companies; trade actions by executive authority are expected. A former official on Miller: "Sometimes he comes up with novel interpretations, like the old saying, 'If your lawyer tells you something isn't legal, you find a different lawyer.'" (R)

Reitz posts a preservation letter to Sen.
