Warren, the third to a senator in a week after Blumenthal and Slotkin, citing 18 U.S.C. 241 and 242 over her planned probe of Trump associates, including fundraiser Meredith O'Rourke; she has until Nov 23 to confirm she "has preserved the material he requested." On X: "My first arrow shot." Miller reposts it: "18 USC 241 and 242."
tl.a: U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz (S.D. Tex.); Sen. Elizabeth Warren; White House chief of staff Stephen Miller

tl.e: Garcia sends preservation letters to a dozen Trump allies, including Stephen Miller and JD Vance, and to Trump family business interests; House Judiciary and Foreign Affairs Democrats ask Cantor Fitzgerald to preserve Nvidia records in a Lutnick probe. (R, headlines: Forbes, Washington Post, WIRED, Politico, Reuters)
tl.a: Rep. Robert Garcia (incoming House Oversight chair); Stephen Miller; JD Vance

Judge Carter holds the first, 3-hour hearing on DOJ's bid to hold about 20,000 California ballots and issues no TRO at the hearing (minutes: application "taken under submission," written order to issue, Dkt 146, entered Oct 28). Per the written order (D): "The government reiterated its threat in open court ... that State and County election officials who do not comply with their letter risk federal charges under 18 U.S.C. 2" (aiding and abetting), and the Court said "these threats must stop" (ECF 149 p.7). tl.a: Judge David Carter, C.D. Cal. (US v. California 2:26-cv-12025)

tl.e: Judge Carter DENIES DOJ's TRO application (Dkt 62) to make California and Los Angeles County segregate and not count the vote-by-mail ballots of ~20,000 people on the "October List" (ECF 149, 26 pp.). Holdings at the likelihood-of-success stage, not final merits: (1) the U.S. likely lacks Article III standing no "interference" with 18 U.S.C. 611 enforcement (DOJ is actively charging people; refusing to help is not impeding, US v. California, 921 F.3d 865), it cannot "spend its way into standing," and vote dilution is too speculative (Clapper, Lake v. Fontes); (2) no cause of action the Supremacy Clause creates none (Armstrong) and there is no equitable tradition of commandeering state election officials; (3) Section 611 does not preempt California election law no conflict, the Elections Clause leaves procedure to the states absent a clear congressional statement (Gregory v. Ashcroft; ITCA), and the theory raises Tenth Amendment anti-commandeering problems; (4) the relief would likely violate the NVRA 90-day bar (the October List is a "systematic" program like the data-match in Mi Familia Vota v. Fontes; "temporary segregation" has the same effect as removal: "a ballot segregated, in effect, would be a ballot removed," because neither DOJ which admits it cannot verify before Election Day, Compl. para 60 nor the counties can verify), VRA 52 U.S.C. 10307(a), and the Civil Rights Act materiality/different-standards provision 52 U.S.C. 10101(a)(2)(A) (procedure applied only to listed voters; A-number matching cannot reach U.S.-born citizens); (5) no irreparable harm the emergency is "solely due to its own neglect" (roll in hand May 8, Weber notified Jul 16, suit Oct 15); (6) equities: "the Court cannot conclude that Plaintiff's process is credible"; (7) Purcell bars relief; (8) the public interest favors voting rights and election staff. Disposition: "DENIES the Application" (p.26). The order appoints no special master and sets no hearing date, no PI schedule and no ruling on the motions to dismiss. DOJ files a notice of appeal of ECF 149 the same day (ECF 152). A CBS headline the same day read "Court dismisses DOJ's request" (the order is a TRO denial; the case stays open).
tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal. (United States v. California, No. 2:26-cv-12025)

tl.e: Carter finds DOJ's list process not credible: DOJ withheld matching rules, confidence-threshold criteria and third-party details, disclosed LexisNexis only the night before the hearing, never explained the HSI "enrichment process," gave no error rates or benchmark validation, and never explained how ~190,000 became ~20,000; with Nevada's 15,903 -> 6,218 -> 185 -> zero record, "the Court cannot conclude that Plaintiff's process is credible." It also relies on the USCIS whistleblower report (County Opp. Ex. H: quota of 5/hour, 40/day, "only twelve minutes" per subject, IDs based "solely on DHS data that is unverified") and finds naturalized citizens most at risk.
tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal.

tl.e: Carter credits LA County declarations that its system "ha[s] no function for setting aside the ballots of designated voters" and that segregation would need changes to "multiple, separate software programs and hardware devices" that "cannot be completed safely and uniformly before Election Day" (Flores Decl. para 43; Bhullar Decl. paras 11, 15).
tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal.

tl.a: Judge David O. Carter, C.D. Cal.

tl.e: U.S. v. California, 2:26-cv-12025, ECF 181, order closing case: "This lawsuit attempted to disrupt an ongoing election and create confusion and uncertainty for voters and election workers alike. The right to vote is sacred. So, too, is trust in our democracy." The Nov 13 hearing on "the validity of the government's list" is moot and vacated. (D)

DHS publishes modified SORN DHS/USCIS-004 SAVE (90 FR 48948-48955, FR Doc. 2025-19735, docket USCIS-2025-0337): adds U.S. citizens by birth; adds full/truncated SSN, U.S. passport number, driver's-license number and SSA-supplied data; adds record sources SSA-60-0058 (Numident), State STATE-05/-26/-39 and driver's-license agencies such as NLETS (DL search "not live at the time of publication"); clarifies voter verification and says it is "reinserting voter registration that was previously published in 76 FR 58525" as an administrative clarification; SSN case creation and the list processor were limited at first to web-browser users, and the list processor creates individual cases ("this is not batch processing"); a new oversight account type may view other user agencies' case data linked "by benefit type ... or by state"; new routine uses L (SSA and other authorized entities) and M (oversight/auditing) effective Dec 1, 2025; keeps routine use G (disclosure to law-enforcement agencies investigating violations of law) while stating SAVE information "is not to be used for administrative (non-criminal) immigration enforcement purposes." Prior version 85 FR 31798 (May 27, 2020); comments due Dec 1, 2025 (the SORN gives no comment count; the "9,361" in earlier notes needs a docket cite, U); exemptions "None." SSA published its companion Numident SORN modification Nov 12, 2025 (90 FR 50879; effective Dec 12, 2025).

SSA modifies Numident SORN 60-0058 (90 FR 50879, FR Doc 2025-19849, docket SSA-2025-0225; applicable on publication Nov 12, 2025; new routine uses effective Dec 12, 2025, comments invited to Dec 12): new routine use 49 lets SSA give DHS "the citizenship and immigration status, lawful or unlawful, of any individual pursuant to 8 U.S.C. 1373(a)" with no agreement, purpose or volume limit written into it; new routine use 50 to Treasury Do Not Pay; existing routine use 2 deleted; signed by Matthew Ramsey (Head of Privacy and Disclosure Policy). The notice never names SAVE or voter verification except existing routine use 36 (HAVA SSN-4 checks for chief election officials). The SORN states no comment count (an earlier "21,298 comments" figure is unsupported, U).

Emmer told Newsmax DOJ is reviewing "four different things," including her age at derivative citizenship. The paper cites a 2025 DOJ memo widening denaturalization to anyone posing an "ongoing threat"; no time limit on civil denaturalization. Omar's office: "an abusive fishing expedition driven by the president's political vendettas." Unsealing hearing Nov 17 (D.D.C. 1:26-mc-00144).

Joint status report in NAACP v. Dhillon (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03461, ECF 28), the FOIA suit over DOJ's election monitors. DOJ quotes the Neff declaration ¶6: "while monitoring, the monitors will not be acting as 'law enforcement personnel,' a 'law enforcement officer,' or a 'law enforcement agent' as commonly understood." DOJ says it "has not yet finished identifying all locations for deploying monitors," will not commit to a date before Election Day, and that publishing them could put monitors at risk. NAACP says DOJ counsel conceded criminal prosecutors and investigators from DOJ criminal components and U.S. Attorneys' offices will serve; that the declaration names DEA, BOP and ATF personnel without the "no agents" language used for the FBI and ICE, and does not mention the U.S. Marshals; and that an ATF employee is among the monitors. DOJ's searches returned 18,993 and 7,842 potentially responsive records; it says none can be produced before Nov 3.

The release describes the Criminal Section as enforcing statutes against "voter intimidation and voter suppression based on race, color, national origin, or religion," and tells the public to report violence or intimidation to local police first. It lists the counties and cities (e.g., Texas: Bexar, Dallas, Harris, Waller, Blanco, Bowie, Nueces; Georgia: Cobb, DeKalb, Fulton, Gwinnett, Chatham, Bibb; Michigan: Lansing, E. Lansing, Grand Rapids, Flint, Detroit, Hamtramck, Warren, Dearborn).

Lawyers Defending American Democracy files a professional-ethics complaint against Dhillon, acting Deputy Assistant AG Robert Keenan and acting Voting Section chief Eric Neff, alleging they kept pursuing the voter-roll suits against 30 states and D.C. after courts "repeatedly rejected" the theory (LDAD: DOJ had lost all 27 cases ruled on as of Oct 23). The complaint quotes Neff telling a Rhode Island court DOJ would run the records against DHS's SAVE.
tl.a: Lawyers Defending American Democracy; Harmeet Dhillon; Robert Keenan; Eric Neff

tl.e: LDAD files an ethics complaint with the State Bar of California against Dhillon, Keenan and Neff over DOJ's voter-record suits, alleging claims that are "frivolous, involve legal and factual misrepresentations, and undermine public confidence in our elections" (allegations).
tl.a: Lawyers Defending American Democracy; Harmeet Dhillon, Robert Keenan, Eric Neff (DOJ Civil Rights Division)

tl.e: Craig Trainor, HUD's fair-housing assistant secretary and a former AFPI staffer, is tapped as acting Assistant Attorney General for Civil Rights, replacing Harmeet Dhillon, according to an administration official. (R)

OPLA legal broadcast "Preserving and Protecting the Integrity of American Elections" (Dec 29, 2025, 5:56 PM, to OPLA Regional and Division personnel): "ICE has begun coordinating with CBP, USCIS, and the Department of Justice" to identify aliens who registered or voted; noncitizens who voted can be removed without conviction and without proof they knew it was illegal, including where the evidence is "insufficient to support a criminal prosecution."
tl.a: ICE OPLA (Deputy PLA Adam V. Loiacono; Acting Deputy PLA Nelson Perez)

tl.e: Sessions introduces bipartisan Stop Identity Fraud and Identity Theft Act to 'strengthen the Nation's digital identity verification infrastructure' (bill number not given).

House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations holds "Emerging Fraud Threats and the Evolving Fraud Landscape" (Serial No. 119-70; Sessions chair; 2:03-3:58 p.m.; most majority members absent for an Administration Middle East briefing). Witnesses: Jordan Burris (Socure Vice President and Head of Public Sector Strategy; former Chief of Staff, White House Office of the Federal CIO), Marisol Cruz Cain (GAO IT & Cybersecurity), David Maimon (SentiLink, Georgia State) and Jay Stanley (ACLU, minority witness). Burris says "identity should be considered critical infrastructure" and that Socure is a Login.gov vendor after competing against 17 others (document verification, facial biometric comparison, device and fraud models); Sessions proposes that Login.gov identity-verification failures (who failed, where, how) be studied and moved "to the organization we talked about this morning, to Pandemic Response Accountability Committee (PRAC)," says Congress will make PRAC's data effort permanent, and asks whether it is "fair game to go back and run people back through" benefit programs because "a lot of people that presently are receiving government benefits might not be exactly as we thought they were," and whether AI flags (e.g., "74 people at your home address") can trigger review. Rep. Randall enters the Wired article "A DOGE Affiliate Is Now in Charge of the US Government ID Platform"; Ranking Member Mfume says DOGE used an SSA identity database to mark people. GAO: Login.gov meets NIST IAL2 after a remote identity-proofing pilot, agencies lack visibility into why users fail, 100M+ users, 50+ agencies, 500 applications incl. state and local. Industry witnesses (SentiLink, Socure) urge "real-time cross-agency data matching," holding payments via an expanded Do Not Pay, continuous identity re-verification and "historical signals" from commercial data.
tl.a: House Oversight Subcommittee on Government Operations

tl.e: FEC Form 13: HPE gave the Trump Vance Inaugural Committee $250,000 on Jan 23, 2025, a week before DOJ sued to block its Juniper purchase. The same report lists Verizon ($1,000,000, Dec 19, 2024), AT&T ($1,000,000) and IBM ($750,000). (D)
tl.a: Hewlett Packard Enterprise; Verizon; AT&T; IBM; Trump Vance Inaugural Committee

tl.e: Ueland's nominee financial disclosure (OGE 278e, signed Mar 18, 2025): Ueland Consulting LLC, President/CEO since 3/2021, $570,420 in consulting fees; sources paying more than $5,000 for his services: American Hospital Association, APTS, Humana Health, Commonwealth Fund, the Heritage Foundation and the America First Policy Institute. Heritage Foundation Visiting Fellow 3/2023-12/2024 ($55,000 fellowship income to the LLC); volunteer, Trump Vance 2025 Transition, Inc. 11/2024-1/2025; advisory board, Center for Constitutional Liberty, Benedictine College 7/2022-1/2025; USCIRF commissioner 5/2022-1/2025.
tl.a: Eric Ueland (OMB nominee, Deputy Director for Management)

tl.e: Vance: "We have activated a major interagency task force" on fraud, two months before the order that formally creates it; at the same briefing he says DOJ will create a new associate attorney general position dedicated to fraud and cites 1,500 subpoenas and 100 indictments.
Vance, as fraud task-force chair, refers Minnesota Gov. Walz and AG Ellison to DOJ's fraud division (post Monday night, Jun 8, 2026; reported Jun 9); outcome unknown.

Daily Beast and CNN: Vance is leasing part of Wolver Hill, a $9 million Middleburg, Va., estate owned through Wolver Hill LLC by data-center developer Chuck Kuhn, and is reportedly eyeing a purchase; lease terms are undisclosed. Vance's June 2026 278e also showed $250,001-$500,000 in Bitcoin.
tl.a: JD Vance; Charles "Chuck" Kuhn (JK Moving; data centers)

tl.e: Task-force press conference on visa fraud; green-card program suspensions and nine university investigations.

Headline (Carolina Coast Online): "Boliek signs Vance fraud pledge, expands NC watchdog efforts." Boliek already sits in DOJ's Southeast Fraud Enforcement Partnership (Jul 30) and his office took a $1.9M Special Attorneys award.
tl.a: North Carolina State Auditor Dave Boliek

tl.e: NSA names Tim Kosiba (ex-TAO requirements & targeting) deputy director.

Richfield, MN observer Nicole Cleland is addressed by name by an agent who cites facial recognition (Jan 10); her Global Entry/TSA PreCheck is revoked Jan 13 (reason as quoted in project notes not confirmed in KSTP; agency per KSTP).

A DOJ privacy lawyer tries to narrow voter-roll sharing to specific individuals (Feb 12, 2026 warning that raw voter data to DHS carries "far too much unnecessary legal risk"); a Mar 4 draft still allows transfer; the final, short DOJ-DHS letter, signed by the acting ICE director about two days later, is broader and drops the proposed party-affiliation redaction.

Per a USCIS whistleblower disclosure released by Sens. Padilla and Schumer (packet ~37 pp; Democracy Defenders Fund cover letter Sept 8): on Aug 21 FDNS officers are told to "stop everything" and watch a 1h45m training ("there will be U.S. citizens in this population"); Aug 24 FDNS is reorganized under HQ control; Aug 25 reviews begin, target Sept 12; quota 5 an hour, 40 a day (~12 minutes each), "up to hundreds of thousands" across 50 states. Inputs: state voter-lookup websites (an internal site links all 50 state portals; VA, FL and Massachusetts flagged "(Attestation)," i.e. users attest to being the voter allegation, R), SAVE (source label "IRIS"; other labels "DOJDHS," "ICE"), Accurint and Thomson Reuters CLEAR, and SSA and State passport data in batch queries; officers are told to create TECS records on "unlawful voters" that can trigger HSI referral; agency counsel called the searches "open-source research."

Bipartisan amicus brief (199 House, 47 Senate, 15 former House members; Schumer and Jeffries listed; no party affiliations given) in No. 26A305 (USPS v. California; Trump v. League of Women Voters of Massachusetts) urges the Supreme Court to deny a stay of the D. Mass. injunction against the USPS mail-ballot Final Rule: the Elections and Postal Clauses give the Executive no power; no statute delegates it; the Rule conflicts with HAVA, NVRA, UOCAVA and Title 39. Filing day not on the copy read (stay denied Sept 14).
tl.a: 261 current and former members of Congress

tl.e: Officers must create a TECS record on anyone judged an "unlawful voter," 40 reviews/day quota; warned "there will be U.S. citizens in this population." USCIS: its criminal unit "was not directly involved" (D, declaration).
tl.a: USCIS whistleblower (via Sens. Padilla/Schumer, posted Sept 13-14)

tl.e: Press conference demanding DHS stop; cites whistleblower claims of daily case quotas.
Two suits seek to keep armed federal agents away from polls: one led by the NAACP (Sept 18) and one by the DSCC, DCCC, DGA, Schumer and Jeffries against DHS, ICE and the FBI (Sept 23)
Polling Place Policy suit vs DHS, ICE, FBI (armed agents at polls, VRA 11(b), APA); separate NAACP-led suit Sept 18.

DSCC v. Trump, D.D.C. 1:26-cv-3674 (filed Oct 20, 2026 by Schumer, Jeffries, DSCC, DCCC, DGA and Nevada Democrats): Elections Clause, separation of powers, anti-commandeering, VRA §11(b); DOJ's roll push began summer 2025; 27 courts dismissed DOJ roll suits; portal "imminent." DOJ says "election integrity is a top priority"; the White House calls it "decisive lawful action" (Axios Oct 21, R).
tl.a: Schumer, Jeffries, DSCC, DCCC, DGA, NV Dems

tl.e: DOJ tells the court its letters to states about alleged noncitizen voters "have no independent legal effect" and "do not themselves change any voter's registration status, withhold a ballot, or alter ballot tabulation"; argues plaintiffs lack standing.

Colom leads Hyde-Smith by 1,138 late Nov 4 with nearly 3,600 mail ballots outstanding and, per unconfirmed reports, upwards of 18,000 affidavit ballots statewide still to be cured (cure deadline Nov 10; counties certify Nov 13); Schumer reportedly sending DSCC legal resources (R).
Ordered four Virginia state agencies (State Police, Corrections) to terminate 287(g) agreements; on Jan 17 rescinded Youngkin EO; 22 sheriffs still participate.

Treasury publishes a Notice of Proposed Designation (91 FR 5990, Feb 10, 2026, FR Doc. 2026-02630, docket TREAS-DO-2026-0034; signed Gary Grippo, Acting Fiscal Assistant Secretary) to add SSA's Numident to the Do Not Pay Working System: Numident "will be used solely for the purpose of verifying the name, SSN, and date of birth" of people receiving federally funded payments or awards under health or income maintenance programs (e.g., Social Security retirement, Medicare, Medicaid, including federally funded state-administered programs); SSA returns only numerical match codes, not other Numident data; SSA discloses under routine use 17 of SORN 60-0058 (90 FR 50879, Nov 12, 2025); comments due Feb 25, 2026; a final designation would be a separate Federal Register notice (whether it was issued: U). Do Not Pay system access uses PIV credentials, Login.gov and ID.me; Do Not Pay estimates $1.5-4.5 billion a year in at-risk payments addressed.
William Kirk appointed PRAC chair (from Mar 1, 2026, succeeding Horowitz).
SBA IG William Kirk (political appointee) became PRAC chair, succeeding Michael Horowitz; he holds SBA IG, PRAC chair and SBA PRAC seat.

SBA OIG Management Advisory Report 26-15 (Sept 24, 2026, IG Kirk to Administrator Loeffler; review period Apr 3, 2025-Apr 30, 2026) finds a fraud-detection AI pilot missing from SBA's public AI inventory: it targets PPP, EIDL, RRF, SVOG and disaster loans plus 8(a) contracts "and the awarding contracting officer for indications of possible collusion"; SBA managers said it "did not qualify as high impact, even though the model would be potentially flagging loans as fraudulent" (OMB presumes such fraud detection high impact); 34 inventoried uses, 19 with PII, none designated high impact; report cites SBA release 26-29 suspending 111,620 California borrowers (Feb 6, 2026); SBA (Deputy CIO, Sept 15) agrees to all six recommendations with Sept 30, 2026 targets.
tl.a: SBA OIG (IG William W. Kirk, also PRAC chair)

tl.e: Hearing on major-event information sharing: NFCA's Mike Sena describes a Super Bowl LX info-sharing environment "that combined... a common public safety Geographic Information System (GIS) analysis tool with a commonly used chat, video, and file sharing technology"; federal DHS/FBI systems "not fully interoperable with state and local platforms"; Sena opposes the Fourth Amendment Is Not For Sale Act.

Horowitz: losing PACE would cost oversight "an invaluable resource"; Dodaro: permanent center "would be ready and there when emergencies occur"; GAO-22-105715 recommended a permanent analytics center.

Blanche's memo "Ending Regulation by Prosecution" disbands DOJ's National Cryptocurrency Enforcement Team "effective immediately" while his disclosure listed roughly $160,000-$485,000 in crypto assets he had agreed to divest; he divested weeks later, largely by gifts to adult children and a grandchild. Campaign Legal Center filed a DOJ IG complaint (Jan 2026); six senators wrote "you should have recused yourself." DOJ says the orders were "appropriately flagged, addressed and cleared in advance."
Blanche at CPAC: "Why is there an objection to sending ICE to polling stations?"

Acting AG memo "Creation of the National Fraud Enforcement Division" (Apr 7, 2026): creates NFED and an NFDC "dedicated to identifying fraud across taxpayer-funded programs"; within 14 days the Criminal Division and EOUSA report ongoing investigations and "significant events ... expected to occur within the next 90 days" (complaints, indictments, pleas, trials, sentencings); each U.S. Attorney's Office details a prosecutor to NFED within 21 days; partners include EO 14395 task-force members; grants to "enable state and local prosecutors"; the memo does not mention elections.
DOJ anti-fraud press conference: "elected officials need to support the Justice Department in stopping this fraud."

Trump v. IRS settlement creates $1.776B "anti-weaponization" fund (May 18); Blanche says DOJ not moving forward (Jun 1-2); Judge Brinkema blocks fund indefinitely (Jun 12); Judge Williams voids settlement as collusive (~Jul).
20+ senators ask Blanche why the Election Crimes Manual was removed

Sen. Schmitt and five other Republican senators write Acting AG Blanche and AAG McDonald (DOJ fraud leadership) asking, by Aug 24, 2026, for the "Status of voter-roll cleanups, specific election-fraud prosecutions, immigration-related fraud schemes," state coordination on removing ineligible voters, federal-state information-sharing barriers, sanctuary jurisdictions, and proposals to make the National Fraud Enforcement Division permanent with "enhanced data-sharing."

At his Senate confirmation hearing, asked by Sen. John Kennedy about his relationship with Trump, Blanche says "I'm his lawyer," then corrects himself to "was his lawyer"; says Trump never asked him to do anything illegal and he "Absolutely not" would if asked. Confirmed 50-49 in August (Newsweek, Aug 16).
Letters (Aug 19, Aug 27, Sept 1) to AG Blanche on DOJ plan to deploy up to 1,000 election monitors; Wyoming GOP officials raised alarms over "aggressive" monitors in August primary.

Wall Street Journal: Pulte "also looked at" the mortgage records of Todd Blanche, then deputy attorney general, after they clashed over the mortgage cases; sources say Pulte was "trying to collect information on Blanche and others." Pulte's lawyer calls that false; DOJ says Blanche has one mortgage. (R)

Sens. Padilla, Durbin and Whitehouse ask AG Blanche (cc FBI Director Patel) to pledge DOJ will not seize ballots, materials or voting equipment before certification and to disclose any seizure plans (answer due Oct 29); Padilla separately secured FBI Director Patel's commitment that the FBI will not seize ballots or machines ahead of the midterms.
NAACP v. Blanche, 1:26-cv-03626, challenges deployment of criminal prosecutors and law-enforcement personnel as election monitors.
AG Blanche won't rule out DOJ intervening in state certification in "some doomsday scenario," while saying he is "not trying to not have an election certified." A statement, not an action
Blanche says lawsuits against other states like the California ballot suit could follow

AG Blanche (CBS Face the Nation; CNN State of the Union, Oct 25): the Alaska suit is "guardrails" and "not saying don't certify," but if a court finds a result "decided because of confusion and not the will of the voters," "we do not think the states should certify"; DOJ wants a procedure "if there is litigation brought by others after the election" and is "doing our own research"; he won't discuss communications with the President; on CNN: "Oh, stop it!... We're not laying any groundwork." (Headlines that "there could be a crime" are unverified.)

Written answer due to Sens. Padilla, Durbin and Whitehouse on committing not to remove ballots, materials or equipment from state custody before certification; no public answer reported as of Oct 30 morning.

In NAACP v. Blanche (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03626-RBW, ECF 22, Nov 2), Judge Walton denies the TRO on DOJ poll monitors without prejudice (finding "a reasonable voter would not be intimidated" by plain-clothes non-law-enforcement volunteers, and that his view "would differ" if DOJ planned to send officers with arrest authority) but orders DOJ to comply with its counsel's concession that monitors "are indeed administrative or clerical personnel and not law enforcement officials, will not be in uniform or display any other insignia ... will not be armed with a firearm, and will not have the power to effectuate arrests," plus the Neff Decl. ¶12 limits (business casual; no visible federal insignia; "not talk with any voter inside the polling place"; talk to voters outside only after they vote; carry credentials). Plaintiffs may file a notice of any Nov 3 violation and the court "will take immediate action." DOJ status report due 7:00 a.m. Nov 3 on how it confirmed no monitor is a law enforcement official with arrest power.

DOJ status report in NAACP v. Blanche (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03626-RBW, ECF 24, filed Nov 3) under Walton's order: "Though there is no prohibition on the use of sworn law enforcement officers as civil rights election monitors, CRT undertook reasonable efforts to avoid using sworn officers"; FBI and DHS personnel excluded; after weeks of consultation "DEA prohibited sworn officers from serving as election monitors"; review with ATF and U.S. Marshals leadership "resulted in the removal of several sworn law enforcement officers from the volunteer monitoring pool"; Bureau of Prisons employees, who "have legal authority to make limited arrests" (18 U.S.C. 3050), remain, because "It is inconceivable that anything could happen at a polling place where a BOP employee serving in a monitoring capacity would be authorized to make an arrest"; "No additional sworn law enforcement officers were identified" on Nov 2.
tl.a: DOJ (Civil Division for CRT); D.D.C. (Judge Walton)

tl.e: On Fox News (MacCallum), on Alaska: "There's a scenario where the incumbent, Senator Sullivan, could lose"; "If it's clear that voters were confused, and again, that's why you need to preserve these ballots"; authorities could "look at the individual ballots."

Watson statement: about 3,600 mail ballots left plus an "unknown" number of affidavit ballots; "Counties have 10 days from the date of the election to submit their certified results to our office, which is November 13." AP (Wed night, 96%): Colom leads Hyde-Smith by 1,138. Alaska: Peltola leads Dan Sullivan by 637 with nearly a quarter uncounted; ranked-choice tabulation Nov 18 (R, Al Jazeera/AP Nov 5). Democracy Docket: if Hyde-Smith loses narrowly the GOP "will likely mount a legal effort to challenge ballots" and DOJ "could be joined"; Blanche vows to keep "fighting tooth and nail" on Alaska (R).
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State Watson; Alaska Division of Elections

tl.e: Washington Post: DOJ braces for congressional subpoenas after the Democratic sweep (likely topics: the Trump IRS settlement, Epstein files, pardons, the Comey prosecution); the story cites an OLC executive-privilege opinion released earlier this year. Blanche on Fox: "It's so disgusting to see them not even wait before the week is out." (R)

At Jackson City Hall, across from the Hinds County Courthouse where Mississippi affidavit voters had to cure by 5 p.m. Nov 10, Blanche, Gov. Reeves, AG Fitch and U.S. Marshals Director Serralta announce more than $63M for Jackson under DOJ's Model Cities Initiative (one of four cities; ~$300M total), including a "Real-Time Public Safety Center" and a "Sky-to-Street Public Safety Network utilizing unmanned aircraft systems." Blanche: "The Model Cities Initiative reflects the Trump Administration's commitment to reducing crime across the country." The release does not mention the election. Demonstrators said the visit, with a large police escort, could deter voters from curing (R, Democracy Docket). The same day Blanche announced St. Louis as another Model Cities recipient (D, DOJ Attorney General news alert, Nov 9), so the Jackson stop was one leg of a grant tour. (D)

Blanche on Fox, the third time in two days: "We cannot let the rhetoric turn from just honest debate to actual criminal conduct"; "There's been so much vile rhetoric coming out of the incoming congressmen and senators, and also from organizations that are outside"; "you cannot threaten." Sen. Slotkin's lawyer Preet Bharara answers that her statement "is entirely lawful." Same Fox & Friends appearance: Blanche says his role is "to defend the administration" (The New Republic). (R)
Bloomberg Law: Singh urges U.S. attorneys onto a "wartime footing," warns of more removals, and asks each office to name 2-3 AUSAs who can move to priority cases in other districts.

At a DOJ press conference: "there's no ongoing investigations, criminal investigations into words that incoming senators or congressmen have said"; "I never said that that point has been crossed"; did not say whether DOJ headquarters approved Reitz's letter ("I don't oversee every single thing that's done"). Same event, per NPR: "We are actively, and will continue to investigate election integrity cases criminally and civilly, and that wasn't expected to start or stop — no matter what the results of the election were last week." DOJ has not rescinded the California grand-jury subpoenas.

Breitbart and The Western Journal report Attorney General Blanche is the latest cabinet official moved onto a military base; The Times counts four cabinet members living on bases amid Iranian threats.

Incoming Democrats are "acting like prosecutors ... They're acting like they're going to cut subpoenas left and right"; "We're going to be there, and we're not going to just stand by willingly." Per Tampa Free Press, Blanche said the administration has been reaching out to private companies and supporters, advising them not to fold under congressional pressure, and alleged outside legal groups are working with incoming House Democrats to target officials including the chief of staff.
tl.a: Attorney General Todd Blanche (Fox, Life, Liberty & Levin)

tl.e: Joint DOJ-Commerce statement on the Megaspeed investigation (press release 26-1365): Commerce opened the probe in 2024; in May 2025 investigators asked Nvidia for records; in June 2025 Nvidia put Megaspeed on its "no sell" list and BIS agents, with Singaporean officials, did an end-use check and interviewed CEO Alice Huang; DOJ then took the criminal lead. "While we don't typically comment on ongoing investigations, it is in the public interest to provide the facts and address inaccurate information circulating in public reporting." Credits "the Department of Commerce under Secretary Howard Lutnick."
tl.a: Department of Commerce; Department of Justice; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; Attorney General Todd Blanche

tl.e: Juneau Independent (Mark Sabbatini): Peltola's win "won't halt a U.S. Department of Justice lawsuit and criminal investigation of her campaign, according to Trump administration officials and media reports"; the probe rests on "allegations Peltola's campaign and Democratic party officials recruited spoiler candidates"; "Peltola and other accused have denied such efforts"; Blanche, last week: "the priority of investigating a criminal potential fraud doesn't stop because of the election, no matter who wins or loses," and a DOJ spokesperson told the Washington Post the department stands by it. Newsweek (Lars Hanson): more than 200 subpoenas (Fox), the probe "reaches into several states" with "more than one criminal target"; target letters went to several people including Marc Elias, whose firm represents Peltola's campaign; "The Justice Department has not publicly identified its targets or the federal laws it believes may have been broken"; Alaska attorney David R. Weber asked Judge Gleason to sanction three DOJ lawyers who brought the certification suit, including U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman; DOJ's Ninth Circuit response on summary affirmance is due Thursday; the Alaska Bureau of Investigation "continues to investigate allegations related to the Alaska US Senate election." Fox News (Peter D'Abrosca), the source of the subpoena count, frames it as "its criminal investigation into Dan J. Sullivan," with "multiple criminal targets" across "multiple states" per a law enforcement source, and says the NYT reported Peltola campaign aides, the DSCC and outside operatives took part in a "ballot composition project"; "Peltola's campaign and the DSCC have denied any wrongdoing." (R)
tl.a: DOJ; AG Todd Blanche; U.S. Attorney Michael Heyman; Alaska Bureau of Investigation; Mary Peltola campaign; Marc Elias

tl.e: Votebeat: the Alaska Senate race is called for Mary Peltola (more than 50%, over 12,000 votes ahead); the Justice Department told Votebeat this week it still plans to pursue its criminal and civil investigation of the second "Dan Sullivan" candidacy (at least 20 preservation or target letters before Election Day); Sen. Sullivan has not conceded and will decide after certification next week.
tl.a: DOJ; Todd Blanche; Mary Peltola; Dan S. Sullivan

tl.e: DHS IG Cuffari reports "systematic obstruction" (March 2026).
Cuffari told Congress DHS had "systematically obstructed" 11 OIG reviews, including the Butler probe.

Under a federal grand jury subpoena, the Arizona Senate gives the FBI dozens of servers and drives holding 200+ terabytes from the 2021 Maricopa "audit" (Cyber Ninjas reports, county electronic records, images of county election systems, possibly ballot images and voter files); Petersen: "The FBI has the records"; Maricopa says it got no subpoena; the AZ SOS weighs legal options to protect voter data; AG Mayes calls it "weaponization."
tl.a: FBI; USAO Arizona (U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine); Arizona Senate President Warren Petersen

tl.e: Arizona's U.S. Attorney announces an investigation of three voter-registration groups (Stand Indivisible Arizona, Worker Power, When We Count) based on undercover videos by a Heritage-affiliated site, refers it to the FBI, and writes Maricopa Recorder Heap and Secretary of State Fontes asking them to review registrations the groups submitted. The videographer says "absolutely no voter registrations were submitted."
tl.a: USAO D. Ariz. (U.S. Attorney Timothy Courchaine); FBI

tl.e: DOJ letter describes arrangement: DOJ gives DHS public voter rolls; DHS "enrich[es]" them with DHS records so they can be run through SAVE.

Sworn declaration in NAACP FOIA suit (D.D.C.): "There will be no Federal Bureau of Investigation or U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement employees, much less agents, serving as monitors"; DOJ "is not using sworn law enforcement officers with arrest powers as monitors in a law enforcement capacity." Says nothing about seizure of ballots or equipment.
tl.a: DOJ Civil Rights Division Voting Section (acting chief Eric Neff)

tl.e: InDepthNH reports acting Voting Section chief Eric Neff told New Hampshire Secretary of State David Scanlan in September that he is under criminal investigation for refusing NH's unredacted voter list, with a demand to preserve evidence ("spoliation ... civil and criminal sanctions"). DOJ's civil suit lost in June; appeal pending (1st Cir. 26-1783).
tl.a: DOJ Voting Section chief Eric Neff; NH SoS David Scanlan

tl.e: FDNS becomes a designated law-enforcement entity as of Oct 6, 2025 (stated in the Bartell declaration n.1, which cites no rule); a new FDNS Criminal Investigative Division employs special agents.

On or around May 8, 2026, USCIS FDNS receives the California voter roll from HSI for noncitizen review (the roll was purchased from the California Secretary of State, buyer not named, and given to HSI by a DHS senior counselor about Mar 19; it holds name, address and DOB, no SSN or ID numbers); FDNS then enhances it with Accurint data. FDNS Associate Director Bartell says USCIS "receives state voter rolls or information on state voter rolls from DHS," analyzes them and refers matches to HSI. HSI's Eric McLoughlin says HSI "initially reviewed the list of millions of registered voters in California" and "formatted and delivered" it without changing data, and describes HSI's statewide role as "data intake (including obtaining bona fide voter rolls), preparation, enrichment, quality review, and routing of leads" (Dkt. 62-3 paras 11, 14, 20). The roll reflects voter registration as of Aug 2025.

A USCIS FDNS list of 20,930 "likely noncitizen" California registrants, built from the purchased California roll (buyer not named) enriched with LexisNexis Accurint and scored by FDNS into confidence levels, is given to HSI and delivered to California on Oct 13, 2026 (Bartell: "My understanding is that list was delivered to California on October 13, 2026"); the process "is distinct from" SAVE, which "was not utilized" (para 14); USCIS later found about 189 records with "minor data discrepancies" on the list and alerted HSI (n.1).

DOJ files its original ex parte application for a TRO and order to show cause to block counting of ~20,000 mail ballots (Oct 19; lodged as attachments to an application to exceed page limits, ECF 22, 22-1, 22-2, with the McLoughlin and Bartell declarations), asking for relief by Nov 3; the case is assigned to Judge Holcomb Oct 20 (ECF 34) and has no hearing or ruling before the Oct 21 transfer.

Oct 21 in United States v. California: the case is transferred to Judge Carter as related to 2:25-cv-09149 (docket ECF 46; ECF 149 cites "Dkt. 44," which on the docket is Judge Holcomb's standing order); DOJ refiles its emergency ex parte TRO application as to noncitizen vote-by-mail ballots (ECF 62; Bartell, McLoughlin and Hamill declarations) after leave to exceed the word limit (ECF 53) and says Los Angeles County had processed more than 331,000 mail ballots since Oct 11 (R); the Court "immediately" sets an Oct 27, 1:00 PM hearing (ECF 64); "a few minutes before 9:00 p.m." DOJ asks for a ruling by noon Oct 22 (ECF 67); on Oct 22 DOJ files a notice of appeal claiming "constructive denial" (ECF 74).

Democracy Docket reports how DHS found ~20,000 California names is 'a mystery' (unnamed third-party platform; roll source not stated); four days later Bartell Decl. #2 (ECF 107-2, Oct 26) names the roll as purchased from the CA SOS and the platform as LexisNexis Accurint.

Bartell Declaration #2 (US v. California ECF 107-2, executed and filed Oct 26 for the Oct 27 TRO hearing before Judge Carter) lays out the FDNS pipeline: roll "purchased from the California Secretary of State and provided to HSI" (Ex. A; buyer not named; no SSNs), reaching HSI about Mar 19 from "a DHS senior counselor" (107-3 ¶5) and FDNS about May 8 (¶21); six fields sent to LexisNexis Accurint, which returns aliases, SSNs, DOBs, dates of death, phones and addresses (¶15); paired with A-numbers (¶16); name+DOB+SSN queries to State and SSA, none without an SSN (¶17); FDNS confidence levels (¶18) and two-level manual review (¶19); refined list to HSI (¶22), which "continued to further refine the data with federal law enforcement systems" (62-3 ¶23); 20,930 names delivered to California Oct 13, ~189 with "minor data discrepancies" (n.1); 17,000+ more under review, "most ... will end up being referred to HSI" (¶24). Bartell: FDNS Associate Director since July 2026, senior counselor to the USCIS Director Sept 2025-Jul 2026, Acting AD Apr-Jul 2026. USCIS receives records "on a rolling basis before the election date" (para 24). Defendants are the State of Alaska, Director Carol Beecher, the Election Boards and the State Ballot Counting Review Board; a "Final Determination Letter" is attached to the complaint. Filing: "it is vital that Defendants not certify any election result that may be impacted by voter confusion." Trump, Oct 23: "Well, I'm one that said, 'Do it.'" The complaint is signed Oct 22 by Associate AG Stanley E. Woodward Jr. and AUSA E. Bryan Wilson; a federal grand jury had earlier been convened on the second Dan Sullivan (R). tl.e: Morelle (House Administration ranking) and Padilla (Senate Rules ranking) write Acting DAG McCotter about the Oct 13 letters, Oct 15 complaint and Oct 16 letter to LA County Counsel, alleging "political weaponization"; they demand answers by 5:00 p.m. Nov 2 on White House direction, how DHS/DOJ built the list, whether private parties supplied data, why DOJ waited, who drafted, private-party input on the legal theory, the "likelihood" threshold and full matching methodology, whether DHS personnel posed as California voters to access voter data, any NVRA 90-day analysis, OPR/ethics consultation, and the thumb-drive cybersecurity and who approved it.
Deadline (5:00 p.m.) for DOJ to answer the Morelle-Padilla Oct 19 questions on the California list and suit.

Senate Rules holds the confirmation hearing for Trump's two Republican FEC nominees (nominated February); the FEC has lacked a quorum for more than a year; only two Democratic commissioners serve. Both "evaded questions about how they would specifically act toward Trump's political operation, MAGA, Inc." Stow: "I pledge to discharge my duties with impartiality"; Woodson (Wiley Rein): "Everyone that will come before me, I will treat exactly the same." Padilla: commissioners must commit to "restoring and defending that independence. Full stop."
tl.a: Senate Rules Committee (Bill Hagerty, Alex Padilla); FEC nominees Ashley Stow and Andrew Woodson

tl.e: En bloc confirmation of IGs: Bell (HHS), Moring (DoD), Walk (USDA, ex-senior adviser to USDA Secretary), D'Esposito (Labor, ex-GOP congressman), Kirk (SBA, also PRAC chair from Mar 1, 2026); sworn Dec 22, 2025-Jan 6, 2026.

Inspectors general announce they have joined the NFDC (Aug 25): DOL OIG (IG Anthony P. D'Esposito) says that "As a signatory of the NFDC Charter" it "committed dedicated analysts and investigators to the prosecutor-led effort," describes NFDC as a centralized space joining federal law enforcement, the IG community and state partners, and says the launch turns "the White House Fraud Task Force's whole-of-government approach into a working reality"; SSA OIG says it can "fuse Social Security-specific intelligence with investigative data from across the federal enforcement community"; PRAC is "bringing its data and analytical capabilities to this partnership." The charter text is not public.

Commerce Secretary Lutnick signs (Sept 8, 2026; published Sept 10, 91 FR 57524, FR Doc. 2026-18481; docket USBC-2026-0628, RIN 0607-AA75; OMB-reviewed significant action) the proposed 2030 census residence criteria: usual residence is where a person has "lawfully spent the greatest number of days" in a Jan 3-Apr 1 "census enumeration period," "evidenced by" tax records (sec. 60.2(a)); all foreign citizens other than LPRs are "Not counted for apportionment" (60.4(b)); Census "is considering utilizing its enormously broad access to administrative records to determine an individual's legal status," calling its holdings "nearly exhaustive of the civilian Federal government's holdings" (Treasury, HHS, DHS, State, War, USPS, state and commercial data), and asks comment on a legal-status question; Part 70 bans race, ethnicity and sexual-orientation questions and 70.3(b) bars noise infusion affecting national/state counts (with DAO 216-26). It cites EO 14151, 14192, 14281, the Jul 21, 2020 apportionment memorandum and OMB M-25-20. Comments were due Oct 13, extended to Nov 2 (FR 2026-20328, Oct 5). TPM reports Commerce overrode Treasury's push to keep tax data only "corroborating" (R). Proposed secs. 60.5-60.6 count military personnel using Department of War data, and Census may consider tax records filed after Apr 1 (91 FR 57526, 57529-30).
Warren letters to Lutnick and others on removed anti-interference language and OMB involvement; answers due Oct 7.

Axios (Nov 11, "Scoop: Bessent confronts Lutnick in Situation Room over China inaction"): at a post-election Situation Room meeting (dated Nov 5 by BeInCrypto's summary), Bessent asked Lutnick why Megaspeed had not been added to Commerce's Entity List; Lutnick said he would "look into" it; others in the room sided with Bessent; Axios counts at least three times this year Lutnick intervened in China actions Trump had signed off on. Commerce spokesperson Kristen Eichamer disputed that a confrontation occurred (R, via Raw Story). Bessent repeated the criticism on television Nov 13 (Foreign Policy Journal/VINnews headlines).
tl.a: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent; Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick; White House Situation Room

tl.e: New York Times (Ana Swanson, Devlin Barrett, Nov 9): BIS agents had spent months building a case that Megaspeed was diverting Nvidia AI chips to China when, in August 2025, Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter emailed the agents seeking information and wrote that Jeff Kessler, a senior Commerce official who reports directly to Secretary Lutnick, had given Nvidia permission to contact them; the agents declined a meeting and forwarded the emails to Kessler, who (per a Commerce official) told them to handle the case by the book; at DOJ's request Commerce paused its work and the case moved to a DOJ criminal inquiry. Commerce says it handled the case "strictly by the book." Trump on Huang: "I haven't heard he's done anything wrong." China calls the spy claim "smears."
tl.a: Commerce Department, Bureau of Industry and Security; Under Secretary-level official Jeff Kessler; Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter; DOJ

tl.e: House Democrats send Cantor Fitzgerald's Brandon Lutnick a demand letter citing CNBC: Cantor held about $1.2 billion in Nvidia stock when Howard Lutnick was confirmed and its reported share count fell nearly 50% between Sept 2025 and March 2026, while Commerce declined to put Megaspeed on the Entity List though four agencies reportedly supported it. Letter: "Secretary Lutnick reportedly blocked efforts within the U.S. government to close them, undermining national security while decisively benefiting Cantor Fitzgerald's bottom line." Cantor calls the allegations "baseless" and says the holdings were mainly client equity-swap hedges. Lutnick to testify to Senate Banking, reportedly Dec 10. (R)
tl.a: Reps. Jamie Raskin, Gregory Meeks, Sydney Kamlager-Dove; Brandon Lutnick; Cantor Fitzgerald; Howard Lutnick; Commerce

tl.e: J. Michael Luttig publishes warning on a possible Jan 3, 2027 House Clerk-roll maneuver.
New House convenes; Clerk prepares initial roll (Luttig scenario).

DOJ says Sept 10 State Citizenship Lists "do not yet exist"; Sept 25 counsel Joshua Schopf on pre-midterm release: "We might. It's possible. I cannot say."; Xinis orders immediate notice of any planned release.
tl.a: DOJ (EPIC v. DHS/SSA, D. Md., Judge Xinis)

tl.e: Federal Ballot Mail Portal launched (EO 14399); PMG Steiner Sept 4; Sept 18 work stopped on mail-voting computer system after court intervention.

Postmaster General Steiner says work on the mail-voting computer system stopped after court intervention ("There's an injunction so we're not doing anything") and "Everything is solved if people vote early"; a Sept 16 USPS memo said it will "not be enforcing any of these new rules in the 2026 federal election" (reported Sept 18).
Virginia whistleblower: USCIS staff with abbreviated training directed to search state voter-registration systems, sometimes via voter self-lookup attestations; VA AG demands logs preserved.
tl.a: Virginia whistleblower / VA AG Jay Jones

tl.e: Vacates FEMA FY2026 HSGP election conditions (SAVE check of all registrants within 120 days, poll-worker citizenship, plan to transition off bar-code/QR systems, 5% manual audit, reconciliation), the 20% holdback (>$200M) and the Aug 10 memo, as beyond FEMA's authority; vacatur not limited to plaintiffs; FEMA "will comply." The 3% election-security spending requirement is left in place.
tl.a: D.D.C. Judge Amir Ali (Nashville v. DHS, 1:26-cv-02886)

tl.e: Politico (Sam Ogozalek, Chris Marquette, June 5, 2026): a Delaware filing lists Mark Bednar (Duffy's former spokesperson, now a Monument Advocacy principal and Peraton lobbyist) and Maxwell Docksey (former Duffy constituent-services staffer, now spokesperson for the House campaign of Duffy's son-in-law Michael Alfonso in WI-7) among six directors of Great American Road Trip Inc., the 501(c)(4) that paid production costs for Duffy's family travel series; sponsors include DOT-regulated Boeing and Toyota and the U.S. Travel Association (also a Bednar client); Peraton is not a sponsor. Barnes says neither had a fundraising role. Kedric Payne (Campaign Legal Center): an "ethical concern"; Richard Painter: "They're too close to regulated industry." DOT says ethics attorneys cleared Duffy and the nonprofit agreed it would get no "favorable consideration" for federal awards. Sen. Murray asked DOT's IG to investigate.
tl.a: Sean Duffy; Great American Road Trip Inc. (Tori Barnes); Mark Bednar; Maxwell Docksey; Michael Alfonso

tl.e: RuntimeWire (Ryan Merket, Nov 15), from procurement records: on May 8, 2026 modification P00002 to Peraton's Surface Surveillance Initiative delivery order (693KA726F00011) removed "performance bond optional pricing"; on Sept 23, P00004 to the BNATCS master contract (693KA726D00003) removed "IRB requirements in section 11.2 and Exhibit 12" (IRB undefined). S&P downgraded Peraton Corp. from B- to CCC+ with a negative outlook on Apr 17, 2026; Bloomberg reported an Oct 2025 FAA presentation flagged a high risk of financial instability; FAA's Aug 2025 solicitation let it require guarantors if a bidder lacked financial capacity, and whether it did is unknown. GAO: $1.5B ceiling, about $876M negotiated integrator price. Monument Advocacy reported $30,000 a quarter for Peraton in Q3 and Q4 2025 with lobbyist Mark Bednar, Duffy's former congressional communications director; Politico (June) reported Bednar was a director of Great American Road Trip Inc., the nonprofit that paid for Duffy's family travel series (Peraton not a sponsor); six Democratic senators led by Murray asked DOT's IG on June 8 to investigate the show's sponsorships. Veritas funds have Israeli institutional investors (Clal, Migdal, Menora). RuntimeWire: the records "do not establish whether the changes weakened the government's protections" or political influence; DOT says career staff and the law guided contracting. Fast Company: Bedford, "Peraton, think of them as an extension of me."
tl.a: Peraton (Veritas Capital); Mark Bednar (Monument Advocacy); Sean Duffy

tl.e: Punchbowl: Curtis "has deep concerns about the White House's new pick to lead GAO, Eric Ueland," according to his office, and "is concerned about the nomination being too partisan and about how the process played out" at HSGAC. Washington Sun: "Senate Republicans are rushing to confirm Eric Ueland to a 15-year term before relinquishing Senate control." Murray: "Ueland orchestrated the president's destructive mass firing campaign, is presiding over the razing of USAID, and is the last person who should be leading GAO." Wray: fast-tracking "violates both the letter and the spirit of the law." Greenblatt: Ueland would lead an agency that evaluates decisions he helped shape, which "raises serious questions about potential conflicts of interest" (GovExec).
tl.a: Sen. John Curtis (R-Utah); Sen. Patty Murray; Henry Wray (former GAO attorney); Mark Lee Greenblatt (former Interior IG); Eric Ueland

tl.e: OGE FOIA release (appeal FY 27-010): OGE's Seth Jaffe emails the White House's Scott Gast under OGE's "Inquiry into Ethics Risk (IiER)" procedure to follow up on four congressional letters "concerning potential conflicts of interest (COI) involving DOGE and Elon Musk," including "DOGE/CFPB" and "DOGE/FAA (among other concerns)"; OGE's recommendation text is withheld (b)(5). An attached letter cites reports that the FAA "may cancel a $2.4 billion contract that it awarded to Verizon in 2023 to upgrade a communications platform for air traffic control facilities" and "plans to pay Musk's Starlink." The release shows no White House reply. (D)
tl.a: Office of Government Ethics (Seth Jaffe; Christopher Swartz); White House Counsel's Office (Scott Gast); DOGE; Elon Musk

tl.e: DOJ biography identifies Graham Billings as acting NFDC director (joined May from W.D.N.C.).
DoD letter: no active-duty or federalized Guard at polls, no interference with ballots/machines; Slotkin Oct 1 update: DOJ, DHS and FBI had NOT given the same written assurance.
tl.a: DoD Asst. Sec. Mark Ditlevson / Sen. Slotkin

tl.e: Georgia SEB executive director seeks federal intervention on voting-system security and alleged record alteration.
Letter urging DOJ to force voting-software updates before November and stop QR-code tabulation.

Wisconsin court denies a temporary injunction that would have allowed a provisional-ballot backup where an absentee ballot may arrive late (Dane County 2026CV002404); receipt deadline stays 8 p.m. Election Day.
tl.a: Dane County Circuit Court (Judge Rhonda Lanford)

tl.e: Presidential memorandum creates committee of inquiry into Lisa Cook mortgage allegations; Nov 5 hearing; findings on removal for cause.
Salesforce ballroom gifts $1M each (Oct 2025; Dec 24, 2025; Jan 29, 2026—three days after Jan 26 Army award).

Army award to Salesforce's Computable Insights ($5.6B-ceiling IDIQ, Missionforce) Jan 26, 2026; WaPo (Oct 15): Benioff gave $1M (Oct 2025) and Salesforce gave $1M Dec 24, 2025 and $1M Jan 29, 2026 to ballroom fund; Computable Insights is the White House's Salesforce route.
X post: "The era of Super Intelligence is here. AIForce is officially SIForce." Only completed large-company SI rename.

IB 589 replaces the HSGP fusion-center article "due to an administrative error": fusion centers using FY2026 funds must support regional Homeland Security Task Forces (tips, leads, SARs, assigned personnel, joint products on HSIN), support identity-theft/illicit-ID enforcement and report 287(g) status and seats held for ICE ERO, support benefit-fraud tracing, and align products to HIPF Priority One, with quarterly reporting to FEMA.
tl.a: FEMA Grant Programs Directorate (Acting Assoc. Admin. Jonathon P. Myers)

tl.e: Weber writes Acting DAG McCotter rejecting the Oct 13 demands: DHS never gave data or methodology (refused to write, insisted on a call/meeting); the list (~20,000, "a fraction" of DHS's 190,000) was not sent to her; demands violate VRA 10307(a), the NVRA 90-day bar, Cal. Const. art. II secs. 2, 2.5 and Elec. Code; the letter "may utilize a policy" vacated in Common Cause (D.D.C. Oct 9); she will review real evidence but "will not disenfranchise thousands of Californians."

Acting Deputy AG McCotter writes Los Angeles County Counsel (cc Secretary of State Weber and Registrar Logan) that officials who count ballots of listed voters after "actual notice" could be "aiders and abettors to a federal crime" (18 U.S.C. 611 and 2) and that "The legal consequences for either facilitating or ignoring a federal crime are significant" ("knowingly tabulate" is Democracy Docket's paraphrase; the exact "risk becoming aiders and abettors" wording is verified only for Essayli's Oct 23 letter; the scanned letter is still unread), treating the list itself as notice; the letter concedes the list includes people outside LA County.
California must verify the citizenship of those more than 20,000 registrants before mail-in ballots are counted; list "just the floor"; "we're not perfect."
AP and CalMatters report that in Pennsylvania DHS claimed more than 14,000 possible noncitizen registrants while nine people are charged; DOJ puts the national total at 156 charged.

Los Angeles County's sworn TRO opposition in United States v. California says "the October List is unreliable": only 7,035 of DOJ's ~20,000 records have county addresses; in a 200-name sample 42.4% are active, 42.9% canceled and 4.6% inactive registrations, 71.2% never voted, and 25.8% list a U.S. birthplace (NPR: 38.9% of entries with a meaningful birthplace); the list began from a roster over a year old from an unidentified source via an unnamed commercial platform; ballots are already commingled. DOJ's McCotter: "we're not perfect" (NPR). NPR reports 112 of the 200 as canceled or inactive, which does not match the filing's percentages (about 95); the filing governs. Judge Carter adopts these figures in the order's background (ECF 149 p.5, citing Bhullar Decl. Dkt 32-3 paras 24-25). DOJ spokesperson Pels: California "cannot facilitate the violation of federal law," no "willful blindness."

DOJ spokeswoman Pels: DOJ is "following the facts and the law, not anyone's political timetable"; Acting DAG McCotter: "Every illegal vote cancels out the vote of a lawful American citizen"; DOJ says Operation Protect the Vote charged 48 people in five states this month.

DOJ letters to election officials in all 50 states order preservation of federal election records for 22 months under 52 U.S.C. 20701 (registration forms, pollbooks, sign-in sheets, ID copies, mail-ballot requests and envelopes, and the ballots themselves); "It is a crime to willfully fail to comply with Section 20701"; up to one year in prison. Disclosed in a footnote to DOJ's Oct 30 Boasberg filing.

McCotter, replying on X to U.S. Attorney Reitz's post of his preservation letter to Sen. Blumenthal: "The First Amendment expressly prohibits Congress from infringing the speech and association rights of Americans." Blumenthal: he will "not be intimidated"; the administration is "weaponizing the Department of Justice to baselessly target Congress in direct violation of the Constitution." WSJ called the letter "an unusual move."
tl.a: Acting Deputy Attorney General Trent McCotter; Sen. Richard Blumenthal

tl.e: Sacramento Bee: a federal grand-jury subpoena dated Sept 3, requested by AUSA Kevin Khasigian, ordered Sacramento County to produce voter records for several people "from 2021 through the present day" (full registration file, voting history, registration updates and affidavits); questions went to FBI Special Agent Laura Giouzelis. Similar subpoenas went to other counties in the district, to Secretary of State Shirley Weber's office and to the DMV. An affidavit: "Between September 2, 2026, and September 4, 2026, special agents with the FBI served grand jury subpoenas on the California Secretary of State, the Fresno Registrar of Voters, and the California Department of Motor Vehicles"; "By October 1, 2026, the FBI had received substantive responses for every subpoena served." Sacramento County says it produced records redacted of candidate choices and party. The records became "the backbone of a dozen criminal cases" against green-card holders in the Eastern District, and those charges "were then cited in other court cases, lending credence to the government's database of possible noncitizen voters." UC Davis's Kevin Johnson: "This is extraordinary"; "a fishing expedition." DOJ told the Bee the prosecutions continue after the election. (R)
tl.a: U.S. Attorney's Office, E.D. Cal. (AUSAs Kevin Khasigian, Joshua Banister); FBI (Special Agent Laura Giouzelis); California Secretary of State; California DMV; county registrars

tl.e: U.S. Attorneys send 48-hour letters to California county registrars (count unresolved, U: at least 18 per the L.A. County registrar's office as reported by CBS/AP; 57 of 58 per Here Columbia; all 58 per Democracy Docket body text) asking counties to work with DOJ and DHS to "identify who on the accompanying list is a citizen and who is not," set aside unverified ballots, and send SSNs and ID data. Essayli's letter to San Bernardino (1,133 names) warns officials who knowingly tabulate them "risk becoming aiders and abettors to a federal crime"; two uniformed DHS officers hand-delivered Napa's letter (42 names); Amador's lists 4 names. The state AG says the lists contain errors; Mendocino's lists people who don't live there. DOJ, Oct 24: "not requesting a purge, cancellation of registrations, or any programmatic action." No county reported complying. CNN saw San Bernardino's letter. Essayli: "Any election official who knowingly processes the ballot of a noncitizen is opening themselves to legal jeopardy." Contra Costa's letter lists 407 names and threatens legal action; LA Registrar Dean Logan says "some or all" counties received letters. Judge Carter's order states that on Oct 23 "the United States sent letters to every county in California requiring them to set aside the votes of alleged non-citizens," warning that officials "risk significant federal scrutiny" (ECF 149 p.7; D that the court said it; county count still U pending the letters).
Logan statement: did not open USB; DOJ letter told counties to respond to a DHS headquarters election mailbox by Oct 15 noon EST, cc USA Bilal Essayli.
Essayli: DOJ not trying to cancel votes; "emergency action because of the actions of California"; if dismissed, DOJ will take matter to "other courts."
Essayli: "overwhelming evidence" that tens of thousands of noncitizens registered in California.
Essayli held "unlawfully serving as a 'de facto' United States Attorney"; disqualified from two criminal cases (Ramirez, Tran); order delayed five business days; Essayli will keep serving.
tl.a: Judge J. Michael Seabright (sitting in C.D. Cal.)

tl.e: After Carter's TRO denial, Essayli: "We filed our Notice of Appeal and will immediately seek an emergency order from the Ninth Circuit"; says the Solicitor General authorized it; "This ongoing emergency disenfranchises American citizens through dilution."
tl.a: First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli (C.D. Cal.)

tl.e: Bloomberg Law: Justice Department leadership directed California's U.S. attorneys to begin criminal probes, including grand-jury subpoenas, of state and local officials over the administration of "illegal voting"; pressure came from the Deputy AG's office; Essayli's office reportedly eager to investigate officials including Secretary of State Weber. Targets and statutes not known. DOJ: "does not comment on leaks about alleged grand jury subpoenas."
tl.a: DOJ leadership; USAO C.D. Cal. (Essayli) and at least one other CA district

tl.e: DOJ announces actions against North Korea's crypto theft, including a "North Korean Super Intelligence-Enabled Social Engineering Campaign Known as 'FaceStealer'" that targeted crypto holders and people "Working the Open-Source Supply Chain"; NSD "will use every tool at its disposal to seize"; Essayli: North Korea funds "its malign activities."
tl.a: DOJ National Security Division (M. Scott Proctor); Criminal Division (A. Tysen Duva); C.D. Cal. (First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli)

tl.e: A federal judge refuses DOJ's request to delay the ruling that Essayli is serving unlawfully as Los Angeles's top federal prosecutor (R, Los Angeles Times; Bloomberg Law).
tl.a: Bill Essayli (U.S. Attorney's Office, C.D. Cal.); federal judge (C.D. Cal.)

tl.e: Ukraine strikes Russian data centers (Oct 8-18); Dmitriev (Oct 16): US-Russia discussing joint data-centre projects; Trump open to trilateral with Xi and Putin (Oct 19-20).
Dmitriev: "We are also discussing joint projects in the field of Russian and US data centres," incl. small nuclear plants (no U.S. confirmation).

In Texas, as early voting opens, U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz posts a video: "If you violate federal election law, I will hunt you down and prosecute you," promising help to federal monitors at "key" polling places. No follow-up action reported yet

Reitz announces referral procedures with Texas SOS and AG, coordination with DHS, FBI and Civil Rights Division to surge resources, election officers to advise monitors; invokes foreign actors' "NGO allies."

Reitz (U.S. Attorney, Southern District of Texas) sends Sen. Richard Blumenthal a preservation demand: "formally give you notice of your obligation to preserve all documents, communications, and other electronically stored information relevant to your intent to deprive citizens of their core constitutional rights in violation of 18 USC statutes 241 and 242"; "This demand applies to you, your staff, employees, agents, consultants, campaign personnel"; warns of "significant legal consequences"; deadline Nov 18. Blumenthal led the inquiry into Trump ballroom donors and family business deals. The letter (read) cites NAACP v. Alabama ex rel. Patterson and warns of "sanctions, adverse-inference instructions, or other penalties."
tl.a: U.S. Attorney Aaron F. Reitz (S.D. Tex.)

tl.e: CBS News, Democracy Docket, Law360, Tampa Free Press (Nov 16): Campaign for Accountability filed a bar complaint against U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz for "Threatening Senators for Congressional Oversight"; quoted by CBS's Scott MacFarlane: "Mr. Reitz, the chief federal prosecutor in his district, threatened prosecution. No probable cause could support either charge." Baptist News Global: the group asks the Texas Bar to investigate.
tl.a: Campaign for Accountability; U.S. Attorney Aaron Reitz (S.D. Tex.); Sens. Richard Blumenthal, Elizabeth Warren

tl.e: Shirley testifies to the Senate Homeland Security committee. He says California voter rolls "allow for 126 year olds to be registered," that "a dog was able to vote in 2 elections" and that "the homeless were being paid to vote," and urges voter ID. No sources given in the written testimony. (D)
tl.a: Senate Homeland Security Committee / Nick Shirley

tl.e: WHIP (NFED Criminal Tip Rewards Pilot) terms and FAQ posted; America.gov privacy policy updated (fraud form goes browser-direct to Treasury Fraud.gov; ZDR with unnamed "SI providers"; Cloudflare logs 12 months); whitehouse.gov/fraud modified same day; first $10,000 award to Nick Shirley.
United States v. California moves from Judge John Holcomb (assigned Oct 20) to Judge Carter as a related case (Carter earlier dismissed DOJ's suit against Weber); first hearing set for Oct 27.

Arizona AG and Secretary of State sue Maricopa County Recorder Justin Heap (filed Oct 21) to restore 25 citizens removed as "not eligible" after SAVE flags (207 flagged; 52 of 60 prior voters found citizens); the Recorder agrees Oct 23 to reinstate them.

Save America pays Brand Woodward Law $1,392,540 in 12 "legal consulting" disbursements: $685,301 in 10 payments to "Brand Woodward Law" (Oct 19, 2021 to Dec 1, 2023) and $707,239 in 2 payments to "Brand Woodward Law, LP" (Sept 6 and Dec 26, 2024). None after Dec 26, 2024. Woodward's May 23, 2025 ethics agreement names him co-founder of the firm. (D)
tl.a: Save America PAC; Brand Woodward Law; Stanley Woodward Jr. (Associate Attorney General)

tl.e: Per the court, Mizelle meets Levi and HPE's Schultz at DOJ without HPE's lawyers of record; about June 25 he hands the negotiations to Stanley Woodward Jr. Antitrust Division staff appear to have been left out after June 10. (D)
tl.a: Chad Mizelle (DOJ); William Levi; John Schultz (HPE); Stanley Woodward Jr.

tl.e: Per the court, at 7:08 pm HPE's Schultz sends Woodward a draft competitive impact statement, the explanation DOJ files to justify a settlement; the settlement is filed June 28, and Rinner testified DOJ changed nothing significant except dropping a price pledge. (D)
tl.a: John Schultz (HPE); Stanley Woodward Jr.; DOJ

tl.e: DOJ tells the Ninth Circuit the Alaska Senate case is moot and asks it to vacate Judge Gleason's standing ruling (Munsingwear) rather than affirm: "there no longer exists any means" to tell which Daniel J. Sullivan votes were meant for Sen. Sullivan. It argues the court could have ordered "preservation and segregation of potentially tainted ballots," that "State law cannot, of course, stand in the way of court orders vindicating federal law," and that the contrary view "could have unpredictable consequences in future elections"; opposes sanctions (DktEntry 39). (D)
tl.a: DOJ (Associate Attorney General Stanley E. Woodward, Jr.; U.S. Attorney Michael J. Heyman; AUSA E. Bryan Wilson); U.S. v. Alaska (9th Cir. 26-7304)

tl.e: DOJ asks the court to "preserve and segregate all ballots ranking Daniel J. Sullivan" in the Alaska Senate race to check for voter confusion.

Alaska's Republican-led state government asks Judge Gleason to dismiss DOJ's suit to condition certification of the Senate race; state attorneys call segregating ballots that rank Daniel J. Sullivan "not even possible."
tl.a: State of Alaska (US v. Alaska, Judge Gleason)

tl.e: State Department files its STATE-26 passport-records notice (public inspection Oct 22; published Oct 23, signed by Timothy J. Kootz, Senior Agency Official for Privacy). "Voter eligibility" is added to the SUMMARY and PURPOSES effective on publication; new routine use (w), effective Nov 23 unless revised, covers "Various entities including, but not limited to, Federal, state, territorial, tribal, and local government agencies, and non-profit organizations, utilizing federal government verification platforms, for the purpose of verifying the identity or citizenship for users accessing government websites and applications, voter eligibility, and other governmental services"; no platform is named; the catch-all (x) for other agencies is kept (whether it was relettered from (u) is not stated, U); the stated reasons (cloud storage, OMB breach guidance, administrative hearings, "additional users for identity verification") omit voter eligibility; STATE-02 rescinded (FR 2026-21694); comments due Nov 23. Effective on publication: the renamed system, storage in a government cloud (ESOC) and the purposes listing "voter eligibility."

Ninth Circuit oral argument in 26-7070 (Bennett, Bumatay, Sanchez) on DOJ's emergency motion to segregate ~20,000 mail ballots: Bennett, "I don't see how we have jurisdiction," and "How can it preempt something that is expressly authorized by a provision of the Constitution?" (states decide which votes count, Smiley v. Holm); Judge Sanchez asks DOJ's Matthew Donnelly "which third parties were involved in providing the data" Donnelly could not answer; no ruling.

Acting U.S. Attorney Charles Neil Floyd (W.D. Wash.) and First AUSA Pete Serrano (E.D. Wash.) ask WA Secretary of State Hobbs to sequester the ballots of 405 alleged noncitizens "pending confirmation," claiming 1,500+ past ballots ("only the tip of the iceberg"); method: questioning detainees and border crossers about voting, cross-referenced with immigration and voter data "one person at a time"; HSI Seattle to investigate. Hobbs says some are citizens, one record is from 1994, and there have been 60+ federal subpoenas for individual voter records. No federal case over the request was found in W.D. or E.D. Wash. as of Oct 28; so far it is a letter, not a lawsuit (U, CourtListener search).

Letter to Washington Secretary of State Hobbs on "Noncitizen Voting in the 2026 Federal Election": DHS gave the offices a list of persons who, "with a high level of confidence, have voted"; "the individuals identified are or were noncitizens (i.e., they may have subsequently naturalized)"; "over 400 individuals and over 1,500 total votes." It asks officials to "not verify the signature and/or tabulate the ballot until citizenship can be determined," routes replies to a DHS election mailbox, threatens "emergency relief," and says the offices expect a second DHS list before the general election.
tl.a: U.S. Attorneys, E.D. and W.D. Wash. (Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd; FAUSA Pete Serrano)

tl.e: After Hobbs rejects the 405-ballot hold, Floyd says the state is "knowingly sending out ballots to non-citizens" and "the State of Washington does nothing to confirm citizenship"; unclear whether DOJ will sue.
tl.a: Acting U.S. Attorney Neil Floyd (W.D. Wash.)

tl.e: DOJ leaders gamed out election "doomsday" scenarios from foreign cyberattacks to chaos at polls (three unnamed officials, improbable); intel official: "Nobody knows what the president might do if the mid-terms don't go his way."

Hobbs rejects the U.S. Attorneys' demand to set aside ballots of 405 listed voters: "many of the persons on your list are United States citizens"; not counting them would "likely be unlawful" without individualized proof; many are not registered or are inactive; the list has "several glaring deficiencies" and no stated sources. USAO W.D. Wash. will "decide next steps."
tl.a: Washington Secretary of State Steve Hobbs

tl.e: Potter County Republican Party v. Benge (N.D. Tex. 2:26-cv-00215) is filed and assigned to Judge Matthew Kacsmaryk (Amarillo). It asks the court to bar certification of the November federal results unless every paper ballot in Texas is hand-counted, citing voting-equipment "components manufactured by foreign adversaries," supply-chain tampering and unnamed reports of AI hacking voting systems; it alleges no actual breach or miscounted vote (R, Yahoo/Texas Tribune Oct 29). Standing orders entered Oct 28 (D, docket).
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party; Daniel Rogers

tl.e: Judge Kacsmaryk sets an expedited schedule on Potter County's motion to dismiss the hand-count-before-certification suit: plaintiffs respond by Nov 14, reply by Nov 17; "The Court will not consider any motions for an extension."
tl.a: Potter County Republican Party v. Benge (N.D. Tex., Kacsmaryk)

tl.e: Potter County class hand-count suit: the court grants leave for a pro se amica brief supporting plaintiffs (ECF 78-79) and denies the county's motion to dismiss as moot after the amended complaint (ECF 80). (D)
tl.a: Judge Matthew Kacsmaryk; Potter County; Lori L. Gallagher

tl.e: Potter County Republican Party v. Benge (N.D. Tex. 2:26-cv-00215), ECF 81-84: Benge files a second motion to dismiss (lack of jurisdiction, failure to state a claim); Judge Kacsmaryk denies an extension and sets plaintiffs' preliminary-injunction motion for Nov 23, response Nov 27, reply Nov 30, and orders plaintiffs to answer the motion to dismiss by Nov 23.
tl.a: Matthew Kacsmaryk (N.D. Tex.); Christy Benge (Potter County elections administrator); Potter County Republican Party

tl.e: CNN (Nov 10): FBI agents served Alaska Senate candidate Gerald Heikes on Oct 31 with a grand-jury subpoena "signed by a top leader of the civil rights division in Washington, DC, rather than by a prosecutor in Alaska," demanding records on Peltola's campaign, the Elias Law Group and several PACs. (R)

Peltola's campaign sues the State of Alaska for information on rejected mail ballots; Peltola leads Sen. Sullivan 102,962 to 102,325 (637) with about 74% of expected vote counted (ABC, Nov 7); ranked-choice results Nov 18 (R).

Intervenors ask the Ninth Circuit to summarily affirm Judge Gleason's Nov 1 dismissal of U.S. v. Alaska (which sought to bar certifying a Sullivan loss) and seek sanctions, calling the appeal "embarrassing and indefensible." Peltola's lead grows as counting continues (ADN, Alaska Beacon, Nov 9). (R)
tl.a: League of Women Voters of Alaska, Common Cause (9th Cir. No. 26-7304)

tl.e: "Peltola win doesn't end DOJ scrutiny of Alaska Senate race, officials say" (R, Washington Post, headline); "Hundreds of subpoenas fly in DOJ's 'Decoy Dan' probe as Democrat Peltola declared winner in Alaska" (R, Fox News, headline).

Judge Trina Thompson (N.D. Cal., SEIU v. DOJ) issues a TRO barring DOJ and DHS from demanding that election officials remove voters, withhold ballots or segregate votes because federal officials allege ineligibility, and from related prosecution threats; DOJ must notify affected jurisdictions and tell the court of pending related search-warrant applications, grand-jury subpoenas and demands for election materials. The order runs to Nov 16 (not just Election Day); next hearing Nov 13.

DOJ (AUSA Kao, U.S. Attorney Missakian) tells the court it "lacks jurisdiction" over the Oct 30 order because of the appeal (ECF 74). Thompson then stays all preliminary-injunction proceedings: "Until further notice from the Ninth Circuit, the Court stays the current proceeding. The hearing set for November 13, 2026, is hereby VACATED"; plaintiffs "can move for an injunction before the Ninth Circuit" (ECF 78). (D)
tl.a: N.D. Cal. (Judge Trina L. Thompson), SEIU v. DOJ 3:26-cv-12800, ECF 74 and 78

tl.e: Heyman confirms a months-long federal criminal probe of the alleged spoiler-candidate scheme, cites a "significant surge of law enforcement assets to Alaska," names no targets or crimes and asks the public for tips; dozens of grand-jury subpoenas this week (R, source).

Newsom writes to the chief judges of California's four federal districts warning the administration may seek search warrants to seize ballots, election records and counting equipment before certification, and will "quickly pivot to the criminal forum" after civil losses; he knows of no pending application; encloses a UC Berkeley guide on assessing election-materials warrants; cites AB 282 (Sept), which makes illegal pre-certification seizure a felony.
Bonta issues a legal advisory for judges and election officials on handling search warrants for election materials, citing the FBI's Fulton County seizure.

A 20-AG coalition opposes DOD's August 2026 change to the Federal Post Card Application, which removed the checkbox "I am a U.S. citizen living outside the country, I have never lived in the United States," calling the "emergency changes" unexplained under the APA; 37 states and D.C. let never-resided citizens vote.
tl.a: California AG Rob Bonta, Nevada AG Aaron Ford, Washington AG Nick Brown (co-leads); Department of Defense (FVAP)
