tl.e: On federal noncitizen-voting arrests in Ohio, LaRose says "my office uses federal law enforcement resources and data to review Ohio's voter registration database" and credits "the unprecedented collaboration between my office and the federal government."
tl.a: Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose

tl.e: Ohio says its office was "the intended recipient of a suspicious mailing that contained a powdery white substance," intercepted by U.S. Postal Service investigators "who are dealing with similar mailings sent to election officials in multiple states"; the FBI is handling the Ohio matter.
tl.a: Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose; FBI; USPS inspectors

tl.e: LaRose refers a voter-registration operation (Black Fork Strategies / Field Forward Ohio) to the U.S. Attorney for the Northern District of Ohio and the FBI Cleveland Field Office, plus state and county prosecutors, to assess whether its conduct "may constitute violations of federal criminal law"; about 5,000 forms in Summit County and 4,000 in Hamilton, 109 delivered late.
tl.a: Ohio Secretary of State Frank LaRose

tl.e: Raffensperger asks Census acting director George Cook for "all the identifying information" behind ~400 Georgia cases (his audit found fewer than a dozen); Wisconsin experts reject ~500.

Georgia's release "Anthropic AI Agent Accessed Publicly Available Information, Georgia Elections Remain Secure" says "Accessing public information is not a hack, and pretending otherwise is reckless and dangerous" and that the Data Hub "is separate from the state's voter registration system"; it says the White House contacted the office Oct 9.
tl.a: Georgia Secretary of State Brad Raffensperger

tl.e: Raffensperger opens an investigation after a routine review finds a memory card with 388 uncounted votes in Seminole County; adding them flips state House District 154 to the Republican incumbent by 262. Counties certify Nov 9. "That is unacceptable, and we intend to find out exactly how it happened." (R)
tl.a: Georgia Secretary of State / Seminole County

tl.e: Florida's readiness update says the Office of Election Crimes and Security made "nearly 900 referrals of potential election fraud to law enforcement" last year; it names no federal partner. (Florida's Sept 24 AG release credited USCIS as "instrumental in confirming non-citizen status.")
tl.a: Florida Secretary of State Cord Byrd

tl.e: Joint OAG-USAO-FBI-HSI announcement: 7 defendants charged; election integrity framed as national-security priority.
tl.a: Texas AG Paxton; USAO; FBI; HSI

tl.e: Paxton announces arrests of convicted felons accused of voting illegally during early voting, on AG warrants in Montgomery County: "Today, my office arrested convicted felons for voting illegally in Texas."

RAGA Mississippi PAC gives Fitch $50,000 (Aug 30, 2019) and $100,000 (Oct 2, 2019) in her first attorney general race; other contributions of $20,000 or more: Kathy Henry $52,100, United Financial $100,000, William Mounger $25,000.
tl.a: Lynn Fitch; Republican Attorneys General Association (RAGA Mississippi PAC)

tl.e: Mississippi campaign-finance filings: Jeremy Lieberman gives Lynn Fitch $666,666 on Oct 18, 2019, her largest itemized contribution; Pomerantz LLP gives $20,000 (Jul 22, 2019). Legal Newsline reported plaintiffs' lawyers "rain cash" on Fitch with Mississippi as a potential client.

Fitch announces her 2027 campaign for governor as "a Trump conservative who doesn't back down from a fight," saying she backed Trump "from the beginning"; eight-stop announcement tour Aug 5-7; Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America (Marjorie Dannenfelser) endorses Aug 5; cash on hand $3.55M at end of 2025 (Magnolia Tribune). Mississippi Today (Feb 2024): about $727,000 of her $1.27M 2023 money came from out-of-state businesses; Legal Newsline (2019) reported national plaintiffs' lawyers as early donors.

Fitch, both Mississippi U.S. Attorneys and the FBI Jackson field office launch "Joint Task Force Vigilance," which "The Department of Justice made ... the first of its kind, a model for bringing together federal and state agencies." The release says the AG's office "was awarded over $2.5 million by the U.S. Department of Justice in July 2026 to establish Joint Task Force Vigilance as a first-of-its-kind model for surging federal and state personnel and resources to fight fraud," funding five prosecutors and "a support and enforcement team to investigate and prosecute fraud, crimes by criminal aliens, human trafficking, and illicit drug activity." No election scope is stated.
tl.a: Mississippi Attorney General Lynn Fitch; U.S. Attorneys (N.D. and S.D. Miss.); FBI

tl.e: Unicorn Riot (Dan Feidt) reviews about 30 Minnesota 15 defense exhibits: records describe an investigation into the finances of CWA Local 7250 and groups tied to a Jan 23 day of action (the union president: an effort to "map out the resistance to ICE"); Federal Reserve wire records were searched from Jan 1, 2023 to Mar 29, 2026; a leaked HSI access-group dataset ("Icepick") lists "HSI-Keyhole_Access," "VSP-Whipple" and HSI PenLink user groups; a spinoff investigation ran in Chicago in April 2026.

Axios: Habba accuses Grenell, then Kennedy Center president, of offering her husband access to Trump for a donation the center never received; Trump asks White House counsel Scharf to investigate. A White House official says the $17.6 million wire came from Congo's finance ministry; Grenell denies it.
tl.a: Alina Habba Mildon; Turhan Mildon; Ric Grenell; Will Scharf

tl.e: Congressman Garcia, other Democrat members of Congress, are intent on threatening and intimidating members of this administration from the president on down to the most junior staffer; "If that's the approach that they're going to take, they're going to be met with a vigorous response from my office and from the Department of Justice every single time." Earlier on Newsmax: subpoenas and investigations "for blatantly unlawful purposes."
tl.a: White House counsel William Scharf (Fox News Sunday)

tl.e: Axios exclusive, then Denver Gazette (Kaelan Deese) and PBS, which posted the memo: a "one-page memo to agency general counsels" from White House counsel Will Scharf says "agencies must notify and obtain approval from both his office and the Office of Legislative Affairs" before agency officials testify to Congress, calling it an "established White House consultation process"; "further guidance regarding other engagements with Congress is forthcoming." A White House official: the administration "will not be extorted, intimidated, or threatened into submission by politically motivated baseless investigations." Scharf to Bloomberg, asked whether agencies will comply with subpoenas: "it depends."
tl.a: White House counsel Will Scharf; White House Office of Legislative Affairs; agency general counsels

tl.e: At the stay hearing in SEIU v. DOJ, AUSA Kenneth Kao agrees it is "fair" to say the California "likely noncitizen" list has a high error rate. Thompson denies DOJ's stay motion, modifies one provision, moves the TRO's end to 5 p.m. Nov 13 and sets the preliminary-injunction hearing for 11 a.m. Nov 13.

Election Day glitches: in Westchester County, N.Y., machines rejected paper ballots and voters' ballots went into "orange emergency ballot bags"; state officials attributed it to "an update to the county's election programming" made after equipment testing. Broward County, Fla., reported "a computer glitch" that stopped voting for about 20 minutes after polls opened. No evidence of foul play reported. Commentator Katie Miller posted "This is how the left steals elections"; Laura Loomer said Democrats were "already trying to steal the election." No sitting federal official found amplifying these as fraud as of ~5 p.m. ET.
tl.a: Westchester County, N.Y.; Broward County, Fla.; commentators

tl.e: Connecticut's Secretary of the State issues a statement on misinformation "posted by the FBI's New Haven office" that wrongly said Election Day was Wednesday: "Do not believe it. Election Day is today, Tuesday, November 3."
tl.a: Connecticut Secretary of the State Stephanie Thomas

tl.e: U.S. v. Williams, D.D.C. 1:25-cr-00322 (Judge AliKhan; prosecuted by the D.C. U.S. Attorney's Office and DOJ's National Security Division). Statement of Offense (ECF 7, Oct 29, 2025): Company One, "fully acquired" in 2018 by Company Two, "a publicly traded, U.S.-based company and defense contractor," sells national-security cyber and intelligence software "exclusively to the U.S. government and select allied governments"; Williams, its general manager from Sept 2024 to Aug 2025, sold Items 1-8 to a "Russia-based software broker" from April 2022 to 2025 under the alias "John Taylor" (one contract: Item 2 for $2,000,000 on Dec 4, 2023; Item 8 delivered July 2025, after the FBI investigation began); in Oct 2024 the company learned its products "had leaked and were possessed by an unauthorized software broker," and Williams oversaw the internal investigator, which blamed "a former employee"; the FBI got the results in Nov 2024; he confessed Aug 6, 2025 and admitted selling at least one item "even after he recognized code he wrote and sold to COMPANY THREE being utilized by a South Korean broker." Government sentencing memo (ECF 24, Feb 10, 2026): the tools went to "multiple partners of the U.S. Intelligence Community" and Five Eyes services; the sales "would have allowed the Russian Broker and its clients to potentially access millions of computers and devices around the world, including in the United States"; victim impact statements from the companies and from "affected government entities" filed under seal; loss over $35 million. Sentenced Feb 24, 2026 to 87 months (R, CyberScoop, which names Trenchant and L3Harris); restitution hearing set for May.
tl.a: Peter Williams; "Company One" (Trenchant) and "Company Two" (L3Harris), named by reporting; Operation Zero ("Company Three")

tl.e: Law-enforcement-at-polls cases (DSCC, NAACP, LULAC/Denver) consolidation discussed; DNC v. DOJ FOIA II on seizures of ballots/equipment; Democracy Forward v. USCIS FOIA on SAVE (production due Oct 28).

At a Nov 2 hearing before Judge Loren AliKhan in suits by the NAACP, LULAC and others over federal agents at polling sites, government counsel relays an FBI statement after social-media videos showed FBI agents and National Guard troops near a D.C. polling place: agents "may have been observed near an active polling location"; the FBI says they were on a roving neighborhood foot patrol for the D.C. Safe and Beautiful Task Force, not an investigation, and that it then directed D.C. employees to avoid polling locations: "Agent personnel were advised that the only exception to that prohibition is if there is an active shooter." The polling place is not identified. Separately, in October National Guard troops were seen next to a D.C. ballot drop box; the task force said troops "had been directed not to monitor polling sites."
tl.a: FBI; DOJ (counsel Catherine Malycke); D.D.C. (Judge AliKhan)

tl.e: A pro-Trump content creator posts on Facebook and X that an FBI raid of a Houston warehouse the night before Election Day found more than 20,000 "fraudulent ballots" cast for Democrats. FBI national office: "No election-related operation occurred." Harris County Clerk Teneshia Hudspeth: "The information circulating on social media is false." PolitiFact rates it Pants on Fire; the attached photos came from unrelated events, including a 2026 FBI search of an election warehouse in Georgia.

NPR reports, and Democracy Docket follows Sept 20, a DHS document obtained by the DNC through FOIA that lists places where election information is distributed in multiple languages, naming Cobb, DeKalb and Gwinnett counties in Georgia. DNC litigation director Dan Freeman calls it "extremely concerning." DHS spokesperson: noncitizens "should not be able to use a purported lack of knowledge of the English language" as an excuse to avoid prosecution.

Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson signs a $50,000, one-year contract for Experian's TrueTrace locating product ("Best Address," USPS change-of-address data and Social Security death data) and runs about 1.9 million voter checks, roughly every active voter, sending at least names and home addresses. The contract states Experian "cannot and will not ... be an insurer or guarantor of the accuracy or reliability" of its data; the office signed off. Experian to the EAC: "Often, this will match their residence; however, we don't verify residency." Mississippi had sued Experian in 2014 over credit-report errors, including wrong addresses (settled 2016) (R).

Watson's office adopts a temporary rule deleting Title 1, Part 17, Chapter 4, the mail-ballot cure provision added in 2020 after a voting-rights suit; a spokesperson confirms there are "no steps for curing a mail-in." Reported Nov 6 (R; rule PDFs on sos.ms.gov not yet confirmed).
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson

tl.e: Watson defends the Experian-based voter inactivations as affidavit ballots decide the Senate race: "The system at the end of the day… is working as it was designed"; "I stand behind and will not apologize for having clean voter rolls"; "I cannot make an election commissioner do his or her job." Rankin County Election Commissioner Tonya Rivers says the state supplied inaccurate data ("That was news to us"). (R)
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson (SuperTalk Mississippi)

tl.e: Watson posts, then deletes within 30 minutes, guidance telling voters to use a mail-ballot signature "cure" process he repealed in August; outdated guidance stays on the SoS website. (R)
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson

tl.e: Watson posted, then deleted (after a Democracy Docket inquiry), that Experian was "crawfishing away from Mississippi," tagging the EAC: "Should we consider a lawsuit? They marketed a product for a specific reason and are now saying it wasn't designed for that reason." Experian (Scott Anderson, to The Atlantic): the product "consisted of supplemental address information and was not designed or intended to validate voter records." Jonson: "Mississippi was never told the data was only supplemental or that it was not intended for this use." Former EAC official Don Palmer (Heritage) defended the process in the Daily Signal (Nov 11). Nov 19: the Legislative Black Caucus asked the Legislature to investigate Watson; Mississippi Today: inactive voters were nearly 60,000 above 2024 and 45,000 above 2022; Watson did not answer a pre-election civil-rights coalition letter asking him to reactivate Experian-flagged voters.
tl.a: Michael Watson (Mississippi SoS); Elizabeth Jonson; Experian (Scott Anderson); Don Palmer (Heritage); Mississippi Legislative Black Caucus

tl.e: Watson: the affidavit ballot "is a catch-all. If we made any mistakes, any errors, we were caught by this affidavit process"; "Mississippi law didn't change. The process didn't change"; the state downloaded Experian data in July 2025 and "uploaded the rest of it to finish it up in 2026"; Experian data came from sources including USPS and credit bureaus; his office now uses different sources.
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State Michael Watson (WLOX)

tl.e: Gov. Reeves signs SB 2588 (the SHIELD Act): the Secretary of State must compare the voter rolls against DHS's SAVE each year; flagged voters get a notice and go to "pending" status until they prove citizenship. A federal judge's June order blocking the expanded SAVE for voter checks kept it from starting July 1 (R, MPB, Jun 25); the Supreme Court revived SAVE Sept 25. Whether Mississippi ran SAVE checks before Nov 3 is not public (U).
tl.a: Mississippi Legislature; Gov. Tate Reeves; DHS USCIS SAVE

tl.e: Mississippi Today analysis: over 230,000 voters, about 1 in 9, are inactive before Election Day; inactivations more than doubled in some counties since the March primaries, up to 1 in 5 in DeSoto and Wilkinson; DeSoto alone made over 15,000 voters inactive, more than a third of the statewide increase. The Secretary of State's office told WAPT it has replaced Experian with another company, IDI Data; Assistant SoS Elizabeth Jonson said questions would be answered "after the election." Researcher Thessalia Merivaki calls the scale a "red flag" (R).
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State; county election commissions; IDI Data

tl.e: After polls closed the state Democratic Party sought emergency relief in DeSoto County Circuit Court, citing late openings, ballot shortages, waits over two hours and reports that "law enforcement officers were checking identification of people entering certain polling locations, creating additional delays and potential barriers to access" (agency not named). The party moved to dismiss Wednesday morning; granted (R, Magnolia Tribune, DeSoto Times-Tribune). UPGRADE (D, complaint read Nov 5): ¶18 "Lewisburg and Twin Lakes Baptist precincts ran out of affidavit ballot envelopes, prohibiting the ability for voters to complete an affidavit ballot"; ¶24 "law enforcement personnel were checking the identification of individuals entering certain polling locations" (no agency named); defendants Circuit Clerk Dale Thompson and the DeSoto County Election Commissioners.
tl.a: Mississippi Democratic Party; DeSoto County Circuit Clerk; DeSoto County Circuit Court (CI2026-691)

tl.e: Garcia sends records-preservation letters to 40 agencies and the National Archives under the Federal Records Act and Presidential Records Act, including messages on apps like Signal, and files an amicus brief defending the PRA: "we will not let him cover his tracks" (D).
tl.a: House Oversight Democrats (Ranking Member Robert Garcia)

tl.e: TRO in OneAmerica Votes v. Trump, W.D. Wash. 2:26-cv-04223-JNW, ECF 21 (Washington only, 14 days): bars DOJ and DHS from demanding that Washington officials remove listed voters, refuse them ballots, or segregate or not tabulate their ballots, and from threatening officials with prosecution for not complying. "DOJ may not demand that election officials set aside a registered voter's ballot because the voter's name appears on a federal list"; "A threat of prosecution made for that purpose is not legal advice. It is the pressure that makes the demand work, and the order restrains the two together." Records Serrano on radio: "If we want to cure the issue, we may just have to cut the state out." Carve-outs: investigating or prosecuting unlawful voters, sharing information, "stating its view of what federal law requires." Stay pending appeal denied; PI hearing Nov 18 (D).
tl.a: U.S. District Judge Jamal N. Whitehead (W.D. Wash.)

tl.e: DOJ opposes a preliminary injunction in OneAmerica Votes v. Trump (W.D. Wash. 2:26-cv-04223, ECF 22-23): plaintiffs lack standing because "Defendants have not and cannot provide another list following the injunction entered in League of Women Voters"; Secretary Hobbs said "I'm not going to do anything with this list"; "Enforcement is not just punishment, it includes investigation into whether a crime has been committed and includes actions designed to prevent criminal activity"; "The Elections Clause does not give the States the power to preempt Congress or the Executive's law enforcement role"; DOJ "seeks only to temporarily segregate unsolicited vote-by-mail ballots where there is credible evidence."
tl.a: DOJ (Kristin B. Johnson); Judge Jamal Whitehead

tl.e: OneAmerica Votes v. Trump (W.D. Wash. 2:26-cv-04223), ECF 24, Nov 16: "Notice to Withdraw Pending Motion" (docket text; document not in RECAP; filer not shown). No plaintiffs' reply was filed by the Nov 16 deadline; the PI hearing was set for Nov 18 and the 14-day TRO (ECF 21, Nov 5) runs to about Nov 19.
tl.a: OneAmerica Votes, Latino Community Fund of Washington State, UFCW (plaintiffs); DOJ, DHS (defendants); Judge Jamal Whitehead

tl.e: OneAmerica Votes v. Trump (W.D. Wash. 2:26-cv-04223), ECF 24 (filed by email Nov 14 during a CM/ECF outage, entered Nov 16), now public: plaintiffs "withdraw the portion of their Motion ... that seeks a preliminary injunction" because "Defendants represent to the Court that, based on the Court's November 5 Order, Defendants have refrained from the conduct the temporary restraining order restrains related to the November 3, 2026 election and that Defendants will not resume that conduct before Washington certifies the election results on December 3, 2026." Withdrawal is "without prejudice and is conditioned on the continued accuracy of Defendants' representations." Same day the court struck the Nov 18 PI hearing. Footnote quotes First AUSA Serrano that DOJ would "continually demand that these [ballots] are segregated" and "may just have to cut the state out."
tl.a: OneAmerica Votes, Latino Community Fund of Washington State, UFCW (plaintiffs; Elias Law Group, Abha Khanna); DOJ, DHS (defendants); Judge Jamal Whitehead

tl.e: Mississippi's Senate race is uncalled: ABC (3:31 p.m. Nov 4, 96% reported) has Colom 462,857 and Hyde-Smith 462,792, a 65-vote gap. Colom's campaign estimates up to 15,000 affidavit ballots; the Secretary of State's office says it has no definitive number. Mail ballots postmarked by Nov 3 count through Nov 10; counties certify Nov 13, the state Dec 3; Mississippi has no recount law, only a post-certification ballot-box exam and court contest (R).
tl.a: Mississippi Secretary of State; Colom and Hyde-Smith campaigns

tl.e: Letter "TO ALL 82 MISSISSIPPI COUNTIES" demanding "the immediate separation, secure custody, and preservation of all affidavit ballots" and associated records (envelopes, receipt books, pollbook and electronic pollbook data, SEMS audit logs, tabulator tapes, resolution-board records, communications with the Secretary of State, "video recordings of ballot storage areas"), through any box examination, contest or runoff; "Because these ballots and records are potential evidence in any box examination under § 23-15-911, election contest, or proceeding before the United States Senate, Candidate Hyde-Smith is entitled to their preservation in an unaltered and identifiable state." Cites 52 U.S.C. 20701; reply demanded by 5 p.m. CT the same day (D).
tl.a: Counsel for Cindy Hyde-Smith for U.S. Senate (Lex Politica), letter posted by the NRSC

tl.e: Colom leads Hyde-Smith by 2,574 (467,930 to 465,356, AP Friday evening), up from 1,813 Thursday. Secretary of State (Thu): 6,936 affidavit ballots processed, ~3,300 absentees outstanding. Rankin County: about half of affidavits cured and about 20% rejected so far; scanning starts 5 pm Nov 10 (cure and receipt deadline). ACLU letter says DeSoto is not giving full public access to affidavit counting. Hyde-Smith: "We are not backing down. This election is not over." (R)

Hinds County, Miss.: NRSC and Hyde-Smith observer Coy Westbrook loudly accuses Election Commissioner Bobbie Graves of discussing ballots out of observers' view ("Untoward, one might say"); Democracy Docket says it may signal grounds for a suit. Colom then led by about 2,500 (Nov 10). (R)

AP, CNN and VoteHub call Mississippi's Senate race for Democrat Scott Colom (lead 4,585 when called); Hyde-Smith concedes Wednesday evening: "I respect the decision of Mississippi voters." Earlier, Hinds County accepted only 817 of 2,426 affidavit ballots (about 34%), mostly wrong precinct or not registered; Watson put the statewide acceptance rate at about 76%. Counties certify by Nov 13; state Dec 3. By district (Mississippi Free Press): D1 167 accepted/349 rejected; D2 126/221; D3 119/268; D4 224/289; D5 (Jackson State) 181/482; overall about 66.3% rejected. Commissioner Felicia McClinton blamed registration-drive forms not filed with the circuit clerk by the deadline. Watson (X, Nov 9): "15,547 affidavit ballots have now been processed with roughly 76% of them being accepted."

More grand-jury subpoenas to California county election officials: at least two top election administrators in San Francisco-area counties served Monday Nov 2, returnable Nov 17, seeking information on how counties responded to DOJ's Oct 23 letter to confirm citizenship or set aside ballots of "suspected aliens"; more expected; cover letter signed by Missakian and deputy John Kucera. Sonoma County Counsel: "there is no legal basis for the federal government's requests for Sonoma County to segregate ballots"; Santa Clara is "evaluating the subpoena" (R).
tl.a: U.S. Attorney's Office, N.D. Cal. (U.S. Attorney Craig Missakian)

tl.e: Rep. Lauren Boebert's campaign says it is "investigating" voting as she trails her Democratic challenger; its attorney is former Colorado Secretary of State Scott Gessler (R).
Protect Our Polls Act introduced (covers military and armed federal law enforcement at polls); Baldwin bill names ICE/CBP/Guard incl. checkpoints near polls; Gallego bill.

Cybersecurity Dive (Eric Geller): at his HSGAC hearing, Palantir CISO Michael LoSapio refused to acknowledge that Joe Biden won the 2020 election and said of Jan. 6, 2021: "I don't believe it was an attack ... I wasn't involved in politics. ... I know what I saw on the news"; he would not take a position on the proposed $385 million CISA cut ("I will come back to this committee with a gap analysis") or comment on CISA's current state ("because I'm not inside today"); called CISA "the cybersecurity version of the 911 system." Sen. Tillis (R) and Sen. Wyden (D) will place holds; Wyden: "You can't have an insurrectionist Palantir executive in charge of our nation's cybersecurity and election security." Ranking Member Peters said he "does not appear to meet the statutory requirements of this position."
tl.a: Michael LoSapio (CISA nominee); Sens. Blumenthal, Slotkin, Hassan, Lankford, Tillis, Wyden

tl.e: CalMatters and Shasta Scout, through the First Amendment Coalition, sue Shasta County under the California Public Records Act for a federal grand-jury subpoena that outgoing Clerk-Registrar Clint Curtis says he received in September concerning June 2026 election ballots; Curtis says the FBI came to inspect the room that month ("I just showed them what we had"). The county says the subpoena is "shielded from disclosure"; eight other counties (including Fresno, Imperial, Los Angeles, Orange, San Bernardino) disclosed theirs. Issuing district not reported. (R)
tl.a: CalMatters, Shasta Scout v. Shasta County (Shasta County Superior Court)

tl.e: Stephen Ehikian is sworn in as acting GSA administrator and deputy administrator. FedScoop describes him as "a former Salesforce vice president" for AI products who had "two AI product stints at Salesforce" and co-founded two AI platforms Salesforce acquired. (D for the appointment, GSA release; R for background)
Michael Rigas, deputy secretary of state for management and resources, becomes acting GSA administrator; Ehikian stays deputy administrator. (R)

Ehikian tells GSA staff he will "transition out of that role" and becomes CEO of C3 AI. Asked about closing 18F, he says he gave his direct reports "specific targets"; he says he was not "formally" part of DOGE but believes in its mission. (R)

TTS director Thomas Shedd emails agencies: "Login.gov's work carries forward as a critical part of Government-wide efforts to promote efficiency and fight fraud"; "we are working to accelerate Login's roadmap." Nextgov reports he told staff he wants to use Login.gov to root out fraud. (R)
Ed Forst, former Cushman & Wakefield CEO, is sworn in as GSA administrator after Senate confirmation. (R)
Barbaccia is named acting director of GSA's Technology Transformation Services (home of Login.gov) and an adviser to GSA Administrator Ed Forst, while staying federal CIO. (R)

Corcos, then a DOGE representative and special adviser to Treasury Secretary Bessent, removes about 50 IRS IT leaders; he later says prior technical leadership resisted cuts to cybersecurity contracts. He told Fox: "We've so far stopped work and cut about $1.5 billion from the modernization budget." (R)

As Treasury CIO, Corcos defends IRS IT layoffs a day before RIF notices (about 1,300 to IRS staff; IRS down about 25% in 2025, including about 2,000 IT employees): "It's very hard to fire people"; says only 100 to 200 employees are trusted to carry out his reorganization. On sabbatical from Levels, the health-tech company he co-founded. (R)

Treasury CIO Sam Corcos, who entered government with DOGE, now holds three acting GSA posts: head of Technology Transformation Services, deputy commissioner of the Federal Acquisition Service, and assistant commissioner of Login.gov (GSA confirmed). Wired reported he sought access to government data and pushed a unified IRS API. (R)

Gregory Barbaccia starts as federal chief information officer at OMB. Before: Army intelligence (2003-2008), intelligence analyst, about ten years at Palantir (2010-2020; head of intelligence and investigations from 2017), then Elementus and Theorem. Later also federal chief AI officer (Jul 2025) and service delivery lead (Sept 2025). (R)

Barbaccia asks agency CIOs to audit their contracts with Microsoft, Adobe, Salesforce, Oracle and ServiceNow. The Revolving Door Project, citing Bloomberg, says he also conducted DOGE interviews of civil servants. (R)

Barbaccia calls for "responsible data sharing," says the legal setup for data exchanges needs re-evaluating for the digital age, and asks "why do taxpayers have to supply the government with the same information across multiple agencies?" He says Login.gov needs tough resourcing decisions. (R)

GSA names Greg Hogan, former OPM CIO (from day two of the administration; OPM was an early DOGE stronghold) and since Sept 2025 at the White House National Design Studio, director of Login.gov as "acting assistant commissioner," per Barbaccia's email; WIRED headlines it "A DOGE Affiliate Is Now in Charge of the US Government's ID Platform." Barbaccia: "This is about restoring confidence in how government serves the taxpayer." (R)

GSA Administrator Forst announces Barbaccia will leave government Aug 31 and return to Palantir ("Luckily, Palantir gets you back in that way"); role not stated. He had disclosed Palantir stock while in office (POGO/Sherwood). (R)

Heritage president Kevin Roberts: the SAVE America Act is "about national sovereignty and the survival of American democracy itself"; noncitizens in Democratic states give them "18 House seats and electoral votes"; "Diluting the political power of the American people is becoming the Democrat Party's only remaining organizing principle." (D)

Heritage commentary: with the SAVE America Act stalled, Congress can use Art. I, Sec. 5 to judge members' elections, "subpoena state officials and state voting data," "declare elections invalid and order a new election," and "deny representation to states without voter identification laws"; it names Oregon, California, Illinois and Michigan. (D)
Heritage commentary: election security "is a matter of sovereignty"; state officials should "coordinate with federal authorities" for citizenship and immigration data; cites DHS's 250,000 figure. (D)

Ken Cuccinelli (Election Transparency Initiative), in a Heritage commentary dated Oct 8: DOJ "issued litigation hold notices to election officials in 29 states and the District of Columbia in September" for its voter-roll litigation, as the 22-month retention period for 2024 records expired; Nevada and New Hampshire told local officials to keep records. (R)

The Nation: Corcos left the spousal section of his February 2025 financial disclosure blank, then amended it to list his wife's stake in Sana Health (a DoD grantee). His wife, Varvara Russkova Corcos, was a venture partner at GVA Capital, which managed money for Suleyman Kerimov, sanctioned by Treasury in 2018; she stayed until Dec 2018. She says a residual position "had been inadvertently omitted." (R)

Capital B / 'Sipp Talk Media: ballot monitors report wrong locations, shifting times and denied seats at county affidavit-ballot reviews; ACLU of Mississippi reports closed-door counting in some counties; DeSoto commissioner Laura Edler: "no one has been denied access." No federal or law-enforcement presence reported. (R)
Brett Shumate resigns as Assistant Attorney General for the Civil Division, the fourth DOJ official to leave in the last week, per The Hill. (R)
House Republicans elect Rep. Jim Jordan, who helped lead efforts to overturn the 2020 result, as minority leader for the next Congress; (R)
Blumenthal releases a whistleblower report saying the USPS ballot-mail portal was hastily built and error-prone
Scanlan v. Coalition for Open Democracy, No. 26A512: SCOTUS stays D.N.H. student-ID PIs (1:26-cv-647); Jackson dissents; NH student-ID ban holds for Nov 3.

ProPublica: a Forsyth County, Ga., election-board member who belongs to the Election Integrity Network used ELLY data to question more than 22,000 names and dispute the eligibility of 69 voters after the midterm; four "dead" voters were alive; the board rejected his ballot challenges. ELLY's operator Rick Richards promises data on 3,000+ counties to "citizen monitors" and candidates. ELLY is a rebrand of EagleAI (CLC backgrounder, Aug 4).
tl.a: Forsyth County, Ga. (Max Clavijo); ELLY (Rick Richards)

tl.e: U.S. v. Wagner (E.D. Mich. 2:26-cr-20059, ECF 51), motions to dismiss for selective prosecution and for grand-jury disclosure: the case "stems from Operation Metro Surge"; HSI began investigating Wagner Jan 19, 2026 as "a self-identified Antifa member"; the brief calls NSPM-7 "a blueprint for prosecution and harassment" of ICE protesters, quotes the NYT's account of Assistant Deputy AG Aakash Singh telling prosecutors "Go big ... and go loud," and adopts the Sant defendants' surveillance discovery motion (D. Minn. ECF 212). (D)
tl.a: Kyle Wagner; Federal Community Defender (Riyah Basha); HSI; Aakash Singh

tl.e: Commentary lays out the chain: EO 13848 DNI report "No later than December 18th," the July claim of "the largest compromise of election data in history," DOJ monitors, and "if Trump can prove widespread fraud in the 2026 midterms, the pretext will be created to declare a national emergency around the 2028 election." Relays a false claim that the FBI and DHS were "seizing vote counting machines in Texas and Arizona" (fact-checked false).
VRF (Restoration of America affiliate) sues Utah Lt. Gov. Deidre Henderson for every voter's name and birth year and to block Utah's ban on posting rolls online, under the NVRA.
tl.a: Voter Reference Foundation v. Henderson (D. Utah)

tl.e: Judge Bulsara bars AUSA Thomas Price from the case over a Nov 4 letter misstating an ICE arrest injunction: "bad faith, a deliberate attempt to mislead the Court"; warns of default judgment for any further misrepresentation.

Between The Lines (radio) reports DOJ claims Sunrise Movement supports "Antifa-associated anarchist terrorists" and that Sunrise is under investigation along with the AFL-CIO, SEIU, DSA and Direct Action Minnesota; Shiney-Ajay says Sunrise was investigated alongside SEIU and CWA in the Minnesota 15 operation. The DOJ document behind the quote is not named.

IRS emails in the administrative record: IRS Criminal Investigation's Guy Ficco relays that a request for tax information was to be elevated to the National Security Council (partly redacted; text read by OCR); Deputy Commissioner Douglas O'Donnell writes that he alerted Dan Katz, whose response is "we will follow the law" and who wants the views of Treasury and IRS counsel.
tl.a: IRS (Guy Ficco, Heather Maloy, Douglas O'Donnell); Treasury

tl.e: Treasury action memo asks Secretary Bessent to sign the DHS-IRS information-sharing MOU "concerning aliens under criminal investigation" the same day: "In litigation challenging future information sharing between the IRS and DHS, there is a filing deadline today for Defendants... This signed memorandum will be a part of that filing." It relies on 26 U.S.C. 6103(i)(2) and, for the predominant category, 8 U.S.C. 1253(a)(1) (people who overstayed a final removal order by 90 days); a second MOU "below the Secretary level" would operationalize it.
tl.a: Treasury (Tyler Badgley, Chris Pilkerton); Secretary Bessent

tl.e: Johnson statement on his Alaska inquiry: "The reported conspiracy to confuse voters in the Alaska Senate election has fractured confidence in our election system. I expect full compliance with my requests for records ... and applaud the FBI and DOJ for their prompt review of this matter." Nov 12 was the deadline for his Oct 29 letters to Jerid Kurtz, Anton McParland and Elisa Rios.

The Intercept (Nov 13) reports federal grand-jury subpoenas in August to the American Federation of Teachers national headquarters and its University of Michigan local (GEO) in the "Michigan 12" protest case, demanding "complete membership rolls," officer payroll, audit reports and board minutes since January 2023. GEO moved to quash; DOJ declined comment.
tl.a: Federal prosecutor Margaret Smith; FBI agent Kara Phipps (E.D. Mich.)

tl.e: Lobbying disclosures (lda.gov; the old lda.senate.gov links now fail because the system moved): Monument Advocacy reported Peraton from Q1 2025 through a Q2 2026 termination at $30,000 a quarter; Mark Bednar first appears in Q3 2025 with covered positions "Press Secretary, Sen. David Perdue, and Communications Director, Rep. Sean Duffy, Head of Communications, office of the Speaker, Speaker Kevin McCarthy"; issues "federal contracting and FAA modernization" (DOT, OMB, DHS, White House Office, Congress) and "federal contracting and cybersecurity" (DHS, Congress). Peraton's in-house filings ($220,000-$240,000 a quarter in 2026) cover the Intelligence Authorization and defense bills ("communications networks," national security space), the THUD bill's "Brand-New Air Traffic Control System," and "unmanned ground vehicles for law enforcement"; Cassidy & Associates lobbies on DOT air traffic control modernization and intelligence bills; Innovative Federal Strategies on the Defense Travel System, "changes to the background investigations process" and DEA IT.
tl.a: Peraton lobbying: Monument Advocacy (Mark Bednar, Julie Dunne, Tatyana Bolton); Cassidy & Associates; Innovative Federal Strategies; Peraton in-house

tl.e: SpaceX engineers working as DOGE special government employees visit the FAA Air Traffic Control System Command Center and Potomac TRACON; WIRED names them. Bloomberg: Malaska told FAA staff to start a program to deploy thousands of Starlink terminals in the national airspace system; FAA tested Starlink through the L3Harris-run FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) contract. Revolving Door Project: Apr 25, 2025 DOGE staff at FAA had employees sign NDAs on 'Project Lift,' a communications-network upgrade.
tl.a: SpaceX engineers Ted Malaska, Thomas Kiernan, Sam Smeal, Brady Glantz (DOGE special government employees); DOT Sec. Sean Duffy

tl.e: Monument Advocacy's Q1 2026 report for Peraton, the FAA's air traffic control integrator, lists "Issues related to federal contracting and FAA modernization" with DOT, the White House Office and OMB contacted; lobbyist Mark Bednar's listed covered position is "Communications Director, Rep. Sean Duffy." The account ran from Q1 2025 to a Q2 2026 termination; Bednar first appears in Q3 2025. (D)

FedScoop (Lindsey Wilkinson): at an FAA industry event, Peraton's Justin Ciaccio: "We're deploying revolutionary agentic AI for the Peraton team and the entire FAA enterprise"; "Schedules are stress tested before they break"; "Risks are brought up before they become crises." Bedford: "We didn't know if we could do it or not — and the vendors that we brought in weren't sure they could do it." An FAA pamphlet: "No software or platform like these exists on the market today."
tl.a: Bryan Bedford; Justin Ciaccio (Peraton); Sean Duffy

tl.e: Peraton Facebook post on the Modern Skies Summit: Schorer "joined Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy and FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford"; Ciaccio, "who oversees Peraton's modernization effort," spoke with FAA CTO Rebecca Guy on building the system "in three years" rather than 10 to 20; progress listed as "Wires: Nearly 2,400 of 5,100 connections already underway replacing copper lines from the 1960s with fiber, satellite, and wireless," 250+ of 1,600 radio sites, surface awareness at 54 sites; "Powering it all: Peraton's agentic AI analyzing 1.5 million records every single day with 5.7 million schedule and resource records already ingested." L3Harris, separately, says it did the conversion "together with its telco partners and the FAA" (R, GovExec).
tl.a: Peraton (Steve Schorer, chairman and CEO; Justin Ciaccio); Sean Duffy; Bryan Bedford; FAA CTO Rebecca Guy

tl.e: FAA awards ASI a 12-year contract worth up to $875M for Flow Management Data and Services (FMDS, replacing the Traffic Flow Management System at the Command Center) and SMART. Flying reports Palantir and Thales also bid. ASI is backed by Andreessen Horowitz (2023 Series B lead) and Spark Capital ($325M Series C, Oct 20, 2026, $3B valuation); ASI also holds U.S. Air Force and Army contracts (Army award, $99M ceiling, Sep 29, 2026).
tl.a: Air Space Intelligence (ASI; CEO Phillip Buckendorf); FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford; DOT Sec. Duffy

tl.e: Letter to Duffy and Bedford asks FAA to pause SMART at DCA/IAD/BWI, citing an 'egregious lack of transparency' on testing, training and accountability, including performance during 'equipment outages'; Oct 13 letter asks GAO to review SMART and FMDS.
tl.a: Rep. April McClain Delaney, Rep. Don Beyer and ~23-25 House Democrats

tl.e: Politico (via AvBrief Oct 15, Flying Oct 16): an internal FAA document shows a term sheet for an equity stake in ASI, the SMART vendor holding a 12-year FAA contract worth up to $875.9M, including a warrant to buy stock; the first time the FAA has sought such a stake. No Hate Hot Takes (Nov 10, citing The Bulwark and FEC data): ASI's PAC gave $2,500 in March 2026 to Michael Alfonso, who is married to Duffy's daughter, about three months before the award; ASI also won an Army contract up to $99M and a sole-source $26M Air Force order; it raised $325M at a $3B valuation in Oct 2026.

USAspending: task order 693JJ127F00007N (awarded through FHWA, funded by the Immediate Office of the Secretary of Transportation), $1,000,000, Oct 30, 2026-Oct 29, 2027: "THIS TASK ORDER IS FOR USDOT'S OPENAI DAYBREAK SOFTWARE AS A SERVICE (SAAS) OFFERING," via Carahsoft on GSA schedule 47QSWA18D008F. It is the only federal Daybreak purchase found. Daybreak is OpenAI's cyber-defense product line behind Patch the Planet. Earlier: GSA's OneGov deal made ChatGPT Enterprise available to agencies at $1 per agency (D, GSA release, Aug 6, 2025); FAA bought "Azure OpenAI" through GDIT (692M1524F00057, Mar 2024).
tl.a: Office of the Secretary of Transportation (Duffy); OpenAI; Carahsoft

tl.e: Raw Story (Culliton, Davis, Nov 13): ASI builds the FAA AI traffic tool SMART (contract up to $875.9 million per USAspending; Duffy announced it in June; Politico reported FAA working to buy an ownership stake). Citing FEC records, ASI contributed $12,500 to Alfonso's campaign in March 2026. Fox News: Alfonso is Duffy's son-in-law. ASI on X: the ground stop is "not based on or a result of the SMART system."
tl.a: Air Space Intelligence (ASI); Rep.-elect Michael Alfonso (R-WI); DOT Sec. Sean Duffy

tl.e: NYT live (Madison Malone Kircher, ~11:37 am ET Nov 14): Duffy says the agency isolated the location where the faulty upgrade work was done and took it offline: "We feel very comfortable that was the root cause"; "It wasn't a foreign actor." He said it raised questions for the contractor, L3Harris: "We're going to hold people accountable."

Fast Company (Alex Pasternack, Nov 16): a second suspect router was at a radar site in Amarillo, Texas; officials "zeroed in on a feature on the new Juniper routers that broadcast data more widely than necessary" and switched it off on all FAA Juniper routers; the two routers are being tested at L3Harris's Florida offices "with help from Juniper and Cisco engineers and the FBI." HPE: "our equipment was working as configured." Bedford (Nov 14): "This is not part of the Peraton-FAA $12.5 billion modernization effort"; in April he had said "Peraton, think of them as an extension of me." An FAA representative "helped an L3Harris technician gain access" to the site; the technicians' union said its members "were not involved in the upgrades." FAA made "a single, undefinitized award to AT&T" for FENS in August using modernization waiver authority. Fast Company notes the Nov 19, 2009 FTI outage was also a newly installed Harris router with a configuration error.
tl.a: Bryan Bedford; Sean Duffy; L3Harris; HPE/Juniper (Adam Bauer); Rep. James Walkinshaw

tl.e: Duffy (CNN State of the Union, NBC Meet the Press): the outage likely began as L3Harris switched copper to fiber at an air-traffic site in El Dorado, Arkansas; "I can't apologize for what was passed off to us"; "Was this a faulty installation by L3Harris ... Was it a fault of the router itself?"; of the $12.5B already appropriated, $4.75B is telecom and about a third is spent. Larsen and Carson asked why more money is needed; FAA and DOT staff brief their staffs Monday. Johnson will add FAA money to an upcoming "legislative package" (R, CNN, NBC).
tl.a: Transportation Sec. Sean Duffy; Reps. Rick Larsen and Andre Carson; Speaker Mike Johnson

tl.e: Reporting conflicts on who holds the router believed to be behind the Nov 13 FAA failure. CNN (Nov 17): FBI agents "took possession of the router" Monday. Duffy (CNBC, Nov 16): it is at an L3Harris lab in Florida with FAA staff and FBI agents on site; the FBI says it is helping examine the hardware, which stays with the network provider (The Defiant). CNN: "there is no evidence that the router involved in the FAA incident was compromised," and it recalls a Mandiant report that Chinese threat actors had backdoor access to Juniper routers. (R)

NYT (Kate Kelly, Nicholas Nehamas, Karoun Demirjian, Nov 18): the El Dorado copper-to-fiber job ran about 10 a.m.-3 p.m. on a Friday "in order to meet the project's ambitious schedule, and because the work was not considered high risk" (person with knowledge of the investigation); one L3Harris technician did it, approved by the FAA and supervised by an FAA technician (Bedford); Duffy: "we do have to charge forward"; 70% of copper lines replaced, about half in the past year; GAO: the copper-to-fiber switch was sped up 21 months and voice-radio modernization about nine years, with risk of "potential disruptions to the national airspace" (GAO's Kevin Walsh). Peraton, hired Dec 2025 to coordinate the contractors, faced FAA staff resistance and "was under a tight timeline"; Peraton did not respond. The SMART AI routing system (Air Space Intelligence, $875M contract in June) was opposed as launched "too hastily" by Warrenton command-center manager Shawn McClosky and his supervisor LaKisha Price, and both were removed from their positions (four people briefed).
tl.a: Sean Duffy; Bryan Bedford; Peraton; Air Space Intelligence (SMART); Shawn McClosky; LaKisha Price

tl.e: Bedford's Aug 28, 2025 memo (not public) waives FAA rules for the overhaul. GAO-26-107992 quotes it: the Administrator is "implementing a blanket waiver of the existing Acquisition Management System, including its contract clauses, policies, and guidance ... as well as financial, legal, technology, security, and program review processes, as necessary, for all activities associated with BNATCS"; the waiver cites the NAS's "critical role in national security and defense" and says "swift and decisive action is essential." GAO: "As such, the Administrator waived the lifecycle cost estimate requirement." DOT's Aug 12, 2026 letter told GAO the Administrator "did not waive BNATCS from the Acquisition Management System" (D). The Air Current and AvBrief (Sept 25, 2025) reported the memo lets the program circumvent other FAA policy or order "without limitation" (R).

GAO-26-107992, full text: FAA has "11,389 individual project schedules that are not integrated," so projects are "scheduled for installations at the same sites, generally without optimizing the schedules to reduce impacts to controller operations." In May 2026 FAA said it planned "an artificial intelligence tool to automatically identify schedule conflicts"; GAO: "this tool is currently undergoing testing, and the business rules for using the tool and the new process have not been established." DOT's written comments: "Peraton has developed an advanced scheduling tool using AI that will coordinate and manage project scheduling across the BNATCS portfolio"; "these capabilities are in the process of being fully optimized." Existing program contracts "were modified to grant Peraton the authority to manage those contractors on FAA's behalf." In Aug 2025 the Administrator "subjected all BNATCS programs to new accelerated acquisition rules" and amended the Acquisition Management System to add an "Accelerated Acquisitions section." Copper-to-fiber moved up about 21 months, to Dec 2028. GAO warned the risks "could lead to more system outages, ground stops, flight delays, and safety incidents." DOT partially concurred and "did not cite actions that it will take."
tl.a: GAO; FAA; Peraton; Bryan Bedford; DOT Assistant Secretary for Administration

tl.e: Memorandum of Agreement between DHS-USCIS and the Wyoming Secretary of State "regarding participation in the SAVE program for voter registration and voter list maintenance purposes"; DHS digital signature dated 2025.07.02. Authorities cited include 8 U.S.C. 1373(c), the Privacy Act, FISMA, the NVRA and HAVA. The data elements include Social Security number.
tl.a: DHS-USCIS (signed by Broderick); Wyoming Secretary of State (Chuck Gray)

tl.e: CPI's 2022 annual report: since Meadows joined CPI "he has helped incubate and launch groundbreaking new projects and organizations, including the Election Integrity Initiative, the Center for Renewing America, America First Legal Foundation, and the State Freedom Caucus Network"; Personnel Policy Operations "was launched in 2022" as CPI helped "launch groups"; partner groups include the American Accountability Foundation, American Moment and the Election Integrity Network.

Judge Smith grants summary judgment to 20 states: DHS's 2025 grant terms requiring FEMA grant recipients (including disaster and emergency-preparedness funding) to "honor requests for cooperation" with immigration authorities are "both arbitrary and capricious and unconstitutional." The government said it had later decided most disaster grants would not carry the condition.

Before the nomination, "the six Republican members of the legislative commission sent a letter to the White House last week recommending three candidates for the position — Ueland, Brian C. DeBusk and Roland Foster" (Roll Call, Nov 16). Washington Sun: "Paul and other Republican members of the commission suggested Brian DeBusk, a health care executive, and Roland Foster, a longtime Republican staffer in the Senate." GovExec: commission members got "24 hours' notice, on a federal holiday"; in 2010 the commission's search took more than a year.
tl.a: Sen. Rand Paul (HSGAC chair) and the Republican members of the comptroller-general commission

tl.e: Senate confirms Ueland as OMB Deputy Director for Management on a party-line 52-45 vote (Roll Call). By statute "The Deputy Director for Management of the Office of Management and Budget shall be the Executive Chairperson of the Council" of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (5 U.S.C. 424).
tl.a: U.S. Senate; Eric Ueland; Council of the Inspectors General on Integrity and Efficiency (CIGIE)

tl.e: OGE release (Aug 26, 2025): "On August 25th, the White House confirmed to OGE that Eric Ueland, Deputy Director for Management at the Office of Management and Budget, has been designated as OGE's Acting Director." His 2026 annual disclosure lists "Acting Director, Office of Government Ethics (7/2025 12/2025)."
tl.a: Office of Government Ethics; White House; Eric Ueland (OMB Deputy Director for Management)

tl.e: Ueland's 2026 annual disclosure (OGE 278e) lists the federal posts he held alongside his OMB job: "Senior Official Performing the Duties of Controller, Office of Federal Financial Management, Office of Management and Budget (9/2025 Present)"; "Deputy Administrator for Programming and Chief Operating Officer and Deputy Administrator Management and Resources, USAID (10/2025 Present)"; "PTDO Administrator, USAID (11/2025 Present)"; "Acting Director, Office of Government Ethics (7/2025 12/2025)." USAID OIG's Feb 6, 2026 audit memo is addressed to "Eric Ueland, USAID/Performing the Duties of Administrator and Chief Operating Officer." By law the Controller must have "demonstrated ability and practical experience in accounting, financial management, and financial systems" (31 U.S.C. 504); Roll Call: Ueland "lacks the financial background of recent past comptrollers."
tl.a: Eric Ueland (OMB Deputy Director for Management); OMB Office of Federal Financial Management; USAID

tl.e: At a FedScoop event in April, Ueland said AI could "provide a significant supplement to our ability to govern" and hinted at AI reviewing executive orders, OMB memos and other policy documents to "ensure that we are driving the federal agenda on management, resources [and] execution consistent with presidential direction and presidential intent" (FedScoop, Nov 16). GovExec: in March he called shrinking the government and its workforce "priority number one"; last week he called the reshaping "long overdue."
tl.a: Eric Ueland (OMB Deputy Director for Management)

tl.e: Shaheen to Ueland and Lewin (June 24, 2026): she restates her hold on the Apr 20, 2026 Congressional Notification of the agency's "intent to fund as much as $19 billion in Congressionally appropriated funds to 'close out' approximately 5,600 foreign assistance awards that were terminated"; State "has still not sent to Congress the final list" of terminated awards; she asks whether total cost with litigation "could exceed $19 billion" and for the status of 31 remaining USAID properties.
tl.a: USAID (Eric Ueland, performing the duties of Administrator and COO); State (Jeremy Lewin); Sen. Jeanne Shaheen

tl.e: USAID OIG management advisory to Ueland, "Performing the Duties of Administrator and Chief Operating Officer": USAID's late-payment interest to vendors "accelerated sharply in CY 2025, exceeding $8.9 million" under the Prompt Payment Act, "a more than sixfold increase" over the preceding 10 years combined (2015-2024 averaged $130,000 a year).

The last two Comptrollers General (Walker, confirmed 1998; Dodaro, 2010) and Steve Hanke write that "the Nov. 19, 2026, confirmation hearing should be canceled, and the normal appointment process should be adhered to"; "the Commission and its members have never met"; Paul and Trump "have not followed the statutory requirements for the appointment of the Comptroller General." The piece does not name the nominee. (D as published)
tl.a: Gene Dodaro; David M. Walker; Steve H. Hanke (Fortune commentary)

tl.e: Nvidia's board announces an independent investigation "in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort"; a committee of independent directors with outside counsel will run it; the board says it has "no reason to believe" national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised and keeps Huang as CEO. Huang the same day admits an extramarital relationship in an email to staff. Reports name the other party as Alice Huang, a former executive of Singapore data-center firm Megaspeed International, whom U.S. intelligence officials are reported to assess was recruited by China's Ministry of State Security (R).
tl.a: Nvidia board of directors; CEO Jensen Huang

tl.e: After the court's Nov 21, 2025 order, Secretary Bessent writes ICE that it must restrict access to the return information IRS disclosed on Aug 7, 2025 to people "personally and directly engaged" in a nontax criminal investigation, and on completion of use return it or make it "undisclosable" (6103(p)(4)); filed as ECF 55-2.
Treasury opens whistleblower tip page (Feb) and proposes 10-30% awards (March).

Treasury opens a FinCEN whistleblower tip page. Secretary Bessent: "We are going to offer whistleblower payments to anyone who wants to tell us the who, what, when, where, and how this fraud and money laundering has occurred"

OFAC sanctioned Russian national Sergey Sergeyevich Zelenyuk and Matrix LLC ("Operation Zero," St. Petersburg), his assistant Marina Vasanovich, his UAE-based Special Technology Services LLC FZ (also sanctioned by State), Azizjon Mamashoyev and his Advance Security Solutions (UAE and Uzbekistan), and suspected Trickbot member Oleg Kucherov. Operation Zero "acquired the stolen tools and sold them to at least one unauthorized buyer"; it pledges to sell only to non-NATO customers and has sought sales to foreign intelligence agencies. Bessent: "If you steal U.S. trade secrets, we will hold you accountable."
tl.a: Treasury (OFAC); Sergey Zelenyuk; Matrix LLC (Operation Zero); Special Technology Services LLC FZ; Advance Security Solutions

tl.e: Treasury release, Apr 23, 2026, "Treasury Announces Form 990 Transparency Initiative to Expose Hidden Funding and Strengthen Oversight": IRS "plans to revise the Form 990" for 501(c)(3)s to add reporting on "government contracts, government grants, and fiscal sponsorship arrangements"; "The changes are intended to detect misconduct and hold wrongdoers accountable." Bessent: "We are ending the days of hiding fraud, abuse, and extremist activity behind complicated nonprofit arrangements. When bad actors misuse charitable structures, directors and officers should understand that transparency can lead to scrutiny, accountability, and liability under the law." Kies: "Tax-exempt status is not immunity from scrutiny." Proposed regulations and comment to follow.
tl.a: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent; Treasury Assistant Secretary / Acting IRS Chief Counsel Ken Kies; IRS

tl.e: New tipster rewards targeting fraud (Washington Examiner).

Treasury release and FinCEN release, Oct 30 (Bessent in St. Cloud, Minnesota, "alongside other senior U.S. officials"): "From 2021 to 2025, U.S. financial institutions reported more than $8 billion in potentially suspicious wire payments sent through U.S.-based money services businesses (MSBs) at the direction of foreign agents." FinCEN issues an "Alert on Risks Associated with Foreign-Agent-Directed Transactions" and a "Notice on the Use of Charities and Non-Profit Organizations for Illicit Activity," framed "As part of the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud." FinCEN's alert (per coverage) says SARs "provide investigative leads and do not establish criminal wrongdoing." Same day: Salim Said (Feeding Our Future) sentenced to 30 years; new Minnesota fraud charges announced.
tl.a: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent; FinCEN; White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud

tl.e: Nvidia's independent directors retain former acting U.S. Attorney (S.D.N.Y.) Joon H. Kim and Wachtell Lipton to run the Huang investigation (CNBC via TNW). TNW notes the board has no independent chair and no compliance chief, and its lead director once ran the company's law firm.
tl.a: Nvidia independent directors; Joon H. Kim (Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz)

tl.e: Databricks and Palantir announce a strategic product partnership combining Palantir AIP/Foundry with the Databricks Data Intelligence Platform "through the combination of Unity Catalog through Delta Sharing and Palantir's multimodal security system"; the release says joint customers had been using the integration for four months; Databricks Federal's chairman is quoted.
tl.a: Databricks; Palantir Technologies (Ted Mabrey, global head of commercial; Rory Patterson, chairman, Databricks Federal)

tl.e: Lenovo press release: Lenovo joins Databricks as a Consulting & Systems Integration Select Tier Partner, offering Databricks implementation through its AI Center of Excellence; Lenovo built its own global data warehouse on Databricks and Azure from 2022. Lenovo's StoryHub ties the same AI stack to its FIFA World Cup 2026 role ("intelligent tournament operations" and an AI command center).
tl.a: Lenovo (Linda Yao, COO, Solutions & Services Group); Databricks (Greg Taylor, VP Partners)

tl.e: AFGE v. OPM (S.D.N.Y. 1:25-cv-01237), ECF 241, Opinion and Order, Oct 20, 2026 (39 pp.): "the defendants' motion for summary judgment is granted as to the plaintiffs' ultra vires claim but otherwise denied; the plaintiffs' cross motion for summary judgment on their APA claims is granted." "By virtue of the Court's summary judgment ruling, OPM's decision to grant DOGE Agents broad access to its systems of recordings containing PII has been held unlawful." Because "all the access permissions have been rescinded, that access need not be vacated or set aside"; the court asks for the parties' "input ... regarding the precise terms of relief" (plaintiffs had sought deletion or expungement of copies). Bloomberg Government: Cote said no DOGE agent has accessed sensitive OPM data since September 2025 and only one remains at OPM.
tl.a: Judge Denise Cote (S.D.N.Y.); Office of Personnel Management; DOGE agents; plaintiffs AFGE, AALJ, EFF and federal employees

tl.e: IRS posts an early-release draft 2026 Form 1040 that, for the first time, asks on page one under "Other Information": "At the time you file your return, are you, and your spouse if filing jointly, a U.S. citizen, U.S. national, or an alien lawfully authorized to work in the U.S.?" (yes/no per spouse, below the digital-asset question). A new Schedule 3-A, "Federal Public Benefit," accompanies it. NYT (Sept 29): the question comes as the administration tries to cut refundable credits for undocumented filers; experts quoted say it is meant to deter filing. Bloomberg Tax: it could help identify who is ineligible for the child tax credit under the 2025 tax law.

CPA Practice Advisor (Jason Bramwell), Oct 6: nearly a dozen Senate Democrats write to Bisignano urging the IRS to drop the citizenship/work-authorization checkbox from the final 2026 Form 1040; the letter says it serves no "tax administration purpose and risks increasing the tax gap by hundreds of billions of dollars" and "The Internal Revenue Service (IRS) does not need this checkbox to collect taxes."
tl.a: Senate Democrats (about a dozen); IRS CEO Frank Bisignano

tl.e: NPR (Luke Garrett), Nov 9: Palantir hires former Sen. Jon Tester as an advisor on "the government services side" ahead of a Democratic Congress in January; Tester: "My agreement with Palantir is advisory in nature, it is not lobbying." He said Palantir does not build "big databases" or trade in private data and called its problem one of "perception." Gizmodo: Palantir earlier hired former Sen. Mark Begich as a lobbyist; Sludge (June 22) reported a Democratic lobbyist hiring spree. NBC Montana: Tester declined to disclose compensation.
tl.a: Jon Tester (former U.S. senator, D-Mont.); Palantir Technologies; Mark Begich (former senator, Palantir lobbyist)

tl.e: HUD release No. 26-091, Nov 10, 2026: "Secretary Turner today announced that the Department finalized its Verification of Eligible Status rule, guaranteeing only American citizens and certain eligible noncitizens will reside in HUD-funded housing." The rule requires "verification of U.S. citizenship or eligible immigration status for all applicants and tenants in covered HUD programs" and reaches "any tenants currently living in 'mixed status' households." A HUD-DHS "audit of all HUD-assisted households identified nearly 200,000 tenants with incomplete or unknown eligibility verification." Release lists the HUD-DHS MOU with "a data sharing agreement to identify illegal aliens," FHA loans for non-permanent residents "falling to nearly zero percent," PHAs told to "validate citizenship status of all their tenants or risk losing funding," and a hotline "to report illegal aliens and criminal activity in HUD-funded housing." Cites EO "Ending Taxpayer Subsidization of Open Borders."
tl.a: HUD Secretary Scott Turner; HUD; DHS

tl.e: M.P. v. Turner (C.D. Cal. 2:26-cv-13392): mixed-status families and two tenant groups sue to stop HUD's Section 214 rule (effective Dec 14), which requires every applicant and recipient to verify citizenship or status through SAVE and ends prorated assistance; the complaint cites HUD's own estimate of about 36,000 eligible children, including citizens, at risk of displacement. (D)
tl.a: Public Counsel; Union de Vecinos; POWER; Scott Turner (HUD)

tl.e: E.D.N.C. forms the Taxpayer Fraud Task Force (TF2) of federal agents and inspectors general to "identify fraud schemes, investigate them aggressively" across "healthcare, benefits, housing, disaster relief, agriculture, small businesses, tax"; Boyle: "We will find you, we will prosecute you, and a federal prison cell waits for you. Cheaters. Never. Win." FBI SAC Reid Davis calls it "a whole of government approach."
tl.a: U.S. Attorney Ellis Boyle (E.D.N.C.); IRS-CI; FBI; HSI; USPIS; DCIS; NCIS; SBA, HUD, HHS, Education, USDA, USPS and VA OIGs

tl.e: NYT: New Jersey's Office of Attorney Ethics files a complaint recommending discipline of Habba Mildon over her role in a 2021 sexual-harassment settlement with a Bedminster club waitress, citing a conflict of interest and "divided loyalties" as a dues-paying member; penalties range up to disbarment after a hearing.
tl.a: Alina Habba Mildon; New Jersey Office of Attorney Ethics

tl.e: The U.S. did not invite OSCE/ODIHR observers for the 2026 midterms, the first time since it began observing U.S. federal elections in 2002 (it observed 2018 and 2024); ODIHR called it "regrettable" and "not in line with" 1990 Copenhagen commitments; HRW (Sept 25) and Sen. Shaheen (Oct 6) condemned it.
Shaheen condemns decision not to invite OSCE observers.

Mandate for Leadership, p. 790, trade chapter: "Order the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and Department of Justice to contract with U.S.-owned and U.S.-operated artificial intelligence companies that are capable of detecting, identifying, and disrupting both the domestic groups' and CCP influencers' social media operations and funding streams using public information as a rapidly available offensive measure." The 2023 Mandate mentions artificial intelligence about 16 times and has no AI chapter. (D)
tl.a: Heritage Foundation, Project 2025 (Peter Navarro, "The Case for Fair Trade")

tl.e: DOJ sues to block HPE's $14 billion purchase of Juniper Networks (N.D. Cal. 5:25-cv-00951-PCP). The same day Mike Davis posts on X: "Amen. The Trump 47 Justice Department's Antitrust Division is already off to a strong start. 3 into 2? You must sue." (D, quoted in the states' brief)
tl.a: DOJ Antitrust Division; Hewlett Packard Enterprise; Juniper Networks; Mike Davis

tl.e: Per the court and the states' brief, Davis, Levi, HPE chief legal officer John Schultz and HPE's Gregg Melinson meet DOJ's Omeed Assefi at the Metropolitan Club in Washington to discuss settling the HPE case; HPE's lawyers of record begin talks with Antitrust Division staff only afterward. (D)
tl.a: Mike Davis; William Levi; John Schultz (HPE); Omeed Assefi (DOJ)

tl.e: In his deposition in the HPE Tunney Act case (taken in early 2026), Alford testified that Slater told him Davis said: "If you don't approve this settlement, I will destroy you. I will destroy your job at the DOJ." The account is secondhand (Slater was not deposed); HPE says nothing corroborates it; Davis told the WSJ it was "utter bull." Davis's Sept 2025 texts to Slater, quoted in the states' brief, include "You're a coward. And a clown." (D, as quoted in ECF 487 and ECF 482; R for Davis's denial)
tl.a: Roger Alford; Mike Davis; Gail Slater

tl.e: Gail Slater leaves as head of the Antitrust Division (Politico: stepped down; CNN: fired). Per the states' brief, Davis afterward wrote: "I've done more than anyone here on the big tech antitrust fight. Gail was a disaster. I recommended her hiring. And her firing." (R; D for the quote, Davis Ex. 26)
tl.a: Gail Slater; Mike Davis; DOJ Antitrust Division

tl.e: Per Judge Pitts's order, HPE adviser Arthur Schwartz and John Schultz meet CIA Deputy Director Michael Ellis and Under Secretary of Defense Elbridge Colby; Schwartz "later also talked to" CIA Director Ratcliffe; Schultz and CEO Antonio Neri speak with NSA's chief information officer and others at HPE with "individuals connected to the National Security Council." The court: these "undisclosed contacts with national security officials should have been disclosed." (D)
tl.a: Arthur Schwartz; John Schultz (HPE); Antonio Neri (HPE); CIA; DoD; NSA; NSC

tl.e: HPE CEO Antonio Neri gives the RNC $100,000 ($55,700 to its legal proceedings account) while the HPE Tunney Act fight is under way. (D)
tl.a: Antonio Neri (HPE CEO); Republican National Committee

tl.e: DOJ fires Antitrust Division deputies Roger Alford and Bill Rinner for "insubordination" (DOJ via CNN); Alford later testified he was told the firings were "punishment for objecting to the settlement." (R; D for the testimony as quoted in court filings)
tl.a: Roger Alford; Bill Rinner; DOJ Antitrust Division

tl.e: Judge Pitts approves the HPE-Juniper settlement (ECF 482) while finding HPE violated the Tunney Act by not disclosing its contacts with national-security officials and DOJ leadership, and DOJ violated it by not disclosing alternatives it considered; he calls the violations harmless because the intervening states exposed them: "the public would never have known that DOJ leadership overrode the opinions of the Antitrust Division staff." Process complaints go to "independent legal or political action." (D)
tl.a: Judge P. Casey Pitts (N.D. Cal.); Hewlett Packard Enterprise; DOJ

tl.e: L3Harris removes CEO Christopher Kubasik after a board investigation found "conduct inconsistent with" its code of conduct; Sam Mehta becomes CEO. L3Harris runs the FAA's legacy FTI network (contract from 2002, performance to Sept 30, 2032). (R; D for the contract)

Veritas Capital CEO Ramzi Musallam, whose firm owns Peraton (the FAA air traffic control integrator), gives the RNC $442,600 in one day: $132,900 each to its convention, headquarters and legal proceedings accounts, plus $44,300. (D)
tl.a: Ramzi Musallam (Veritas Capital); Peraton; Republican National Committee

tl.e: Checkmate Government Relations registers for HPE on "Issues regarding technology and AI systems." Reuters reports its leader, Ches McDowell, "appears in social media posts hunting with Don Jr. and co-owns a property with him." (D; R for the McDowell tie)
tl.a: Hewlett Packard Enterprise; Checkmate Government Relations; Ches McDowell

tl.e: The Ninth Circuit holds Trump's federalization of the National Guard in Los Angeles "exceeded the President's statutory authority and encroached on Congress's" power, applying the Supreme Court's Chicago reasoning (no showing regular forces could not execute the laws; no "rebellion or danger of rebellion"). (R)
tl.a: Ninth Circuit (Judges Eric D. Miller, Jennifer Sung; Mark J. Bennett dissenting)

tl.e: ProPublica (Corey G. Johnson, Brandon Roberts): ARPA-H director Alicia Jackson praised HHS's removal of "black box" warnings on hormone therapy while holding at least $115,000 in Evernow, the menopause-care company she founded; ethics experts call it an "obvious conflict of interest"; her husband's Palantir stock ($5M-$25M) sits beside a $19M ARPA-H contract with Palantir; HHS says she is on administrative leave. (R)

Raia's written testimony: under NSPM-7 "the FBI now oversees the recently created NSPM-7 Joint Mission Center (JMC), which is composed of personnel from 10 agencies," "integrating intelligence, operational support, and financial analysis to proactively identify networks and prosecute domestic terrorists and related criminal actors. In total, JMC efforts to date have resulted in over 200 total arrests and more than 250 indictments or judicial complaints"; a new "NVE Fusion Cell"; "over 1,474 pending nihilistic violent extremism cases"; FBI co-leads 59 Homeland Security Task Forces with "more than 9,000" personnel; "leading up to the recent midterm elections, the FBI has worked closely with our IC and state and local partners to address any credible threats to local, state, and Federal election officials and infrastructure"; "first Super Intelligence (SI)-related theft of trade secrets conviction" (D).
tl.a: FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia; FBI; NSPM-7 Joint Mission Center

tl.e: Raia's written testimony on the Homeland Security Task Forces: they "bring together over 20 Federal agencies and 440 state, local, and international law enforcement partners," "integrating IC and Department of War (DoW) information into a whole-of-government approach" against cartel and gang "Foreign Terrorist Organizations"; the FTO designations mean the FBI "is empowered to use counterterrorism tools to combat cartels and gangs" (over 2,200 investigations of the 22 designated groups). On nihilistic violent extremists: "threat actors driven by hostility toward society and a desire to destabilize it through chaos and destruction"; the new NVE Fusion Cell co-locates counterterrorism and violent-crimes-against-children experts and works "with foreign partners." His only oversight passage is on FISA 702 (double audits, user access "cut ... by 50%"). (D)
tl.a: FBI Deputy Director Christopher Raia; Homeland Security Task Forces; Department of War

tl.e: DSCC v. Trump (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-01114, the mail-ballot order case): Judge Nichols issues a memorandum opinion (ECF 192) and an order "granting in part and denying in part" the DSCC plaintiffs' preliminary-injunction motion (ECF 163) and granting the LULAC and NAACP plaintiffs' motions (ECF 171, 172) (D, docket).
tl.a: Judge Carl J. Nichols; DSCC; DNC; LULAC; NAACP

tl.e: DOJ: a grand jury indicted Russian national Igor D'iu for conspiring to act as an agent of a foreign government, acting as an unregistered agent, interstate stalking and ID-document fraud "in connection with an alleged scheme to conduct surveillance and gather information about employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company" (D). The Financial Times: "Russian accused of spying on Palantir over assistance to Ukraine" (R, headline).
tl.a: Justice Department National Security Division; Igor D'iu

tl.e: DHS and DOJ announce the Threat Disruption Center inside the Homeland Security Task Force's National Coordination Center, working with "more than 30 federal agencies and 440 state and local partners" and using AI tools to "identify distinct components of criminal networks, as well as their victim footprints" (R, Washington Sun, citing the release). TRM Labs, "the super intelligence (SI) investigations company," is "the primary private-sector partner," providing "the technology and coordination infrastructure" for an effort "that gives private-sector partners a direct role" (D, TRM release). Bloomberg reports $95 million to TRM; the no-bid award runs to June 30, 2027; Chainalysis's protest was dismissed in September (R). HSI's Condon: "bringing together the capabilities, technology, and innovation of the private sector with the investigative authorities and expertise of law enforcement on an unprecedented scale" (R).
tl.a: DHS; DOJ; HSI (Acting EAD John A. Condon); Homeland Security Task Force National Coordination Center; TRM Labs

tl.e: The Atlantic (Ariel Sabar), comparing Affinity Partners filings before and after the midterms: Kushner's firm acquired nearly 700,000 shares of defense contractor Arxis, which supplies components for F-35s, destroyers, nuclear submarines and missile defense, while Kushner works on Russia-Ukraine talks and as Middle East envoy. (R, via Just Security Early Edition, Nov 19)

Lawfare, "After the Flood": the Vulnerabilities Equities Process "is no longer a good match for its original public-policy purpose"; they urge putting it "on hiatus," and say "The VEP should not use any exploits AI labs have submitted to the government" under EO 14409.

depthfirst, founded 2024: CEO Qasim Mithani previously at Amazon and Databricks (R, TechCrunch; his company bio says he built developer and security products in AWS's early days and was an early Databricks leader, building its infrastructure and enterprise platform); co-founder Daniele Perito (ex-Square security and risk engineering); CTO Andrea Michi (ex-Google DeepMind). $40M Series A (Jan 14, 2026) led by Accel with SV Angel, Mantis VC and Alt Capital; $80M Series B (Mar 31, 2026) led by Meritech with Forerunner, The House Fund, Accel, Box Group, Liquid 2, Alt Capital and Mantis VC. Alt Capital is Jack Altman's fund; he is Sam Altman's brother (R).
tl.a: depthfirst (Qasim Mithani, CEO; Daniele Perito; Andrea Michi, CTO); Alt Capital (Jack Altman); Accel; Meritech

tl.e: depthfirst's "phpAfterShell" (CVE-2026-126714, CVSS 9.2): a flaw in PHP's default file-based session handling that can lead to remote code execution; "discovered by depthfirst's frontier AI models working with depthfirst researchers," reported privately to PHP in "late October 2026," fixed Nov 19; the Oct 21 PHP2Shell releases "do not contain the fix"; "This is a separate flaw." Affects PHP 8.2-8.5 before the Nov 19 releases. The page names no government notification. Forbes: the PHP Foundation says exploits "require either non-default configuration or uncommon setups"; Mithani says they work on defaults, warns patches can make systems fail and advises disabling the feature and testing patches first; "A couple of years ago, this would have been almost impossible to find."
tl.a: depthfirst (Qasim Mithani, CEO; Leo Lin, founding researcher); PHP project

tl.e: Forbes: Xint, a startup working with DARPA, used OpenAI's GPT 6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Luna to find five NGINX flaws in October (four with no human help), including a remote-code-execution bug dating to 2015 that works on default settings; F5 confirmed all five and patched Nov 18; Wiz says it and others "separately found the same severe flaws"; Pak claims up to 11.8 million vulnerable NGINX versions running.
tl.a: Xint (Theori; Brian Pak, CEO); F5; Wiz

tl.e: Coruna lineage (Google GTIG and iVerify, Mar 3, 2026, per Wikipedia and Straiker): first seen Feb 2025 with "a customer of a commercial surveillance vendor," then used by "UNC6353, a suspected Russian espionage group" against Ukrainian sites, then by "a financially motivated Chinese threat actor" (UNC6691) for crypto theft; "how it moved between these actors is unclear"; iVerify found "structural similarities with frameworks previously attributed to threat actors affiliated with the United States government." DarkSword: used by commercial surveillance vendors and suspected state actors since Nov 2025 against targets in Saudi Arabia, Turkey, Malaysia and Ukraine. Separately, Peter Williams, a former executive of Trenchant, the exploit unit L3Harris built from Azimuth and Linchpin Labs, was sentenced Feb 24, 2026 to 87 months for selling at least eight exploits "intended for restricted use by the U.S. government and allied partners" to Russian broker Operation Zero, which Treasury sanctioned the same day (R, CyberScoop); some media have linked him to Coruna, which no official source confirms. In the Optimizely payload, Report URI logged the Coruna telemetry channel "BIGNIAO" and a loader path "/JIUJIU888/" and tied the cash-out address to operations in March and Nov 3, 2026.
tl.a: Coruna/DarkSword exploit kits; Peter Williams (ex-Trenchant, an L3Harris unit); Operation Zero
