tl.e: Kim Zetter (Zero Day, May 8, 2026): an amended judgment set Williams's restitution at $10 million to Trenchant and L3Harris (plus $1.3 million already ordered), far below the $35 million prosecutors sought; a sealed damages hearing with the companies was canceled. DTEX (Nov 5, 2025): Trenchant's early-2025 leak inquiry, overseen by Williams, centered on Chrome exploits and fired a researcher who said he worked only on iOS exploits and spyware; former employees backed him. Defense counsel argued the tools were "commercial products," not classified government tools.

Williams plea agreement (ECF 6): pleads to two counts of theft of trade secrets (18 U.S.C. 1832) only; "will not be further prosecuted criminally by this Office for the conduct set forth in the attached Statement of Offense"; estimated guidelines 87-135 months (he got 87); sentencing "may be delayed until your client's cooperation has been completed"; stipulated judicial removal after the sentence, for which the government "has sought and received permission from the Secretary of the DHS." No espionage or export-control count.
tl.a: Peter Williams; U.S. Attorney's Office for D.C.

tl.e: DOT's signed letter to GAO (GAO-26-107992, Appendix III), Aug 12, 2026, from Assistant Secretary for Administration Dr. Anne Byrd: the master schedule "will be enhanced by the project Integrator Peraton's expertise and an AI-enabled Integrated Master Schedule (IMS) tool"; "Peraton has developed an advanced IMS tool, using AI, that will coordinate and manage project scheduling across the BNATCS portfolio, enhancing the identification of conflicts"; "These capabilities are still being fully optimized"; "FAA is leveraging Peraton's expertise, tools, and capabilities to apply additional technology-based scheduling methodologies." Scope is set by "Exhibit 6 of the Integrator Accountability Contract and the Corporate Work Plan." The letter lists SMART as a Phase 2 system awaiting "approval and funding," and says "FAA agrees that multiple site visits to the same facility would add unnecessary disruption." DOT promised "a detailed response to the recommendations within 180 days" (by about March 2027).
tl.a: Dr. Anne Byrd (DOT Assistant Secretary for Administration); FAA; Peraton

tl.e: National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is leaving his post, a White House official told CBS News (6:30 pm ET; Axios first); no reason given. CyberScoop: Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies will reportedly move into an acting role (per Axios); Cairncross's former policy chief Thomas Lind "joined OpenAI in October." ONCD was one of the offices OpenAI says it engaged before disclosing the PHP flaws.
tl.a: Sean Cairncross (National Cyber Director); Kirsten Davies (Pentagon CIO); Thomas Lind

tl.e: The White House names Pentagon CIO Kirsten A. Davies to replace National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross; she "will serve in an acting capacity" and the post requires Senate confirmation (NBC, source close to the White House; Axios first). Davies on X: "Our opportunity is to dominate the cyber landscape for generations to come". Background: nominated DoD CIO May 2025, confirmed 53-43 Dec 18, 2025, sworn in Dec 23; earlier CISO at Unilever and Estee Lauder, CSO Barclays Africa, roles at HP, Siemens, Booz Allen Hamilton, Deloitte Australia; co-founder/CEO of the nonprofit Institute for Cyber (R). NBC: the source said she joins a cyber team of Clayton, Kratsios and Rubio.
tl.a: Kirsten A. Davies (Pentagon CIO); Sean Cairncross; White House

tl.e: The Washington Sun, from Davies's OGE financial disclosure: this spring she bought $1,001-$15,000 each in Cloudflare (one of the awardees on a January Pentagon contract worth up to $151 billion across recipients) and Littelfuse (which owns Basler Electric, awarded a $40,320 contract five days before the purchase), and $2,002-$30,000 in Roper Technologies, whose subsidiaries won Pentagon contracts this year; her ethics agreement promised to avoid real or apparent conflicts. POGO's Dylan Hedtler-Gaudette: "It presents a clear conflict of interest." The Pentagon did not answer.
tl.a: Kirsten Davies (Pentagon CIO; named acting National Cyber Director Nov 19); Cloudflare; Littelfuse; Roper Technologies

tl.e: Heritage names Patrick Davis general counsel. Its release: Davis "served as the Senate-confirmed Assistant Attorney General at the U.S. Department of Justice ... managing the department's relationship with Congress, including the planning and enacting of strategies to advance the Trump administration's legislative priorities"; earlier American Petroleum Institute senior counsel, HPSCI chief investigative counsel, Senate Judiciary deputy chief investigative counsel. (D)
tl.a: Patrick Davis; Heritage Foundation; DOJ Office of Legislative Affairs

tl.e: Save America pays James Otis Law Group LLC (Sauer's firm) $2,714,904 in 29 disbursements, Nov 2, 2023 to Sept 14, 2026: $2,287,062 in 17 payments before his Apr 3, 2025 confirmation and $427,843 in 12 payments after (Apr 28, 2025 to Sept 14, 2026; the 2026 ones labeled "legal consulting & expenses"). Save America is the firm's only Trump-committee payer. Sauer's Mar 1, 2025 ethics agreement: he sells "my financial interests in the law firm and in all outstanding client fees" at a price "fixed before I assume the duties of the position of Solicitor General"; "If the purchaser fails to pay the fixed price for the law firm, I will not receive equity in the law firm to satisfy the debt." His 278e: the firm "will be sold to two other attorneys who currently work with the firm." (D)
tl.a: Save America PAC; James Otis Law Group; D. John Sauer (Solicitor General from Apr 4, 2025)

tl.e: L3Harris announces (Melbourne, Fla., July 1, 2026) an FAA contract "to upgrade and continue to operate the nation's aircraft tracking network through 2045" (more than 700 ground stations providing "real-time, satellite-based flight positioning data"); value not stated. Crandall: "By expanding network capacity, we're ensuring the United States remains the global leader in air traffic management." L3Harris has run the FAA Telecommunications Infrastructure (FTI) network since 2002 and claims "99.99971% network reliability." (D)
tl.a: FAA; L3Harris (Kathy Crandall, President, Mission Networks)

tl.e: DOJ sends Bill Essayli, who runs the Central District of California office as first assistant U.S. attorney, to South Florida to work on the criminal investigation of the FBI's August 2022 Mar-a-Lago search; he keeps the Los Angeles post. A source says his work "is focused on the raid" (Washington Examiner; Politico first). The South Florida probe of former officials, dating to at least August 2025, has lost diGenova (resigned Sept 10) and U.S. Attorney Reding Quiñones (resigned Nov 6).
tl.a: Bill Essayli; DOJ; U.S. Attorney's Office, S.D. Fla. (acting U.S. Attorney Yara Klukas)

tl.e: ProPublica: DoD officials approved, at Feinberg's request, an open-ended extension letting him keep using Cerberus for personal accounting, tax and health care services; Cerberus owns or is majority investor in at least four Golden Dome contractors (North Wind, Stratolaunch, Red River Technology, NetCentrics). Warren wrote him in April and July 2026; the Pentagon says he has no "direct responsibility" for Golden Dome buys.
tl.a: DoD (Steve Feinberg); Cerberus Capital Management; Golden Dome

tl.e: ProPublica: the Pentagon signed two consulting agreements worth $349 million with Alvarez & Marsal Federal, tied to the private equity firm where Kollitides, co-chief of staff to Deputy Secretary Feinberg and head of the Economic Defense Unit and BOND, was a partner for almost 10 years; a $67.6M agreement (Dec 2025) and a $281M no-bid agreement for BOND (June 2026), both "other transaction agreements"; an April 2026 SEC filing called him a "Senior Advisor" to the firm. The Pentagon says he "is in full compliance."
tl.a: DoD (George Kollitides; Steve Feinberg); Alvarez & Marsal Federal; Alvarez & Marsal Capital

tl.e: WSJ: Nxum, a firm in which Hines kept a one-third stake, received about $6.3 million under a Tether deal; the first $2.49M payment came May 11, 2025, while Hines led the GENIUS Act push; Tether later hired him as CEO of its U.S. unit. Nxum says Hines had no role.
tl.a: Bo Hines (former White House crypto council director); Nxum; Tether

tl.e: Reuters: Barrack pushed for TI Capital, led by his business partner, to join the planned $15 billion Kirkuk-Baniyas pipeline; a records request found no conflict-of-interest waiver covering TI Capital. State says he has no interest in the pipeline.
tl.a: Tom Barrack (ambassador to Turkey, envoy to Syria and Iraq); TI Capital (Ziad Ghandour)

tl.e: NYT: Kennedy's disclosure shows $4 million in Skyhorse book advances and more than $270,000 in gifts; his wife's company received $210,000 from MAHA Action. Campaign Legal Center asked the HHS IG to investigate (Sept 25).
tl.a: HHS (Robert F. Kennedy Jr.); MAHA Action; Skyhorse Publishing (Tony Lyons)

tl.e: Bloomberg and ABC: Witkoff's disclosure shows nearly $107 million in 2025 income from the holding company that held his family's World Liberty stake; a firm backed by UAE national security adviser Tahnoon bin Zayed bought 49 percent of the venture. The White House says he "fully divested."

WSJ: six days before her July 2025 confirmation hearing, Guilfoyle asked donor Eric Deters to wire $100,000 to her American Express account; Deters says she offered access to senior officials. The White House asked her to resign Oct 13; she denies it.

Federal investigators interview Richard Barron, who ran Fulton County's 2020 election, for more than two hours at his lawyer's Atlanta office; present: two FBI special agents and two federal prosecutors, including Dan Bishop and Hugh Raymond Evans, the agent who signed the affidavit for the Jan 28 Fulton ballot seizure (AJC; NYT first). NYT via What Happened Today: 10 months after the seizure, 260 analysts assigned, no charges filed.
tl.a: FBI; DOJ; Dan Bishop (U.S. Attorney M.D.N.C., special attorney for election integrity); Hugh Raymond Evans (FBI special agent); Richard Barron (former Fulton County elections director)

tl.e: West Virginia's state legislature is hit by a cyberattack that takes down its website and IT systems from Thursday into Friday; deputy chief of staff Ann Ali: "access to certain Legislature IT systems has been temporarily disabled" and the incident "appears to be limited to the Legislature's computer systems"; no group has claimed it.

DoD IG evaluation DODIG-2026-022 (with DODIG-2026-021 on the Secretary's Signal use): of four recommendations to the DoD CIO, the official "Performing the Duties of the DoD CIO" (Katherine Arrington) agreed to three and "disagreed" with adding the risks of non-DoD messaging to annual cyber training; USD(I&S) only partly agreed to a DoD-wide assessment, which the IG calls unresolved.
Trump v. Illinois: Kavanaugh writes officers "must not make interior immigration stops or arrests based on race or ethnicity."
Durbin letter to DHS quotes Kavanaugh concurrence; asks for any "citizen check" guidance.

USPS EO 14399 mail-ballot rule: PI Sept 4; 1st Cir. denied stay Sept 10; second injunction Sept 13; SCOTUS denied stay Sept 14 (26A305), Kavanaugh: applying rule in 2026 "would be arbitrary and capricious."

sb0663: FinCEN finds ~$270M suspicious student-aid activity (~100 SARs since July alert, >20,000 transactions since Feb), referred to law enforcement as "tip-and-lead information"; Education partners with the Task Force; new FAFSA fraud detection tool; release warns fraudsters may use "super intelligence."

Seven federal grand jury subpoenas seeking voter information reach the Nevada Secretary of State's office between Jun 16 and Sept 2, 2026 (three on Sept 1-2); DOJ declined comment; Secretary Aguilar: "If they can take me out in '26, they have control in '28."

D. Mass. denies the government's motion to transfer California v. Trump to D.D.C. (Apr 28, 2026; 2026 WL 1161857): defendants had not shown the first-to-file rule applied or that transfer served the interest of justice.

D. Mass. grants the states summary judgment (Jun 25, 2026; challenged sections of EO 14399 violate separation of powers); the injunction quoted in HSI's Jul 6, 2026 report bars defendants from implementing Sections 2, 3 and 5 as to the plaintiff states (AZ, CA, CO, CT, DE, DC, IL, PA, ME, MD, MA, MI, MN, NV, NJ, NM, NY, NC, OR, RI, VT, VA, WA, WI) for the Nov 3, 2026 election, including any attempt to "create a new federal program to superintend and control Plaintiff States' maintenance of their voter rolls" or to investigate state officials, and requires defendants to "cease and reverse any implementation"; it does not bar citizenship-verification help "at the request of any State and within the framework provided by Congress." Enjoined Sec. 2 is "Establishment and Transmission of State Citizenship Lists and Prioritization of Investigations and Prosecutions Related to Election Fraud." Claims about elections after Nov 3, 2026 were dismissed Jun 18.
tl.a: D. Mass. (Judge Talwani), California v. Trump, No. 1:26-cv-11581

tl.e: USPS publishes its EO 14399 ballot-mail final rule (FR 2026-17238; effective date listed Aug 21): states are to give USPS a list of mail voters through a Federal Ballot Mail Portal "to the extent practicable" at least 30 days before the election (the EO said 60), and ballot mailings to people not on the list "will not be accepted." A D. Mass. 14-day TRO blocks most sections Aug 27; Judge Talwani's preliminary injunction follows Sept 4, and it stays blocked through Sept 17. The TRO bars USPS from implementing most of the rule, including its design standards and the refusal of noncompliant outbound ballots (CRS). The Supreme Court denies a stay Sept 14 (R); mismatched mailings would be "kicked back to the county" (NACo).

Boasberg partially grants discovery in the Democrats' VRA suit and orders DOJ to identify, by noon Oct 30, every state it has sent demands since Jul 1 to remove specific voters, set aside ballots or refuse to issue ballots; plaintiffs may update standing Oct 31; ruling on a TRO barring more letters promised by Nov 2 unless DOJ moots it by saying it will send no more before the election.

Opinion denying the DSCC TRO for lack of standing records that "on October 31, discovery in this case revealed that the federal government has sent formal demand letters only to Washington and California" (citing ECF 29-31). "Even extraordinary merits questions cannot justify the extraordinary relief of a preliminary injunction ... if those seeking it lack standing"; the government sent letters "attempting to browbeat" states.
tl.a: Chief Judge Boasberg (DSCC v. Trump, D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03674, ECF 33-34)

tl.e: DOJ's late-Sunday filing before Judge Boasberg argues the Democrats lack standing because the administration's efforts have failed: its letters have no force on their own, "absent the intervention of a federal court, nothing will change with regard to any election procedures"; "State governments have refused to comply with the DOJ's letters" (more than 30 states refused voter data); "Expedited discovery has now come and gone" (R).

DOJ asks Boasberg to consider contempt against CHIRLA and its lawyers over the UCLA analysis of the 20,000-name DHS list, and suggests he refer the matter to DOJ for a possible criminal contempt investigation; calls the analysis "political grandstanding" with "no relevance" to standing. UCLA: counsel and experts "fully complied with the Court's orders." No ruling (R).
tl.a: DOJ (CHIRLA v. DHS, D.D.C., Chief Judge Boasberg)

tl.e: In CHIRLA v. DHS (D.D.C. 1:26-cv-03072-JEB, ECF 48), Chief Judge Boasberg grants in part a TRO/preliminary injunction: Defendants may not "issue demands to California election officials seeking to compel the segregation of ballots, or other deviations from existing state elections procedures, based on voters' inclusion on the lists of suspected non-citizens." The Executive Branch "has likely violated the Constitution's Elections Clause"; 18 U.S.C. 611(a) "does not regulate the time, place, or manner of elections"; DOJ's aiding-and-abetting theory is "a red herring," and its role under 611(a) "is limited to prosecuting non-citizens who 'knowingly' cast ballots." The court finds CHIRLA's expert "well qualified and credible": at least 22 citizen members are certain matches to the DOJ list, 66 near-certain, and 6,140 CHIRLA citizen entries are "at risk" under probabilistic criteria. DOJ had sent demands and lists to all 58 counties; some counties are reviewing the lists. DOJ told the court its letters are "not self-executing" but recipients ignore them "at their own legal peril." DOJ's motion to strike and for sanctions (ECF 45) is left pending. $1 bond.

Boasberg dismisses or denies relief in DSCC v. Trump for lack of standing: "Even extraordinary merits questions cannot justify the extraordinary relief" sought; notes the "modest relief" granted the same day in CHIRLA v. DHS.

Late Nov 2 a 2-1 Ninth Circuit panel (Bea, Callahan) stays Thompson's TRO in SEIU v. DOJ, calling DOJ's letters and warnings "core Executive functions"; Chief Judge Murguia dissents. Hours later a majority of active judges votes to rehear en banc, vacating the panel order; the en banc court will decide DOJ's stay request. The TRO remains in place.
tl.a: Ninth Circuit (Bea, Callahan; Murguia dissenting; en banc court)

tl.e: Around noon PT on Election Day, the en banc Ninth Circuit voted 6-5 to reinstate the Nov 2 panel order staying Judge Thompson's TRO "pending further order of the court": "A majority of the en banc court has voted to reinstate the three-judge panel's order filed on November 2, 2026." DOJ may again ask officials to set aside ballots of listed voters while citizenship is checked, and warn that tabulating them could bring prosecution, including aiding-and-abetting liability (states need not comply). The stay also lifts the TRO's requirement that DOJ disclose pending search-warrant applications and grand-jury subpoenas. Dissents: Chief Judge Murguia, Judge Desai. Essayli: "The rule of law prevails. Separation of powers does not allow judges to take control of core executive branch powers"; DOJ "will conduct our criminal investigations without fear or favor."
tl.a: Ninth Circuit (en banc), SEIU v. DOJ, No. 26-7303

tl.e: Text of the en banc order now read (upgrades to D): "A majority of the en banc court has voted to reinstate the three-judge panel's order filed on November 2, 2026. Pending further order of the court, the three-judge panel order ... is reinstated." Concurrence (Miller, joined by Bennett): a district court "does not generally have the authority to enter an injunction prohibiting the Department of Justice from expressing its views about criminal statutes." Dissent (Chief Judge Murguia, joined by Gould, Owens, H.A. Thomas, Desai): "The majority permits Defendants to preempt state election procedures by threat of prosecution"; records that letters were delivered "using uniformed DHS officers" and "Federal marshals reportedly served at least one county employee at home." Desai: the stay came "just after the polls open on Election Day." The reinstated panel order stays the TRO term requiring DOJ to disclose pending search-warrant applications and grand-jury subpoenas.
tl.a: Ninth Circuit (en banc), SEIU v. DOJ, No. 26-7303 (DktEntry 32.1)

tl.e: DHS sheet "Preventing Alien Voting": as of Jun 22, 2026, 25 states processed >68M registration records through SAVE (10 full lists), flagging >400,000 deceased and >28,000 noncitizens (GA, OH, TN, TX, NC, ID, AL, MO, LA, KS table); review of "public voter files from states that have not utilized the SAVE system" found "OVER 250,000" noncitizens in CA, PA, NJ, NV; DHS will support DOJ's review of voter files obtained under NVRA/HAVA; blames Judge Sooknanan for suspension of SAVE enhancements pending appeal.

Judge Wetherell (N.D. Fla., Florida v. DHS, 3:24-cv-00509) enforces the SAVE settlement and orders DHS to restore SAVE bulk-upload and SSN search for FL, IN, OH and IA, conflicting with Judge Sooknanan's June 22 D.D.C. vacatur; Ohio announces restored access Jul 8.

DOJ, D.D.C. 26-1352, vacating DOJ's Voter List Maintenance Policy Oct 9; DOJ says it has appealed; Judge Sooknanan denied a stay Nov 2); argues eligible voters are potential "victims" and gives "subject" its "broad ordinary meaning."
